title: Richard Hightower: 'Specialists live every day like it's a one-day contract' | Press Conference
text: How's everyone? >> Good. >> I'm outstanding. Go ahead. >> What's the benefits of having somebody like Cairo who's been here for so many years as the kicker? >> Yeah, I think the benefits are you get a guy that's extremely consistent, uh very accurate, um you know, is always talked about about him being the most accurate kicker in Bears history and he doesn't even blink an eye at that because he knows the the most important kick is his next kick. So, the benefits of having a guy like that is just having a guy that's dialed in all the time, that knows who he is, that knows what he needs to get done, and uh he's also a value and an asset, a leader um for everybody else, not only in the special teams room, but on the team as well. So, I've been blessed to be around a lot of good kickers and he's definitely one of them. >> In what ways is Cairo the genre of Adam Vinatieri in the army guy? >> Just the way he goes about his business, detail-oriented, um serious, loves loves what he does, um and cares deeply for others. So, he's been a a pleasure to have here. >> What What's your message to your guys with with cutdown day looming in terms of what what they're out there to show and kind of what the next step is either whether you make the team or you're looking elsewhere. >> Yeah, my message to them is the same message as it is day one. Work as hard as you can. Um you're always being evaluated. Everything you do is being evaluated. So, go out and put your best foot forward, whether it's here or somewhere else, we're fighting to keep the shield on our back. And as long as they have that shield and they're in the National Football League and they got something they can work towards. So, just continuing to always inspire, motivate, and then also teach them is is kind of my message to them. >> What's the challenge of having to cut guys less than 24 hours after a game? >> Yeah, it's a huge challenge, man. It's the worst day in National Football League. I don't think anybody uh would shy away from that and especially in an organization like ours where we truly care immensely about people, you know, and we get attached to these guys and at the end of the day it's still a business and we can only have, you know, 50 53 guys on the roster your best 69 guys overall because they'll help you at some point, but it's a tough day. I mean it's a challenge. It gets me every every time, but also it it's a good day cuz some guys are extremely proud of you know, what they've accomplished, but they know that it can still end at any time. So you got to always be pressing forward. It's a great question though. >> Can Can you remember the the hardest cut you ever had to make? >> [clears throat and cough] >> Um they all suck Mark. Honestly, they all suck. They all do. Um I can't really remember I can't really remember the hardest one, but you know, some of them were uh guys are like come in and they're like I know I can do it coach. I know Excuse [clears throat] me. I know that it's not going to be well. >> [laughter] >> Don't want him in here. He's not on our team. All right. So Some guy yeah, cut him right now, right? So >> Some guys come in and be like yeah coach I still believe you know, I know this is not the end for me and then some guys come in and they're bawling in tears. And you just got to you know what I mean? You just got to be there for him just like you would anytime. So um you know, it's uh it's definitely not it's it's definitely never something that anybody that has their heart in the right place in this profession is definitely something that you don't get used to. >> Ben said that for the joint practice last week he wanted to see Bo put in some tough situations. Did you get the type of work you would hope for and what were what did you come away with as far as your evaluation on him? >> Yeah, we really did come away with what we wanted to come away with. We got put in some tough situations and we're asking the tight ends to do the same thing. I mean, we want them challenged at all times because that's what's going to happen to him in the game. And he showed some things, but he also showed um that we need to continue to work on some things. And that's going to be the case for every player, not just Boat. You know, so um he uh he he he held his own. So, we were we were happy about that. And then there were some things that that I feel like he'll tell you that, "Hey, I wasn't good enough on that." So, it's a work in progress. >> You get a rookie ready for a rookie long snapper ready for a real game in week one. What's as far as his learning curve, what what do you warn him about? What do you tell him to focus on extra? Like, what does a rookie curve look like for someone like that who's never done this in an NFL game? >> Yeah, right now, I mean, we're not there yet. I'm getting him ready for this game. Um and telling him every day you got to prove that you belong in the National Football League every day. So, right now we're working on the Tennessee game. And then when we get the next week, then I'll get to that, honestly. I haven't I haven't even addressed that with him other than you need to be prepared to compete every single day. And you're not only competing if there's a guy in the room here, but you're competing against everybody else outside the National Football League. I mean, outside our building in the National Football League. >> What is What are some specific areas of focus for him down the stretch here? >> Just same as accuracy, protection, um being a great teammate, but accuracy, protection, um and making sure um that he snaps a good clean deliverable football. >> Is it really hard Is it hard for a young long snapper to break in the league? It seems like the veterans in the league can do it for a long time. And there's might not be the turnover there that there is at >> Yeah, it's extremely tough. Not only for a long snapper, but for any specialist, right? Any specialist to break in the league cuz there's only like one of those guys. Even when you look at quarterbacks or you look at any other position where there's one player playing at a time, there's usually other people on the roster. Um in this case, what we're talking about, we're talking about one person and one person only. So, I tell them all the time, "Hey, man, if you're in the National Football League and there's 32 teams, you're one of 32." It's more than billions and it's billions of people in the world. So, if you're one of 32, it's pretty special. So, you got to cherish it every day you're in there, and uh you got to live like every day is your last contract. Every day you specialists, we live every day like it's our last day. Like you guys were here with Mercedes. Mercedes had a great quote. He said he lived every day of his life like it was a one-day contract. And that's how we approach it. >> The um the number of fake punts and fake field goals have gone down precipitously over the last decade. I think it was just like nine total last year. >> Mhm. >> Obviously, teams are lining up and going for it more, but can you offer any other reasons why that's dropped? And do you miss that being a bigger part of the game? >> Yeah, fourth-down aggression has been, you know, as you know, a lot of people, you know, statistics weighs into that, analytics weighs into that. Um but we got a bag of them, you know, so and Bigs ain't scared, so you know, I don't I don't I can't speak for any other team, but we got a we got a bag of them, so um we we we like fakes. >> Do you miss Do you miss that being a bigger part of the game, though? Like it used to be that was something that was kind of a a cool play that >> I mean, I'm sure sure, you know, but there there were some good ones last year. There were some good ones. >> Bigs wants to know when you're going to open the bag up. >> Yeah, I mean, >> [clears throat] >> Bigs knows it's the coach head coach's call. >> I got a bag bigger than Bigs ever got a bag full of fakes, okay? >> Hey, Richard, there was some talk yesterday about Jaylen bringing the team together and just sort of veteran leadership as a whole and being a players-led locker room. And in your corner, how like how important is that in your room that it's not just you doing it, but somebody really kind of grabs the special teams room? >> I think it's extremely important. I think that's something that we want to foster. You know, we want to foster competition. We want to foster, you know, the leadership and those leaders stepping up, taking taking the bull by the horns. A A Daniel Hardy is one of those guys. Like he He is man at the maturation process in this kid from when he first got here to now to where he'll speak up in the meeting and we'll give him the floor and what he sees and how he could help a young kid and he'll talk through things. Uh D Jack is that way. DeMarco Jackson's that way. Um Elijah Hicks is that way, you know, so we've been fortunate um to have some guys that that what we call they have little crap in their neck and they're not afraid to to speak up and and tell tell somebody when it's right and tell somebody when it's wrong. So, we always want to foster that. Like always want that. I I love that. >> Is that kind of a maybe a legacy of Travis Homer? Cuz I don't know those guys would talk well about him. I don't know if how much of a >> Yeah, I mean that's a That's That's obviously he was a a tremendous leader. Yeah, tremendous leader. >> Given all the time that Elliott has missed, how do you acclimate yourself with what you're working with quickly here as the regular season approaches? >> Yeah, just we got some time with him in the offseason, you know, uh but the one thing about that kid is he's dialed in. Like he's although he hasn't been on the field, he hasn't missed a beat in the meeting room and he comes up for extra meeting time. Like he's like a I mean he's like a a machine. Like he's in there at coach, I'm in there. I'm in there at 6:00 every every other morning. I'm in there at 6:00. You going to be there? I'm going to be there. I'll be there. [snorts] And he's there with questions and notes and everything. So, I mean he's taken full advantage of his time off to try to get better although even though he couldn't do it physically. So, we'll see what it looks like whenever they fully um clear him. >> What stands out about what Kaden Davis has brought to the special teams group? >> Man, outstanding talent, man. Kaden was a a good a great acquisition that that the front office made. He works his tail off. Uh really um a joy to be around. He's like a sponge, you know? There's a kid that's fought, you know, on multiple, you know, obviously released or cut from multiple teams, but has fought, you know, time in and time out. I got a ultimate respect for Kaden Davis. It's kind of like Kalif Raymond's story. Kalif had been cut so many different times. And then special teams you deal with a lot of guys that have that have had that happen to them. But do they have the perseverance to, you know, to push through? And I and I think Kaden does. And I and I'm uh I'm happy and excited to see what he'll bring to the table this week. He'll get more opportunities. >> Savannah, over here. >> Savannah Kmet is someone who might be on the roster bubble. Uh has I think played less than 100 career snaps on special teams. How has he carved out a role this camp? >> Yeah, he had he hadn't played a ton in his career, but what is my job? My job and our job, Coach Blevins and I, is to develop him to be able to do that. So, if you noticed, he's been on a lot of stuff, you know? And he's made some headway there. And he's done a good job improving. Like we take a lot of pride in helping guys that haven't done it or for another person or another coach or somebody in their life to tell them that they can do it, well then the place is here for you in Chicago. Cuz we going to teach you how to do it. And we going to help you learn how to do it. And we'll correct it when it's wrong. We'll show you when it's right. And we going to we going to help you extend your career. That's what we take pride in. He's back. All right. He got cut. He's back. >> Thanks, guys. >> Bad bug in here. Thanks a lot.

title: Michael Penix Jr. and other Atlanta Falcons players speak to media post-practice | Press Conference
text: Mike, how's it feel to be back out there 11 on 111? >> It feel good. It feel good. Excited to be back out there um doing all that team stuff and um it feel good. >> What was kind of your expectations for this week and and getting more of those 11 reps? Obviously Kevin's talked admium about how much work you've been doing outside of the 11 period, but kind of what was this week like for you and what were you wanting to show? >> Yeah, it was great. Just uh I just wanted to get get back in the rhythm of things. you know, obviously whenever you put a D lineman out there, things start moving a little bit faster. So, um just getting back to slowing the game down in in that aspect of it. So, and I I do feel like, you know, each day uh since since my first day out there, I've been getting better and uh getting more com comfortable and confident with that. So, >> what's the hardest part about from where you've been all off seasonason to being in whole team drill? Like, what's the hardest aspect of that curve >> into 11? It's just more reps. It ain't hard though, but that's just what that's what come with it. So, but it's not hard. It's It's exciting for me cuz like now I don't I get more than eight reps a day. So, I'm like great, let's go. >> Kind of took like a a minor hit. It appeared on Monday where like Chris got pushed back. >> Mhm. >> How much does that help at all? A little bit to kind of get brushed. I know it was a huge hit, but >> Yeah. Um it's great. I mean, obviously we uh we we don't want that obviously out there, you know, they they preach not to let quarterbacks get hit, but it's football, you know, that those things happen. you know, accidents happen, but it's good. I felt good. I feel confident. I completed a pass, thank God. So, feel good. >> Physically, based on the timeline that you're on, do you feel like you could start week one, you'd be ready to go in terms of reps and the way you feel? >> Yeah, I I feel great. Like right now, um I I got cleared to do 11 on 111 for practice, you know, obviously. Um, you know, but each and every day I'm getting better, getting more confident. You know, I I I'm not playing this week because, you know, obviously I only had three practices under my belt under uh doing 11 on 111 stuff, but uh I've been feeling really good. And, you know, as long as I keep the track that I'm on, I I definitely feel like I I will be where I need to be mentally and physically, you know, to to feel confident enough to go out there in week one. And, you know, as far as, you know, being healthy and all that, I feel good. So, >> Monday, we saw you scramble out, roll out to the right side. We know that's not your game. It's not you something we do a lot. But how did it feel get out and do that? >> Yeah. Uh um it felt it felt good. It felt good to get out of the pocket. Um probably got about six yards, but it's positive, man. But um it feels good, you know. I I that running aspect of it. That's that's the easy that was the easiest part coming back from, you know, as far as straight line stuff, you know, but um it felt good to be able to just be out there and, you know, reacting to the pressure and, you know, getting out of the pocket, you know, whenever I needed to. Did you want to play? Did you have that conversation? Did you want to play Friday? >> This Friday or soon? >> No, it's soon. I only had three practices. Lebanon. I don't want to go out there and do that, you know. But um I feel good though, you know. But that's at the same time, you know, like like I said, I only had three practices. >> What's the part in your game because there was so much a lot of mental reps for you, you know, picking up the new offense. What's the part of that that maybe you've seen the most growth in before you were cleared to do to do everything? >> Say that again. My bad. >> You were taking so many mental reps and there was a lot of stuff, you know, that you couldn't go full tilt for so long up until this week. You know, what part of your game did you see so much growth in before, you know, you were able to get out there, you know, with no restrictions? >> Uh, just being quick in my reads, you know, and just understand um each play call and why it's called and what we're trying to get out of it. So, I I definitely feel like, you know, all those mental reps helped with that so that I can go out there and play fast, you know, play smart cuz, you know, I feel like for everybody, not everybody will say it at the quarterback position, but anytime it's your first time out there at 11 on 11 on 11 is moving fast. You know what I'm saying? So, u to be able to slow that down and, you know, uh just continue to get those reps and get more comfortable in my shoes, it feels good. >> You mentioned having just three practices. Uh, how many practices do you think you would need to feel comfortable that we back to being old Michael Penn Jr.? >> It ain't no number on that. I just know three practices. It's like, d, I just got clear. It's like, hey, all right, let let me get my feet wet a little bit. But, um, it's no number on that, you know. It's no number on how many practices I feel, you know. Obviously, I feel like I got to trust trust my body, you know, um, see how how my body feels, you know, and, you know, mentally and stuff like that as well. So, I say that's it's more of that than a number of reps and stuff like that. >> You've been through this obviously twice before. Are you you feel similar now compared to the previous times like where you were like timewise? >> No, it's different. Um I had a different different procedure uh that that extended my recovery period. Uh so it's a little bit different. >> Yeah. different procedure in order to you hope make it more stable in the >> That's exactly what it was to make it more stable. Yeah. >> We were talking to Tommy uh earlier this week and it was after your first day back and he said that there was so much joy out on the field amongst you and he said even like teammates wise there was a lot of he felt a lot of joy amongst the offense seeing you back out there. Did you feel that as well that first day when you stepped on the field? >> Yeah, for sure. I mean, I feel like everybody knows what I've been through throughout my career, all the injuries, the up uh as far as like all the injuries, ups and downs and stuff like that. So, I feel like a lot of people is was excited to be able to see me back out there and, you know, obviously doing what I love, you know, because I at the same time, you know, for everybody like you you don't want to see anybody go through, you know, injuries and stuff like that, but we all know it's a part of the game. But whenever you see a brother, you know, get through that, you know, and come back healthy and, you know, come back out there and competing with with you is is definitely awesome to see. So, >> how's your mind doing? >> I'm great. All right. you gotten I'd imagine the more reps you've had, you trust your knee a little bit more now. >> Yeah, that that's that's all it is, you know, just reps, you know, and um that that builds confidence, you know, so yeah, absolutely. >> Anything else? >> Saw someone drop a basketball to you in high school. >> They did. >> It's probably the same one that circled around when I was getting drafted. >> Like you said, when's the last time you took a shot? >> I couldn't even tell you. It's been a while. I ain't I ain't seen no hoop in so long. [clears throat] I wasn't a shooter, though. I was just a dunker. >> Yeah, [laughter] I understand. >> I still got it, though. >> All right. >> I didn't say you didn't. >> No, I'm just playing. I know it. >> All right. Uh, but John, first things first, Michael Panick's getting out there for 11 on 11s. What did it mean to you to see him out there and and kind of what was the overall vibes like on that first day? >> Yeah, I mean, it was it was great. Um, it was just cool to see him like before practice. he was just like in his routine uh prepping to get ready to to get back to 11 on 111s. Um but I think it's really cool just to see all the teammates around him, especially on the offense, like really bring them in and understand what he brings. But um that's that's my dude, man. And and I'm happy that he's back cuz I know that injury uh really sucked for him and his family. So it's just cool to see uh one of our brothers back out there just just playing free. >> How did it look to you this week? >> It looked good. It looked I mean, it was definitely a ramp up for him. So, I mean, it's you just take it one day at a time and I think he, you know, felt comfortable. I think he looked fast like he he told me this morning that he would that he would get me in a race and I'm like, "Mike, I'm Mike, chill out, bro. Chill out, bro." Uh, but it's just cool to see his confidence up and and him going out there to to go have fun, man. >> With Kellian's run game, are are there things they're asking of you that are new to you that are changed for you? What do you like about it? What what makes it click in your opinion? >> I mean, for me, like so I I ran this this run scheme in and off, I'm sorry, in college uh with SARKC. So, a lot of lot of I don't want to explain too much, but a lot of different things to come at you. You you really don't know what we're going to do. Um so, I really appreciate that. Um meaning like we have a lot of different var variations, but for me, man, like it's it's it's to create space for yourself. um and you know that he does a really good job and being intentional and trying to get us to the second level as fast as possible because he you know when we get to the second level I feel like that's what we're super dangerous um as runners. So I I've been appreciating what uh Coach Callahan does for this for this run game. >> When he explains concepts to you, how how far back has he gone tapewise? >> Oh, we gone we gone far. We we going back to I think Adrian Peterson when he was with the commander. Um well I mean commanders now. Um but yeah we we we've gone far back. Uh I've seen DeMarco Murray. I've seen a lot of different guys man. Like so I think it's uh it's cool to see how far he's you know obviously how long he's been coaching but just all the backs that he has coached and all the schemes that he's coached has been it's been fun to watch. >> Is there more on you physically in this game? I just noticed yesterday a lot like it seemed like you were just like really banging in there. like between the tackles it was like a different look to kind of the way it's been before. >> Um not really not really more uh they just want to create opportunities. Uh and for me like I appreciate it and you know I think probably what you saw was a lot of different other run schemes that we've run that you probably haven't seen here in a long time. So you know like I told him like it's it's back to college for me. And you know, the thing I enjoy is we'll throw one at you and then the next play or the next time we run the ball, like it'll be a completely different scheme and just create that var um variety of plays is has been fun, but yeah, there's there's a lot to go into it. >> The other day the social media team did one of those questions was about name the most famous person in your phone. I feel like that wasn't fair. Did they >> not famous? I'm not famous. Yeah, but you're [laughter] >> u Well, I appreciate it. I appreciate it. Um I mean I I I didn't see the the question board cuz I I want to say >> you compete because it wouldn't have been fair. >> Shoot. I you know, but I appreciate them saying me, you know, they see me every day, so it's cool. >> Other than MC, what's your kind of your top five famous folks in your >> Man, I got some I got some I got some cool people. [laughter] I met I met some I met some cool people. I'll keep it. I I'll keep it in. I'll keep it in. I'll keep it in on that one. [laughter] [snorts] >> Uh we talked about the run game, but it seems like the screen game too is going to be an important to this. Is is there also different wrinkles you think for for you especially in it with Tommy Reese's offense? >> Yeah. Um lot lot of a couple new screens. Um, you know, we've been doing, uh, uh, the same kind of screen the past year, uh, which which has been effective, but, uh, I love us having to add more screens, um, and screens that, you know, can go across the play. Like, there's just so many things that we can do with with that scheme. So, you know, thing I like about Tommy, man, is, you know, he what if he sees something work, you know, he's he's going to add it. Um, and if he sees another team do it really well, shoot, we'll we'll add that, too. uh because we just have the players that can, you know, execute the plays and and make it all work. >> The evolution of the run game here and just the versatility that's being added in. How much do you think that that can show off what you talk about all the time, what you believe this offense is capable of? >> I mean, I think when it when it works how it's supposed to, I mean, this offense will be will be dangerous. Um because one it opens up the pass game in a very high level and then you know even if you put eight guys in the box or if you want to stack the box like we still have so many more variety of runs that that can work against it. So you know I I I really appreciate that and you know even when we're studying and looking at different defenses with me me and coach Petri like he'll tell me you know this is how this run will work. This is how this run will work against this defense or against this look. So, we have a run scheme for every single look and and it's it's cool to watch. >> You and coach Petri have a great relationship. We know. >> Yeah. >> He's so hands-on in between plays, whether it's you or the other B- Rob. >> Um, talk about the dialogue that's happening and just that connection and how much that benefits you guys in that room. >> I mean, it's it's everything. Um, the the thing with Coach Petri is, you know, there's always something that we can get better at every single play. you know, it the play could look perfect, but maybe our footwork is a little little off. So, he's he's very big, you know, with the little details. And it doesn't matter who you are. Uh it doesn't matter what you achieve. Like, he he doesn't care about none of that. Pass game, run game, blocking, every single every single aspect, but then on top of that, like he's going to coach you super hard and you know he's going to love you up and joke around with you, but when it's time to work, like we going to work. Has everyone >> Well, Cash gave his away, so [laughter] that's that's that's insane. I don't know. He was like, I just gave it away. I didn't know what to do with it. I was like, bro, they gave it to you. Um and then I think TG's doing pretty good. I think I think he's actually taking care of it. I gotta ask B Rob. Uh Nate, I feel like he's taking care of it, but I don't know. But I I I'll show you mine. I'll show you mine. >> Dolly Parton. >> Yeah. I mean, I went to Nashville and I saw like her u her house uh when I went to Nashville a couple years back. And it was it was super cool to see that. I don't know if it was her house, but I think it was like a museum type. I don't know. But uh yeah, it's pretty sad that that she uh she passed away. Um so yeah, rest in peace to her and her and her family. >> You're video game player, right? >> What's kind of your favorite game? >> I've been playing uh college football 27 and then I've been playing FC uh 26. So I'm just waiting for 27. That's the soccer game, but I'm on it all the time. Me and uh my best friend Jonathan. Um you know, I know he's been doing acting stuff, but we've been on every single day like getting after it. So cool. >> Play play remotely or he lives here? >> No, he lives in LA. Uh but we play like online. >> Who do you play with in college football? >> Oh, Texas. Texas every single time. Um Yeah, that's that's I don't play nobody else. >> Speaking of to a degree, speaking of that to a degree, Kendall Daniels talks a lot in practice. >> And we've gotten his side of it and his teammate side of it, but he talks to you. >> Absolutely. I I love it. I mean, I told him before um this, you know, we started training camp, I was like, "What's the one thing that you need from me that's going to make you better?" And he was like, "Just talk. Just get in my ear." And I'll be in his ear. And knowing me, like, I don't talk at all. Like, that's not that's not my game. But when it comes to him, I always have something to say. And it's easy because he went to Oklahoma State first and then he went to Oklahoma. Like, what are we doing? Um, [laughter] so it just it's just good to like tick him off. Uh, but he huge talker. uh like he gets under some guys skin, but I I enjoy it. I love it, man. Like I just have fun with it. And I said, "If you gonna talk," he I told him this week, I was like, "You ain't talked this much this week." I was like, "I ain't hear you at all. I even see you in my in my vision." And he was like, "I'll get back to it." So it's cool. It's cool to see it. >> So you know what buttons to push? >> Absolutely. Absolutely. He It's But he's he's going to be a great player. Like obviously everybody sees it, but you know, I enjoy how he works every single day. >> How much does it help you to play this week? >> Say it again. How much does it help you to play this week in Miami? >> Um, I don't know. They they'll let me know uh soon. Um, but yeah, just go from there. >> Well, Kevin said, is that you plan to play a lot of the ones? I mean, is it how helpful can it be if you are out there? >> I mean, it'll be great. Um, but I know like they have a they have plans, they have things that they want to do. Uh, so I guess we'll just we'll see you on Friday. >> Your friend Jonathan, is he is he a famous actor? you mention. >> Yeah, he he's one of the one of So, what is his last name? >> Davis. John the Davis. >> Banks. >> Out of Yeah. Outer Banks. >> Okay. Excuse me. >> Shout out. >> Yeah. Yeah. He's Yep. Yep. [clears throat] Yeah. It's my It's my brother right there. [laughter] >> He's about to play uh He's about to play Snoop Dogg in the in his biopic. So, it'll be It'll be cool. Yeah, it'll be cool. >> Yep. >> Do you have a part in that? >> I do not. [laughter] I'll be I'll be I'll be in the season. We'll be in the season. Uh they're they're just about to start shooting. Yeah. Yeah. This would be cool. >> And you said a few weeks back, you know, after you got your deal, you know, about the legacy you wanted to leave for other running backs, you know, Jir gets his few days later. What's it been like now? You know, a few weeks have passed, you know, kind of the response and kind of letting that legacy that you wanted to leave, you know, kind of set in. >> Yeah. I mean, you know, ju just cuz I got the contract, like that's that's just a goal from, you know, God to bless me with that. But for me, like, you know, I feel we're still just getting started. Um, just in my game and how I've been progressing and just my career, like I feel this this season right here, um, I'm always trying to be better than the last season. Like that's that's been my goals, like always be better than last season. So, you know, just how I've been working and how we've been working in practice. like I think we're going to show uh that because we work super hard here and coach Defensky like sets a standard and I take it to heart and it is I I think I like that it doesn't matter who you are like everybody's going to get coached up the same way. So that's what I like about this team and it just it just shows how he cares about everybody. So yeah. >> How's everything been the last few days? Quite a whirlwind. >> Uh it's been great man. Uh happy to be here in Atlanta. um trying to get back into football shape. Um obviously coach know that. So they basically giving me one day on and one day recovery and one day on this week so and next week we'll build off of that. >> What went into that decision to unretire? >> Uh so I wasn't supposed to retire. Um said I wasn't going to tell the story, but I'm going to tell it. Um yeah, man. Uh got a phone call um from my mom's doctor um telling me that she don't have much longer to be on this earth. Um so I let the team know. Obviously they wasn't trying to let me leave, but uh that was the only thing I had left to retire. So I retired. Um dealt with that after losing my mom. I lost my grandma. Then after my grandma, I just lost my dad. So y'all obviously know what I've been through. Um so to get a phone call from Cleveland, um shout out to AB for just calling me and seeing where I was at mentally. Um he was just asking me that I want to play football again, you know. Um did I still love the game, you know? Um and I was like, "Yeah, I love it, man. I need to come back because I'm at my lowest right now." So, um, he told me to come in and do a workout and we'll go from there. Uh, got to Cleveland, went through the workout, everything went well. Um, but we couldn't get the numbers right. So, I told him, man, just call me back when you figure it out. And I guess after working out, uh, Coach Stfansky saw me in the end and they was like, all right, yeah, we need another end because I guess our guys went down. So, they need a veteran in the room. So when he called me, I was like, man, this is perfect because it's close to home for me. So I'm originally from Alabama, if you guys know. Um, so this is like home. So I'm just happy to be back and happy to get back started. >> Thank you for for sharing that with us. And and I mean, I guess just like >> coming back from all of that, obviously a very emotional time for you. Does it feel good to be back out here, you know, doing what you know, what you love for a very long time? >> Yeah, man. because I can see this as my uh happy place. >> Give me a second. >> Yeah, all the time. But yeah, this is my happy place, man. um come back, play football. Um I was in a dark place, but you know, um coming out, running out on the field, you know, the fans, not only just the fans, man, the joy that I get from winning and just getting sacks, you know. Um I started late in Uh my senior year in high school, man, I didn't know how to play football. My coach always told me just to go get the quarterback. So, ever since you told me that, man, I've been good at it. Um, when I retired, I think I had 70 sacks, man. So, now I'm trying to reach a 100. So, any way I can get to it'll be good. But, man, I'm happy to be back, man. And like I said, this my happy place and [snorts] ready to get going. >> Who did you lean on this spring? >> This spring, one of my good friends. Um, obviously when I retired, you know, a lot of people fell off. Um, when I retired, you know, I wasn't a bigname guy anymore. So, lost a lot of friends, man. But I had one friend that was there with me, um, Wallace Gilberry. He was a guy >> that played 10 years in the league. And when I was in Kentucky, he was in Cincinnati. So, that's how we connected. And he's from Mobile, Alabama. Um, so me being from Alabama, that's not that far. Montgomery and Mobile is not that far from each other. So, u man, he took me up under his wing, man, and was there with me the whole time, man. So, big shout out to him for sure. >> When you say you want to reach 100 sacks. >> Yeah. How do you feel? Like, do you believe you can play for a while longer? >> Oh, yeah. For sure, man. Like I said, I started late if you understand what I'm saying. So, I didn't play from pee-wee on up high school. I played my senior year in high school. So, I'm still young in the game, man. body still feel good. But you know how people see in comments and say that I retired that I'm getting old, but that wasn't a reason and I just told y'all what happened. So man, yeah, I got a lot left in the tank for sure. >> So like how much were you like training from I guess October onward. >> So when I retired, I was like, man, should I stay retired? So I know my trainer was always calling me um basically when I was in a dark place, he was calling me, man, let's get a workout in or something, Z. So, I started working out twice a week and then I started posting my videos and when I started posting my videos, that's when a lot of interest came from like Cleveland and and then Atlanta call. So, that's how I ended up here today in this chair. >> Darius, uh, you could have gone anywhere and played, you know, potentially. How important was it, you know, to be in a place with people that you know that you're comfortable with, >> you know, as you come back from, you know, not just getting back in football, but from, you know, a lot of personal stuff that happened in your life. Uh just trying to figure out the right situation. Um obviously when I was going to Cleveland, they was telling me that they wanted me to be the third guy um in the pass rush room, you know, in the DM room. But when I got the call here, they was like, "Man, we need you like to come in and play for us." So I was like, "All right, that's a better situation." And then I'm familiar with the head coach, man, cuz you know, he was with me in Cleveland. So I felt more comfortable coming here. And like I said, man, my mom, man, rest her soul, man. She always wanted me to be in Atlanta with the Falcons. Like I said, I'm from Alabama, so she always wanted the fam to come up and support me for the games because that's a closer ride. I think two and a half, three hours. >> Um, so to get the phone call from Atlanta, it was great. And that's another reason why I picked Atlanta. >> Zarius, your defensive coordinator, Rick, he's been through a lot, same as you recently as well. What's that relationship been like? Obviously, it's in the early days, but what's it been like with Rick? >> You know what? When I first met him, he told me his situation. I don't know if he knew about mine or not, but he told me and I said, "Coach, come here, man. Just give me a hug, man. Cuz I know exactly what you going through, man." So, that's how we immediately connected. Um, and when I sat down and talked to him, he kept it kept it 100 with me, man. He was like, "Z, whatever you may need or however you may feel in the game, just let me know and we can adjust." So, I'm a Dcoordinator that's willing to do that type of stuff, man. Um, tip my hat off to him, man. And I can't wait to get an opportunity to play for him. >> We talked to Nate Ali earlier today and he mentioned you bring the iPad out and you're coaching up the younger guys. You're already doing that. You haven't been here long. Why is that important for you to do that? >> Uh, cuz it's all about passing the game to the next generation. Um, when I I can remember when I was a rookie, I had guys like Terrell Suggs, Eric Wed, CJ Mosley, um, just a bunch of guys, man, older guys that was veterans. And I I learned from them, and that's why I was able to go off and do great things in the NFL because, you know, I took notes from them guys. So, um, now that I'm in year 12, you know, I think it's time to pass the game down to the younger generation, man. And uh we got some great guys in the room. Uh like I said, I'mma take him up under my wing and help him the best way possible. >> What are your first impressions of Nate Holly? >> Uh great coach, man. Uh I love him, man. Uh guy who can get the job done, man. Um but I can't wait to get started, man. Hopefully next week I can put the pads on and uh we'll go from there. We just talked about the emotional journey obviously that you've been on in the offseason, but what were your emotions when you realized I'm getting an opportunity to not only play football again, but to be at a place that is close to where you grew up? >> Man, I don't know if people believe in God, man. But it's nothing but God. U obviously he had a plan for me and he knew what I was about to go through. So, um, now that I'm past that, it's really just getting back on the field, man, and being who I am. You know, Zadirius Smith dog crawling, getting sacks, and helping the young guys. You know, >> you talk about finding uh the joy. Sorry. Go ahead, Sam. >> I was going to say, have you allowed yourself to think about running out into the first home game with some family members here to see you? >> That's a great idea, man. I'm thinking about that. So, I've been thinking, should I do a Greyhound bus, you know, two Greyhound buses and just park it in front of my church because that's the people who my mama always wanted to come was the church family. Um, so to park two buses in front of the church, possibly put it on Facebook like if you guys want to come to the game, just get on the bus. So, I'm working on that right now. >> You talk about finding the joy in in the game again and coming back to you. And there was a moment, you know, it's your first game up in Indie and you're not playing this past weekend, but the whole team rushes onto the field and there's a very clear shot of you running onto the field as well. >> Uh when you kind of take that whole moment, like how much of that moment was that joy just like coming back? >> Um just after what I just told y'all. Um and if y'all go back and watch the video, you'll know the reason why now. um cuz I haven't been that happy in a long time, you know. So, just to be around a great group of guys, um I feel like in the locker room, we can relate to each other because we are the chosen ones in our family and don't nobody really take care of us. So, to come here and be able to have that joy again, I I feel comfortable here and it's feel like family in the locker room. So, that's where I get the joy from for sure. Zarius, what did you learn about yourself over the last year plus? >> I could say after I retired, um, being more of a family man, being with the kids, taking them to school, giving him a bath. I would say with my oldest son, building that relationship with him because he's 12. So you got to think about, sorry [clears throat] my voice at 12 years old, me being in the league for 12 years, I missed out on so much from being around him. So I say just growing as a father and as a young man, you know, >> being as vocal as you are, is that has that always been part of your your game? Yeah. >> Yeah. I always tried to uh communicate the loudest. I mean, I think it started when I was in middle school playing basketball, just communicating and trying to be, you know, you get a lot of stuff done just by just by talking. You know, if you go out there and be quiet, a lot of things can go bad. And I feel like when the whole defense is talking and communicating, um the play the play shows. Was that kind of a a goal to bring that sorry uh kind of to the defense when you first arrived here? Did that come about a little more naturally once you felt comfortable? Like >> it definitely was a comfort thing. You know, you don't want to come in and just I mean, you're going to come in and communicate, but you the guys don't know you. You don't know the guys really. So, you're just trying to um break the ice and try to earn their respect cuz anybody can go out there and just say anything, but the guys don't respect you. It's kind of hard to listen to a guy that they don't respect. So just having to earn a respect of the older guys but going out there and and communicating at a high level they um they respect you a little bit more. >> You noticed in kind of the fiveman fronts you've slid off to the edge at times. Uh as a pass rusher, how do you feel like your game where is it and where do you think it can go? >> Um it has to get better. It definitely has to get better. Um I wouldn't consider myself a pass rusher yet. Uh just outside linebacker sometimes but um you know it needs to get better. you know, I've I've been put in that position a couple times, so just being able to work on it. But it's good that I'm getting different exposure and, you know, our whole linebacker room can be moved around to that spot and we all have. So, just being able to um put that in our arsenal as a linebacker core um be great. >> And the last last one for me is um I can't think of maybe a better linebacker for you to be paired with than Devon Dappo like in the league. Just your backgrounds, your skills, >> what have you learned from him and how much has he imparted upon you? It's helped me a lot just because he's been a safety before just like I was in college and he actually made the transition in the NFL. Um, so his was a little bit harder than mine. I got to play a little bit of linebacker in college. So, just being able to learn from him and see what he sees and we think alike a lot of times just because we both play that position and having to guard slots on third down and being third down backers. um being three down backers, being able to play first, second down, and not having to come out on third down, being able to stay in and guard bigger tight ends or even slots. So, um it's good, you know, having him in front of me and being able to help me. >> Other than Divine, has there been anyone you've leaned on so far this summer? I mean, I feel like all the the whole defense, uh, everybody just has helped me and, you know, everybody give me a little bit of tips here and there, like the back end, Jesse Bates, and, you know, Xavier Watts and AJ Terrell and Mike Hughes is just, it's been great just listening to those guys and they help me out and they tell me to take over the huddle. You know, hearing that from guys that's that's been in the game and, you know, made a lot of money and made an impact on the game. so far. I mean, their careers. It's been great for me to be able to listen to those guys and understand if they're they're on my side. You know, we're all in this together. We're trying to win. >> And I know Nate Ali's not your position coach, but talked a lot about nicknames this morning. Do Do you have one yet? >> Uh, no. They just called me KD. I had the logo in college, but I feel like I got to earn that one before I start start saying that. >> Tell us about your progress since you've been here. Did you give yourself if you could give yourself a grade, what would you say beginning up to now? >> Um, if I can give myself a grade from the start of camp, I'll say a C++. You know, just being able to There's a lot more I got to get better at. Y'all see the good plays, but there's a lot more things that I can I can work on. I don't just say that just to be humble, but there is a lot more things that I need to get better at, and I know that. So, just being able to come in with the same mindset every day. Kendall on sorry one more that good a good play that you had was uh that screen against Indie where you kind of read it immediately. I don't think I've ever seen somebody just predict play like that. How can you walk me through how you saw that so quickly? >> Um the play fake I mean it was just >> uh I would say just film study and you know having guys you know the guys on the outside they helped me out a lot once they saw it. They was yelling screen. So, just being able to get my eyes in the right spot and seeing the lineman um get out late, just being able to go and make a play and just try not to miss the tackle.

title: Nate Ollie & Justin Hood speak on defensive development through AT&T Training Camp | Atlanta Falcons
text: What's your uh you know confidence level being able to create pressure with three four not having to blitz a ton? >> Uh man, we got a good group of guys that we that we're working with and then man it's whatever it takes to win on our part. If it's coming with five, coming with six, rushing with four. End of the day is whatever it takes to win. >> You go into a year with an idea of we're going to be blitz he savvy we're going to have to evolve and become blitz he savvy. I mean how how do you enter a year like from a mindset viewpoint in that regard? Uh, like I was saying, man, every every time you going into there, man, my mindset right now personally is just whatever it takes to win. If it's blitzing fives, it's blitzing six, it's rushing forward, whatever we got to do to win, we trying to win games >> without James, without Walkers. I mean, like, do you have to, do you need more out of the guys you, you know, have in your room? Do you, how much can you do what you guys did last year? Can you repeat it with the guys you have now? Oh, I mean, how how do you kind of >> man? Just uh just asking everybody to to step up uh step up, you know, fill the shoes, but whatever we got to do to win. Uh that's that's the most important part. Whatever it takes to win. >> Senary Smith, what what does he bring to kind of the group and and this defense? >> Oh, he's juicy, man. Like watching him, he still he's still got some rush left. Uh he looks good out there and uh just excited. He brings energy. Great energy. What he's bringing to the group, it's infectious, man. Everybody's loving when he's around. Uh even like we was out there at the game and he got his iPad. that he's coaching guys up. He's out there like, man, if you hit this move, you would have got this. So, just bringing a vet in there, having a veteran presence in there, and it's everybody can lean on him. A guy that been doing it for a long time, that's exciting to have. >> You talk a lot about energy and physicality. Do you feel like this group is where you want it to be entering week one? >> Yes, man. We It's always there's always room to improve, to work every single day, but love the energy uh that these guys are bringing every single day, man. That's what we we got to have energy. Got to have juice, especially on the defensive line. So really want those guys to embrace the dark room mentality and getting off on the football every play. >> What have you learned about this year's group? There's some civilian faces, but there also a lot of new faces. >> There's news, man. Just this group, man, was really these guys just willing to learn and embrace that dark room mentality. There's a lot of guys coming in uh just new to a tactile system and more than anything that tactile it's a it's a mindset more than anything. You know what I'm saying? Like get off, get off, get off. And it sounds like I'm not coaching, but I'm really coaching. Like that's that's what it is. is getting off the football and having that dark room mentality and blowing stuff up on the way. >> When we talked to Mason Smith, he was saying that he felt like in this attack style front that you preached like that there was a level of this game maybe that we could unlock. Have you seen that come to fruition out here? >> Yes, it takes the it takes the thinking out. Uh man, like I said, you think, you stink. So, just telling those guys just to line up and just go, right? Go. Like you're not you're not reading blocks. Uh you're just blowing stuff up, right? It's all just it's controlled chaos and just doing that right getting the guys get off the ball. The dark room mentality takes the thinking out just going to get off the ball. >> Where do you feel like Brandon Dorless is at this point? >> Uh as in >> like in his development. How's he been doing? >> He he Oh, Doris, he been doing great. I've been doing great. We've been telling him just chasing every day just consistency. Just being consistency. Not not so much the the sacks and things like that. If you just work every day about being consistent, every the sacks and everything else, all that stuff will come. Just being consistent every day. >> You mentioned, you just said that it may not sound like I'm coaching, but I'm really coaching. Do you think that the the way you coach gets a bad rap of not being coaching, just being, "Hey guys, go get them." Do you? >> No. No. I I don't think that. It's just I just joke with the guys like that cuz it's like it sound like I'm not, but that's really I want you to do. I want you to get off the ball and run in a dark room. >> All right. When did you first become aware of this attack style? When did you bump into this attack style system? And how did you come to think this is the way to play? >> So, yeah. So, man, my whole life I've been in Reed uh like a Reed style defense when I got to uh Philly my first year in the league in 2019 with Jim Schwarz. >> Okay. >> Uh so, that was the first time I learned about the tactile defense and I'm like, I don't want to coach Dline another way. That is my style. That's repping my style, my energy, right? And it allows guys to unlock their superpowers and to be themselves. And you could you could take a smaller defensive tackle uh somewhere and then you could get that guy running off the football or like like with the Jets like they had Bryce Huff. Like you get a smaller defensive lineman, you get that guys rolling, get them get him a head started, bam, he can set edges and do those things. So that's why I love the tactile system. It really unlocks defensive lineman superpowers. I >> was chatting with Zach Harrison a few weeks ago. He said you're a huge nickname guy. >> Oh yeah. >> Why is that? How do you come up with them, >> man? I It's something been doing since we've been in the league, man. It's just It's funny. You just see guys embrace it. You just see guys embrace their nickname. Other players call people wild dog, big dog, just whatever. And you see guys, it's is it's funny. You see them, they just embrace their nickname. They turn to their alter ego when they out there on the football field. So, it's just something that we just kept up. >> What's the most creative one you have right now? >> Right now, I don't know if y'all know we call it Kell. We call him Big Twitch. Call him Big Twitch. So, that's that's about it. >> What's your nickname? Who me? I'm just Nate. >> You got you got anything for Jack Strand? We're trying to >> Oh, man. >> trying to workshop something, >> man. That dude, he's great, man. He don't need one. He He rolling. >> Speaking of Zack, you know, he was having such a great life year last year before, uh, before he went down. How have you seen his development, especially because he was playing mostly as an edge kind of pass rusher type guy in college? >> So, uh, his role, man, just his his big thing is just staying healthy. That's that's the one thing we've been preaching with him, just staying healthy. Uh, taking care of his body. Uh because like you said, he he was he was doing great for us, right? He was kind of leading us in sacks at one point and he's the ambassador of strain. Like you talk about a guy that strains that works hard and do all the right things, man. You like you just want him to stay healthy. That's that's what we've been preaching to him like taking care of his body, staying healthy. Part of that's my part too, like with the reps, keeping reps off of him and stuff right there. Just want him to stay healthy. >> We talked to Carlos Allen Jr. on Monday. Hometown guy. Excited to What's been your evaluation of him so far? >> Man, he man, he had a great he had a great practice last week. like a great week of practice last week and we got a little joke. We had a little running joke with him in there too like we gave him a little nickname just told him I want you to be zoned out. So you out there you got to be zoned out when you out there and then so I embrace that like man he was zoned out. He was out there just doing his thing getting off the football and it just was preaching to him just man just get off the ball. You just get off the ball. If we all getting off the ball it's all control chaos. You don't want a weak link when you out there. That's when the the things happen when you got one guy getting off the ball and you got another guy reading and now it's a big old vertical seam in there. So, you want everybody getting off the ball and attacking. >> Is zoned out his nickname? >> Yeah, that's his nickname. >> When you guys landed Smith in in April, I think it was from Jacksonville to where he he's at now. Where have you seen him improve the most? >> Uh, embracing it, man. He he you talk about a guy that's embracing like the dark room mentality. Uh, he's doing that. He's he's embracing it. Uh then I think it's part of it too like just being around a group of people around somewhere people that care about him. I think that's important to him too. But I I just liking out the way he been embracing the the mentality. >> I believe you were in Houston in 24. >> Yes. >> How much did you evaluate him when he was coming out I think was it >> LSU? Yeah. I I I loved him coming out. Loved his game coming out uh young. He was young. Um didn't play a lot of football. Had some injuries and things like that. But like we was always thinking we was over there like maybe we can get this guy in attacked out front. We can unlock some potential out of him. >> Let's kind of talked about like his mind and it seems to me like he's in a really clear head space right now. Probably as clear as it's been as a pro. When when he got here, how much work did you guys have to put into trying to kind of train his mind and helping him kind of realign his mind, I guess? >> Um not not too much. just like said just show them that you care about him and just get him just embrace the dark room mentality. Uh just getting off the football. We don't you know it's not a lot of we don't do a lot of multiple defense probably a lot of front variation but as far as us up front man it's just getting off the football. So just kind of take the thinking out of them and get them going. >> Nate, you mentioned the the front variation. Can you explain some of the benefits of of kind of like altering those looks and where guys are aligning in the techniques? >> Um I won't go too in deep. Can't give away too much sauce. No, I'm playing. No, but uh No, I've been good, man. I've been in like a four down my whole career. Like a four down front, 4-3. Uh still a tact style front, but just here just being with Brick and and and you know, I was with Brick with the Jets, too. Just involving to different fronts variation. It been pretty good to see the, you know, the league changing. You got involved with the lead. So, seeing the things we doing right here, mixing in two fronts been great. >> I know he's outside of your room, but what do you think of Kendall Daniels trash talking energy? >> Oh, man. I love it. I love it. Like you talking about being a the linebacker, the quarterback for the defense out there. I love he's out there getting guys lined up. He's out there trash talking, man. I'm loving what we seeing from him right now. Everybody's feeding off his energy, too, as well. >> He communicates pretty well with your guys for >> Oh, great. Great with the guys getting guys lined up. We had it the other day like we, you know, we got a whatever, you know, check system and he's in there communicating and getting guys lined up. He It's good, man. Really love where he's at right now. >> I know Deshawn is banged up right now, but how important is uh he to what you guys want to do and do you think he might be back pretty soon? Yeah, just just with him, we just, you know, got good good game, you know, watching him, you know, free agency. Just just got to see him when the pass come on. Like where we going to be when the pass come on? Uh just looking forward to him just being there for us. >> Wise, are you guys ahead of where you were last year at this time, do you think? >> Um yeah, I think we are that we're doing a good job just up front talking about it, talking about our edge setting, talking about being more stout on double teams, talking about being more precision in our run fits. Uh he talks about that. that he preaches that and man one shoot man that's a guy that you just willing to go to war for the way that he talks to get up from the room and he got he got command of the room uh that's always important too when somebody walk in the room do they got I'm saying I don't know if I'm saying it right that roar that roar I'm saying it right >> roar yeah there we go there we go mike that out now mic that out so he got he got that about him you know when he when he come when he steps in front of the room >> when uh you know being with him for a couple years now you know you as you're working your way up as a coach how has he made you better as a coach Uh man, he's he's always challenging you. So just telling guys like everything just happens for a reason and just you can you can walk around with your head hang down low or walk with your chin up and good things happen. Um, good in the meeting room, good out on the grass. Uh, young energy, youthful, um, ask a lot of great questions. So, he's fun to work with and uh, you know, you you you come in with him every single day and you just see how eager he is to learn. So, it's encouraging. >> What's your confidence level when he can play a lot of snaps early on this year? >> Yeah. Um, his preparation will tell us that, right? and how he progresses. I think he missed the last maybe three weeks of practice around around there to not be out there. I mean, he kind of acclimated well, it would appear, but how much did that hurt him, do you think? >> Yeah. So, we always challenge our guys to to we call them free reps, right? So, uh, reps that aren't taxing on your body. I'm not on my feet taking the rep, but I'm learning through the guy in front of me. Um and and so far he's used those reps, right? So that's important and it's also gonna help facilitate his growth. >> Jesse's missed quite a bit of practice just with the team and that's allowed Demarco Helms to get some time. What What have you seen from DeMarco um that's why you put him in that spot? >> Yeah. Um DeMarco's growth has been great. Uh it's been fun to watch him grow in the sense of uh the extra reps and you never know coming into camp like where am I slaughtered? How many reps am I going to get? Especially when you have guys returning. U Marco stepped in. we haven't missed a beat and it's been really fun to watch his growth. I've been with Marco for three years now. Um, you know, this is the best that he's looked and I also think just in terms of his approach and his work, I can't commend him enough. >> And then next to him, you got Xavier who's now playing with a guy who's like less experienced than Jesse at least in that position. Is it does that help Xavier kind of take more leadership in in that respect uh with this position? Um, I wouldn't necessarily characterize it as leadership, but you definitely see that there's more communication. Um, when you start to play with someone, you know, when X and Jess are on the field, you kind of develop a chemistry, if you will. Um, some things don't need to be said, right? It's forced, you know, DeMarco and X to communicate more, right? So, um, it's been fun to watch that as well. And I think, uh, you know, when you look at X and just his preparation and obviously the play style that we saw last year, um, you kind of see that come to fruition. and then playing with, you know, uh, u Demarco, you kind of see how he can become a leader in some regard. So, >> following up on Xavier and what you just said, how would you compare where he is now compared to when he was a rookie at this point last year? >> Um, I think his preparation, his approach has definitely grown. As a rookie, you know, you don't really know what to expect. You come in and, oh, these walls are pretty cool. Oh, this is my shirt. This is my jersey. None of those things really affect him or he's not interested in those things at all. um you you kind of just see more focused and narrow focus, right? What's important? What do I need to know right now? What's going to affect me right now? Um and then we always talk about, you know, just really understanding our defense at the highest level, which is great, but then taking in the indicators from the offense and he can play with more anticipation. >> What do you feel like is underrated about what X brings to the field? >> Um I would say his his calm demeanor. I don't know if you guys have spent a lot of time around X. Never too high, never too low. It's really fun to watch because it's like I I don't know if he's paying attention. Oh, he is paying attention. There you go. So, um he's just extremely calm and it also brings a calming, you know, kind of comfort I will I will say to uh to everyone else around him. So, it's been good. >> How beneficial has it been to watch the relationship between he and Jesse over the last year? >> Uh it's been great. So, um you you watch Jesse, right, who you know has been an allp pro, pro bowler, all of that, right? And you watch him work with a young guy, right? you watch him uh kind of help and and and facilitate the growth of X. So, um naturally through that they develop a really close relationship which has been coming uh fun to watch. Um but you you see Jesse kind of take X under his wing if you will and and help facilitate that growth. So I think that's just the leader that that Jesse is and kind of who he is as a person. So it's been good. >> Getting back to Avon, has he progressed more at this point on the outside or as a Nickelback? Um, I think where he's progressed the most is his understanding of defense and then his understanding of how he's going to get attacked. Um, the thing with him when you put him on the on the grass, it's you can see the coverage skills. I think right now it's just helping him facilitate the uh, I guess the football IQ, if you will, which isn't low, but just the awareness of fast motion, what windows, you know, what's a change down compared to a rundown, all of those things. So, um, not necessarily if he's inside or outside, it's just more so his his mindset in terms of how he's being attacked and how he looks at offenses. >> Justin, when you got two former safeties who are, you know, 64, 65 in the heart of the defense, I'm curious, how does that impact the secondary and the way that you guys kind of work with the linebackers in coverage and in tandem with all of that? >> Yeah. Well, you're talking about length specifically. >> Yeah. Well, I'm a short guy, so I like having length. Um yeah, it it closes the windows, right? Makes it harder on the quarterback, all of those things, right? Um this is the game of football, right? The land of big people, if you will. So, um it definitely helps to have length, half size, and then, you know, obviously the speed to and the movement skills to, you know, go along with that. Do >> you find that allows your guys to maybe take maybe more risks or like play on the ball a little more freely or anything like that? >> Um I wouldn't necessarily say that. What I would say is that it allows them to be um I guess the word would be more forgiving, right? You don't have to be as exact knowing that um you know, I can still reach the ball if I need to or I can close this window if I need to. Um but length is a good thing. Um you know, we always look at like tackle rates, you know, PBU rates, uh ability to affect throws, things like that. And length also comes up like when you're evaluating those types of things and defensive players that can do that. How does the how difficult is the DB room making it on you to decide who's going to make this football team? >> The thing I I love most about the the room is that it is about competition. Um and it's really cool to see because it is a a healthy competition. Those guys come in ready to compete every single day. Um and there's a a natural friendship to it, right? Um I think it just goes back to our team. You look at the first touchdown that we scored last last week, right? Everybody ran out on the field. It's the same way in practice. It's the same way in the meeting. You ask a challenging question. just like ooh let's figure this out together, right? So, um it has been difficult or will be difficult, right? The the business side of football. Um but it's been really fun to just watch guys come together collectively and try and grow. Bless you. >> Excuse me. >> Have you seen CJ Henderson take strides in the last what two years since you've gotten? >> Um yes, without a doubt. And and it's been funny. So, you can naturally see the you've always seen the uh natural ability, right? The movement skills, the speed, the tempo. Um, you know, I think right now he's playing with the most confidence that he's ever had. And I commend him because he's done the work, right? That's that's who he is. And since he's been around here, like he's been he's been really fun to work with. Asks a ton of questions. And we joke all the time like he is always in the building. Like he is here. He's he facetimed me last week and I'm looking up, you know, through the FaceTime. I'm like, "Oh, you're you're in the team room, huh?" He's like, "Yeah." Like he's he's always here. So he's put in the work. So it's been fun to see his growth as well. I believe you were at Kent State when Clark was coming out of high school. How how much did you recruit him then, if at all? >> Uh, I did not recruit Clark because when he was coming out of high school, uh, I think I was like coaching division three football or something like that. So, probably. Okay. >> So, Clark wasn't about to come play for me. >> So, when you got here to where Clark is at now, how much have you seen him improve? I mean, how do you kind of weigh his game so far? >> Yeah, the biggest thing with Clark's been his mindset. um when I first got here uh he came in and the the biggest questions were how do I make plays, right? So his mindset was I need to go make plays, right? I could have 20 bad plays but I made an interception, right? So and I talked to Clark about holistically like where we can take his game and how he can grow, right? and he's done the work and and to this point, right, coming into training camp, um he's put himself in position to not only make the plays, right, and have big plays on the ball, but also be right on the other 19 plays where the ball doesn't necessarily come his way. Um and Clark is also got he he's always here, but when I come into my office, I promise you, 5 minutes later in the morning, Clark Phillips walks in and he essentially starts the day with me in my office um asking a ton of questions. his notebook is full of full of notes. Um, so you just see the growth from how do I make plays? Can I make this interception to okay, let me understand where I need to align, where my eyes need to be, what's my process to make sure that I'm right on every single snap. >> He uh he said yesterday he's hooped with you >> prior. >> Clark quite the hooper. How's Clark's game? >> Clark and I have played basketball. Um, let's just say that that day I didn't lose a game. >> Out of how many games? Uh, I don't want to embarrass Clark, but it was four. No, I'm joking. I'm I'm joking. Uh, Clark's a good athlete, obviously, and I'm, you know, old, short, and bald. So, um, Clark's definitely a good athlete. We'll leave it at that. >> I may be connecting dots that aren't there, so just bear with me there. But when it comes to the cross training of Avon Terrell and obviously at the beginning of camp getting a lot of reps outside moving more towards inside work as of late in terms of the bulk of his reps. How much of that was facilitated by how much Avon had grown in his development and y'all wanting to put more on his plate and simultaneously the work of my Q's across from AJ. Does that make sense? What >> it does it does and I would say it's more so the work that 12 has done right. Um, so, okay, he can handle more. Let's give him more. Let's see how he thrives. Where is he gonna fit best? Um, and I would say it's more so his work. Um, and Mike's done a phenomenal job. Mike Hughes is a nine-year NFL vet, former first round draft pick. Like, he came into it with the highest expectations for himself and his competition in his mind is how do I become the best version of myself so that the Atlanta Falcons can move forward and get to where we want to get to? And I think both those guys have done a really good job. When would you like to see Jesse Bates ideally back on the field to be ready for September 13th? I imagine he doesn't need a ton of time. >> Um Jesse's when he's ready to go play, we're excited to throw him back out there. We've all seen what he can do, the ball production, the leadership, his play style. So when he's ready to go, we'll be excited about it. >> Clark and AJ have brought up at times that it kind of seems at least for them that you're preaching the ball more and scoop and all that stuff. Is that a Kevin thing? is that you guys as a staff just collectively trying to preach that more. >> We've always preached the ball. You know, as a defense, we talk about the ball being oxygen. Every time we start a meeting, a defensive unit meeting with brick, we start with the football. Um I think the term coin the the the term if you will of of scoop, right? Kevin's come in and made an emphasis of if the ball is on the ground, we scoop, we pick it up. So, um for us, I think often on the grass, what you get is what you emphasize. So, often, you know, we're just yelling scoop the ball up, attack the football. Um, you know, turnover margin is a big indicator of of wins, if you will. So, if we can take the ball away at a high rate, we're going to put ourselves in position to at least have the chance to win games. >> Thank you, guys. Have a good weekend.

text: You guys seem to really, it seemed like both sides of both offense and defense maybe a little slower start than you guys wanted, but you guys really came around on both sides. >> Yeah. As soon as you let it out, what's it do? It just it goes. So, that's that's basically what happened today. You know, we were able we were we were a little wild at sometimes, but I think everyone had had fun and it was pretty pretty um had good had pretty good sportsmanship for the most part. Uh I wouldn't say it to wake us up to get going. No, I think I think we were already I think we were playing well. I think there was just certain things that maybe one or two guys had messed up in that what people were calling slow in the first, you know, part of the the practice.
