title: Jesse Minter Recaps Joint Practice With Commanders | Baltimore Ravens
text: Uh really good work. Appreciate the Commanders coming over, making the trip. Um again, another great opportunity for us to to really get that real real work in against somebody else. A lot of a lot of great stuff on in all three phases. I think obviously look at the tape to see it in more in detail. Um but I really like where we're at, like where our team's at, like the uh physicality that we're playing with, like the competitive spirit that we're playing with. And uh we'll have a lot of things to to learn from hopefully and get better and uh keep chasing the best version of us come September. >> Coach, I know you probably didn't see too much of Lamar today, but uh we got to talk to him a little bit. What have you thought about him and his kind of comfort level that he's developed with this new offense? >> Yeah, I think Lamar's done a great job. It started obviously it started all the way back in the spring. Um you know, I think he really enjoys the offensive coaches, the offensive system, what they're trying to do. He understands it all. Um he kind of sees the vision and sees what it can be. Uh so now it's just the daily process, daily work to get the reps that you need to get, get the plays in, get comfortable with all the different things that that uh you know, we're asking him to do and I think he's done an unbelievable job. Um so I'm looking forward to seeing that seeing that in live action here soon. >> Coach, see with you know, obviously it's a little tape as you said, but what did you see from this practice maybe that was different or stood out from the two of Minnesota? >> Uh I you know, I honestly, I'm not sure yet. Just just not having seen the film. I thought uh the special teams period, I thought there were some really good work there on the kickoff kickoff return stuff. Like that kind of makes it almost like individual battles where you can evaluate players, uh but also within the team setting. So saw some really good things uh during that period. Uh I thought defensively I thought we started out really well in the red zone. Uh you know, both in the pass scale and in the team. I thought our guys were locked in on what we're trying to do, what we're trying to take away. Um and then again, just kind of look at the tape. Uh, I've I've, you know, just looking back and forth, I think Derek had some really nice runs. I think we're able to get some good movement. I think we improved on some of our blitz recognition and things like that. Uh, so again, you're searching for improvement and I'll look forward to really diving into the tape here here soon. >> Now that the joint practices are over, did you get the value you wanted out of them, especially for the starters that will not play at all this season? >> I really do. I mean, we got three really good days of, um, you know, you can you can practice good on good and I love the way our guys compete in practice and, uh, we practice at a high level and physical and things like that. But when you when you get a chance just to go against somebody else, it just sort of it sort of gives your mind a little bit of that game mentality, getting ready to defend something, being able to look at tape and and look at things. So, I think we got a lot a lot out of it. We were able to try some different things, uh, you know, schematically on both sides of the ball. So, uh, I love the work that we got. Glad we did it and, uh, now it's now it's on to, you know, obviously wrapping up this preseason, figuring out the the very best 53 players for this particular team at this particular time, and, uh, then all eyes forward to Indy. >> As you close out this, uh, training camp, is there anything that stood out to you? Something, I guess, that biggest area of growth, I guess, for >> Yeah, um, I mean, it's it's just been so many things. Uh, when you see young players come in, um, you know, you hope you kind of have a vision for what you how you want them to develop, what you want them to be able to do. Uh, I think all of our young guys, I mean, you can all I can point to every single one of them of of just tremendous areas that they've improved in and gotten better in. Uh, and so, I think that's a credit to them as players first, credit to the personnel side for bringing in the right type of guys, credit to the coaches for working with them. Uh, so, I've just been overall pleased with just the improvement in the development that we've made with a lot of our young players. >> Just saw Zay and Zion on the sideline. >> Nothing major. Both of those guys, uh, dealing with some minor things and and looking out for the for the week one week one health versus today health. >> Jeff, do you have any update on Tony? I guess he's playing Friday. >> Yeah, he's again dealing with something small. I'm not sure if he'll make it to Friday. We'll kind of see how that plays out. But just dealing with dealing with some minor things. >> Coach, it seems like on the defensive field, some of your leaders like Miles Killebrew, Miles Wilson are making plays. How good is it to see kind of your best players, your leaders kind of coming up with those type of >> Yeah, it's awesome to see. Um you know, you want your best players, your most vocal players, your leaders to play the not necessarily have to play the best, but play with the right mentality, play within the scheme, do the things that they're supposed to do because now they can lead by example. They can hold guys to that standard. We got a great thing with those guys right now of just doing their job, executing, being where they're supposed to be. And it shows up when they make plays. And and those three guys in particular Trey and I mean all the guys, Coleus. We got a lot of really good players that if we if we do what we're supposed to do and we execute and we work together that it'll be hopefully a different guy every play making a nice play and everybody will have a chance to make plays. >> Jesse, a couple of minutes ago you mentioned like talking about this practice and then looking forward to roster cut down. In between there's a football game to play. And I'm wondering what are you looking for from that in terms of who plays maybe the different than before and what you're looking to get >> Yeah, there there's potentially a few more guys. Not a lot, but a couple more guys may add it to the to the not play list, but you know, I see this man as there's a bunch of spots that guys are fighting for. And it's a it's a great eval opportunity to not only figure out the the uh you know, latter part of the 53-man roster, but also the practice squad. And so it's an unbelievable eval opportunity for us. We still want to play to the style of football and the identity that we want to play. And uh that's what we'll be looking to do on Friday. >> Coach, having not had an opportunity to see the film yet, what if anything stood out to you about Washington? >> Yeah, Washington, I think they have a really good football team. Uh they dealt with some adversity last year with a lot of injuries. I think Jayden Daniels is is one of the one of the premier quarterbacks, has a chance to be one of the real premier quarterbacks. Uh obviously played like that a couple years ago. He dealt with the injury last year. Um but when you have a guy like that, it gives you a chance. And so, now you know they got some weapons on offense. They got a bunch of versatile pieces on defense. Uh they got some they added some really good pass rushers. Uh they got Frankie Luuvu. I mean, they got a lot of talent, and I see a team that that plays really hard, plays with a good spirit. Um and so yeah, I think those guys, you know, it'll be fun to watch. >> Coach, in the recent past, they've mostly gone with the 25-25-3. Do you have discussions with Eric about that? And would you say that that's something set in stone, but that would be the preference? >> I think there's a there's a beauty in constructing a 53-man roster, to your point, where you know, there is a requirement of like uh minimum number of players at every position to be able to function at a level throughout, you know, the first few months of the season. Uh you know, there's also I think maybe at the very bottom there's wiggle room to take a potentially best player available in the final spot or two. So, um you know, it'll be interesting to see how it shakes out. Eric's done an unbelievable job with the roster, and uh you know, look forward to seeing how we, you know, uh come together and and see what it looks like come this weekend. >> Coach, how do you mentally prepare to get ready for the next game? And with the 53-man roster, how do you kind of take it in and figure things out on your end? >> Yeah, I mean, it's it's constant evaluation of the guys and constant um you know, I I think like you really have to keep like a running ranking of players in your head. And that that's for the position coaches, that's for the coordinators, that's for the head coach because that's really what it what it comes down to. It's not just like, oh, we get to play a game and then some of these guys will be gone. Like, we get to have input and say over who we think gives us the best opportunity to be the best football team we can be. So, it's a combination of going in and evaluating it, looking at it. I do think, you know, it's like, where do you put more stock into joint practices versus a normal practice and trying to weigh all that, trying to weigh the age of players, all those things and um put the pick pick the best guys that we can. >> Two more. >> How do you approach it with your voice, your input now this year compared to years past where I'm sure you're part of the discussions, but you know, there's a lot of people in the room with that. >> Yeah, it's the same thing. I mean, it's just uh I think, you know, I think you come up in this profession, you get to this spot, like, you you you want to uh help identify the guys on the team and and you I think we work really well together uh in that regard of kind of what we want the team to look like. Uh so, it's constant just conversations, communication, collaboration, um and again, just trying to all put our heads together to come up with the best roster possible. >> Good. >> Thank you.

You know, it's a blessing for all of us to be up here. Able to have these joint practices really cool. And it's cool after. But you know, while we're within the lines, you know, we we all feel the same way. We're I'm just a Carolina Panther. That's all that matters. You know, within those those lines. >> Bryce, can you take us through the pick down the middle of the field >> [clears throat] >> where you tried to get the team back? >> Yeah, yeah, bad decision. One of those that you want back. One to force a play down field when there's not one there. And again, that's things that you know, you got to watch going going to the film. Make sure that you have that mindset of of growth. And you know, obviously that's not not a decision that you know, I need to be making. So, again, this is what these camps are for to be able to able to grow. >> Bryce, joint practices can get kind of spicy sometimes. You know, how do you find the balance between taking it too far and then just having high energy? >> Yeah, you know, I think that you know, it's just the competitive spirit with the professional mindset. I think both teams did a good job today. You know, it's always going to get Yeah, it's going to get physical. You know, it's always going to be up a a little notch in joint practices. But also, we understand we're all pros. We're all fighting for the same thing in different spots. You know, we all have the same you know, that level of of mutual respect. So, you know, not not taking any steps off the gas, but having that respect for each other. And I think you know, I was only on our field in special teams, but from what I heard, I think we we both sides did a good job of that today. I love how tough we are. I love our mindset. I love how willing we are to go to that next day again, good or bad. We've had so many opportunities to turn the page. And I think we've done that. I think that, you know, being able to have this extended period of training camp, having that extra week, it's allowed us that that time to, you know, kind of feel the mundane and and learn how to fight through it. That's a lot of what the season is, you know, when you get into those double-digit weeks, it feels like you've been doing the same thing every day. How do you still find that same spark? How do you still have the same energy and attention to detail? I think we've done a laid a great foundation for that here in training camp. So, I'm super excited, you know, for the rest of this week, rest of camp, for everything to play out, you know, how it does. But, I mean, I couldn't be prouder of this group for this camp. >> Bryce, you had a nice off-platform throw down the sideline to Jonathan Brooks. Is that a part of his game that maybe is a little underrated and can really help you guys? >> Yeah, for sure. Someone has super, super soft hands off the backfield, great knack for, you know, scramble drill, even routes out the backfield, certain things. He's done a great job for us in camp. So, you know, we're we're excited, you know, there's so much stuff that, again, he's been working so hard. The world hasn't been able to see a lot of, you know, a lot of things that he can do and haven't seen the work he's put in, but you know, we we love what he brings. We're excited for all that stuff, but I definitely trust him with with things like that. >> [music] [music]

title: Derrick Brown reflects on training camp | Carolina Panthers
text: What do you get out of these joint practices that you can't necessarily get out of out of a preseason game? Uh >> I think you know uh for us the joint practice I mean is good on good right like their best versus our best and then we going out here and we get great work. Um high reps uh you know a lot of situations where you know it's more than three and outs or five six seven eight nine 10 plays in a row and I think that type of work is good for the season. You never know what you're going to be putting in in week one. So just continuing to get that stuff in week in and week out has been great. >> Derek, it looked like that at times the defense controlled the line of scrimmage. At other times CJ Stra was able to find completions. How would you characterize the first team defense is dead? >> Uh you know we we had an average day. Um for us, you know, we want to be able to dominate the line of scrimmage. I mean C's a good quarterback, right? I mean he's going to find his dinks and dunks, right? They're getting the ball out quick today. So I mean for us it's about going in here, watching the tape, being honest with ourel and getting back to work. Why why' you characterize it as average? You just think what what went >> I got high expectations. I got real expectations. >> Speaking of high expectations, how do you feel about the growth of the defense just in general this uh this entire training camp? >> I'll tell you what, we're a lot farther than we were when we showed up in April. And uh a lot I would say like this, like being the older guy now and just kind of sitting around and seeing the younger guys, it's insane to like see how they were on day one. Like what in the world to like, you know, these guys are getting it. like it's it's nice to be able to sit there and celebrate with celebrate it with them. Be able to use the same, you know, terminology cuz they understand what we're talking about. Now, >> is there a certain moment with one of the young guys where it's like, okay, he he's he's going to be all right here. He's got it figured out. >> Yeah, I think uh I think the our room especially, you know, we got Lee, Aaron, KB, Parker, EG, like we got a lot of young guys in our room and Jared. Um, and I think it's just so fun to watch them like in the preseason games like you see like certain things you do in practice that don't work in the game and then you know vice versa, right? It's just one of those learning moments where like okay like this is what the structure is going to look like. These are the schemes in which we're going to get in the game, right? Like it's the constantly going in every single week and like the bread and butter is what the next team is going to use, right? We we didn't do well in this in one preseason game. Now we show up next week. They're going to try it. So, I think it's just them starting to understand that mindset and then just being able to react to it. >> Derrick, >> you guys talked after last season about how you guys have set the standard going forward. How have you seen this camp kind of live? >> Uh, I mean, I think, you know, too, like for us, you know, I think it starts with the it starts with the trenches, right? Whoever wins the line of scrimmage wins the game, right? Like that. We know that, right? Like they can run the ball all day, then you going to lose. If they if they if they can't run the ball day, you got a very high chance of winning, right? Both sides of the ball. And I think we know we know that. And like that's what our team is built on, that toughness of being able to do that up front, right? Like we continue every single day to take that step as we get closer to September 13th. I think we're going to be all right. >> You go from you go from last in the league, you know, defense two years ago, 16th. You feel like this defense is poised to to make another step forward? >> I'm going to say we working. We working. I don't want to say too much. Y'all going to try to put me on Twitter later on and cut this video out and try to do all that. So, we not going to do that. They're where would you rank this camp in terms of physicality compared to previous ones? >> Uh I mean I think they're all they're all with physicality like you always say like the first day of pads is the most physical, right? Like then like everybody's got it out of their system. Okay, now bring the technique back. All right. Now it's just not head banging, head coging the whole time. It's just getting back to the technique, fixing the technique. Like I always say like I I believe Rob and Der are two of the best guards in the NFL, right? Like, but I can't play them the same, right? Like, you got to be able to know your opponent every single day, day in, day out. >> The reason I asked is David said this was the first year in his three years here that he had to kind of tell folks to scale it back. >> Oh, yeah. We had we had some we had some good hits, some side shots, some fighting, and uh you know, you got to love it. It's like it's like coach having a whole group of grown men that get upset. Yeah. Sometimes you just go after it. What have you seen from young guys like Lee Hunter, Aaron Hall, Cam Jackson? >> I mean, their their persistence to be able to listen and pick this stuff up. Uh, I think Coach W does a great job of just consistently pouring on us every single day of, you know, we got to win the line of scrimmage. We got to get knocked back. And I think those guys are starting to take that and get extension and, you know, do all the things to be really good defensive linemen. >> Derek, you go against the offensive line daily. How would you describe the depth of the unit? >> I think we got some depth, right? I mean I mean it's good when you get all your uh all your big money guys back up front of course. Um got Monroe in there and he's learning. Feel like every single day we're gonna go out and practice. My job give him the best big dog look he can that he can see in the inside. Um, I feel like Jaylen's job is to give him the best outside look, right? And I think it's just that continu the continuation every single day of, you know, trying to get each other better, right? Like where she obviously started for a long time switching over playing him and like I said, Dame, Rob, Luke in the inside, like it's just consistency. Got Chandler Zala coming in and he's had a really good camp. Derrick, you alluded to both Dave today and Julie yesterday talked about how connected this team feels and probably the most since they've been here and somebody who's been a leader for a long time. How have you seen that evolve? When do you how do you see those things come up? Where do they show themselves? >> I think it starts with the accountability, right? Like it's not a offensive guys hold offensive guys accountable, defensive guys hold defensive guys accountable, right? It's a you know when something's wrong, speak up and say something, right? We have that we everybody has that ability, right? If some like even even if it comes to me, if I'm off my game and like somebody needs to say something to me, say it to me like and I think we've opened that door and been able to have that communication, that open forum of where we can do that. >> Derek, uh you alluded to it earlier, but the defense didn't give up a lot of deep plays, deep passes, stuff like this. Um how encouraging is that for um you know, a leader on defense? >> I mean, that's very encouraging. His bombs were back that you can get your ass whooped. So, we got to we don't want to do that for sure. >> Yeah. And then, uh, to conclude on the defensive side, uh, they put together a pretty nice two-minute drill at the end. How important is it for from like I know you're obviously a player, but to coach the rest of your team and be like, "Hey, this can't happen." And what can you possibly learn? >> Self accountability, right? We got to go in here and watch the tape. Take take ownership, right? We we didn't like the way that two minute ended, but I mean, we're going to go in here and get better. We're going to go in here and watch that tape and be honest with one another. And I, you know, I think that just it doesn't start with the coaches, right? Like it starts with the players, right? You got to get like sometimes you get in a room like get on my ass, I got to get on somebody else's ass. And that's just how it goes. >> Good. Awesome. >> Appreciate y'all. [music] [music]

title: Panthers Live Press Conference
text: Heat. Heat. >> [music] [music] >> Heat. Heat. Heat. Hey. Hey. Hey. Down. Hey. Hey. >> Hey, where do you go? >> All right, what a great day. Uh, exactly what we wanted. Demo and I, you know, talked all through the week. Uh, connected last night to make sure we got what we needed out of this day. It was a physical practice. It was fantastic. Uh, in two words, Denil Hunter, Will Anderson, I think that's four words, actually. But, um, those guys are fantastic players. Uh, that's exactly what we need to see. Monroe needs it. Rasheed needs it. Um, you know, when we dropped back today, we couldn't really do much. Uh, other than Bryce extending and and getting a couple of plays going, the rush was phenomenal and, uh, and that's exactly, you know, just the information we need to be able to regroup. Uh, the run game was fine. I can't wait to go see the defensive side. Uh, heard reports, some good, some bad, but all in all, a physical practice. Uh nothing crazy. Popped off uh with the guys. A couple of little extra physical plays. The guys handled it well. Uh got right back to work and so I was really proud of that. >> How different is it for Monroe in these joint practices going up against somebody like Wilson? >> Oh, it's fantastic. I mean, this is what he needs. This is what Monroe needs as he works his fundamentals, his technique, all the little different things. It just gets magnified when you play two rushers like this. And um we didn't need the one-on-one pass rush. We got that in the natural flow of things. And so there's a lot of good tape to coach off of. >> Bryce getting a little frustrated. He he let one rip off his back back foot that he typically doesn't do. Picked off. >> Yeah. He just competing, you know, he's trying to make something happen. And um days can get frustrating like that. And he and I kind of talked about it, you know, two periods in with a little bit of football left to go in the practice and just said, "Hey, look, there'll be days like this. We can make adjustments. You know, we can we can use chip help. We can run the ball. we can throw quickly to manufacture and we'll wait for those right moments because he's so opportunistic. When he finds those moments, he knows when he can take his shots and get those one-on- ones. And there'll be days like this. And you got to just you got to be patient. You got to move the ball and you got to find those explosives when you can get them. >> To be clear, you guys were not making those adjustments today. You kept to the script. >> We did. We we we didn't script this out. It was all call it. Um I wanted to take advantage of another opportunity for Brad to call it against a defense like this and we did use some chip help and all that. Um but again, we dropped back without help sometimes and just said, "Okay, let's just see where we're at right here." And and uh they were better than us today. >> Have you made a decision about the starters on Friday? >> Yeah, we will not play the starters. Do and I talked about that last night. Um decided the amount of work we were going to get them. This practice was really got the starters a ton of reps. They took about 75% of the snaps with the twos and threes kind of getting a little bit of work just to make sure their body's moving and they're in the rhythm of it. Um, but those guys will finish it out for us and a great opportunity for them uh to compete and show us what they got. >> Dave, what's the best way for Monroe to take the lessons here today and try to shore them up in two weeks? >> It's just right to the film, you know, and and and it's good and bad and it's both things you have to take, as I talked to the group afterwards, you know, these are such valuable opportunities to be able to go against a new group with a different skill set um to be able to see those things, you know, that maybe you start to get comfortable with something, but you got to tighten up another part of your game. So, he'll go right into the film right now um with coach Gilbert and the O line and and they'll work on those things, clean it up and and we'll go from there. >> Uh what does it say? And maybe it's something that you and Demo talked about also, but no fights today. >> Just an unbelievable um job as a group as a whole for Demo and I just communicating what we're looking for. the guy's understanding. All that does is distract us from the goal of today, which is to get a really physical practice to get as many reps as we can in different situations. We got to get the conditioning part of it. When the fights happen, it slows the whole thing down. It's like these big resets and and it's just a distraction. And so, that part of it, but I also know it's really important when when the coaches get together to plan on joint practices, your play style has to make sense with each other. And I know Demo coaches his guys really hard and they play physical and fast and that's the way we coach our guys. We have a physical brand of ball that we practice with. So, it's very comfortable for us to be in that setting without taking it personally. >> What's uh impressed you most about Jimmy Horn in this camp is he's battled up through that. his growth, the natural progression of just the time on task, spending time with Rob, spending time with Keshan Coleman in the wide receiver room, picking up the little nuances of the concepts and um throughout that whole entire practice I I mean process, he's still fast and he's still making plays for us, whether it's in our joints, our regular practices, or in preseason games. Um Jimmy has done such a great job. He's doing an excellent job fielding the ball in the return game as well, which is something that we really challenged him on this year. So, he's taking the challenges the right way and we're seeing improvement in the things that we've talked about. So, I'm really proud of Jimmy for that. >> For all intents and purposes, this kind of wraps up training camp. >> What did you learn about your team that maybe didn't know a couple months ago? >> Um, couple of things. I was talking about this with uh with the coaches and and I actually was talking with Derek a little bit yesterday, but the things I know about our group, we're a connected group. The guys really enjoy working together. um being around each other. It's it's been since in my, you know, uh two and a half years here. This is the most I've seen guys linger in the building together, do things on their own. Um and really connected that way. It's a physical group. You know, this is the first time I've had to ask them to back off of some of the collisions, the physical part up front. We always going to need that, but it was the space collisions. We were getting pretty crazy for a while there before we got into the Jacksonville joint week and and all that. And um it just says something about the group and nobody was complaining, you know, it was just I wanted guys to be smarter about certain situations. So I know that we have a physical group and then on top of that there's guys that have a lot of familiarity in what we're doing. So the information, the concepts, the growth, the things that Brad's adding, Ajaro's adding, Tracy's adding to our different phases. We're further along um than we've been in terms of just adding nuances to our core concept. So I'm really proud of that part, too. >> You mentioned that connected piece yesterday as well. said it's the closest team he's probably ever been on. >> Yeah. >> How important is that? >> It's really important. And you know, first of all, the the making sure we're on top of our details, making sure we're playing really good, clean football is first and foremost. But when games get hard, when things get challenging at the end of games, at the end of the season, that connection is going to matter. That connection is going to just allow you to give a little bit more for your teammate whether it's next standing next to you or across the ball. Those things really matter as you get down the stretch. >> How about far away is the offense right now? I know Houston's defense is terrific, but that was it looked fairly like they were pretty dominant. >> Yeah, it was pretty lopsided today. I'll be honest. title: Exclusive Interview with Jason Tarver
text: Welcome back to Cleveland Browns Daily brought to you by Bally Bet, official sports betting partner of your Cleveland Browns. And no, it's not Christmas, folks. It just feels that way because we have our great friend of the program, linebacker, coach Jason Tarver, with us. Tarf, how you doing? >> I'm good. I love my the intros that you give me every time, too. So, >> well, they're they're justified. They're earned. We get excited when we get to to spend a little time here together. How do you kind of assess this training camp, how it's all gone? It feels long. I don't know if it's felt long to you guys and the players, but this has felt like a long time obviously right out here on these fields. >> Well, I think it's it's been good. We got a lot of good reps and a lot of our younger players have got a ton of experience and you can see it. They're getting better on the field, on the field, off the field, study habits, learning how to get their bodies ready day in and day out. That's part of camp is you got to do it every day and you got to be better the next day. >> So, I said it's like Christmas to get to talk to you. I bet you thought it was like Christmas when Carson Swessinger returned to the field for you. What's it like been getting number 49 back? >> It's good. He's back doing some things and then he'll ramp up even more. But yeah, it's good to see Carson. But what was great about it is our younger linebackers got to assume the role of the play callers and that's helped us both for depth for them personally and also for our defense. >> Well, I know you're a sickler that if even if you can't be out here physically, you got to be out here mentally. Carson was out here every day. What was it like with him in the meeting room? I'm sure all he wants to do is play football, but how's he still been there as kind of, you know, really the leader in that room coming off of being the defensive rookie of the year? >> Yeah, we have competitions to see who answers things quickly or makes the call or knows the next whatever, check, whatever. And so Carson likes to be first and it's always good when somebody gets ahead of him a couple times. Just keep him challenged. But he was great. He had different assignments on the field. Sometimes just help a young player, make sure their stance is good or watch Nate. Hey, check Nate's eyes or things like that. We put he he had a lot of tasks not only to help himself put his eyes in the position, but also help the players get better. >> And he's going into his second year. Yeah. But you feel like he's like a coach in the room already. That's awesome. How about Quincy Williams who's come in and clearly you can see his speed. Been a first team all pro. Not many people do that in their career. Been a first team all pro in this defense. He brings a lot of energy, a lot of joviality, the joker, the nickname, all of it. What's it been like with Quincy? Quincy, you you said it. And in the last couple days, his getting ready to play, his speed has really showed up. And when Quincy when Quincy sets his feet, gets his feet apart of the starter downs and gets his eyes right, there's not many faster than him. He says fastest linebacker. So anytime he doesn't look like it, then that way I can say that didn't look like the fastest linebacker. So [laughter] then at Quincy, then the next play, he's even faster. So we we're excited about him. We're excited about the whole room. And at any position in the NFL, you need all different body types because you don't know when, you know, things are going to happen. Sometimes you got to play downhill run game all the time. Sometimes you got to play in space. Quincy can do all of it. So, we're glad he's here. >> All right, let's go back to last week, the joint practice. Finally, you get to see, you know, arguably the best offense in the NFL, led by arguably the best quarterback in the NFL right now, but you get to do it in a practice environment. How valuable was that Thursday here with the Buffalo Bills? Oh, extremely valuable that quarterback. He's he's basically me sitting on your shoulders tall and [laughter] he can throw it from any angle at any point in time. And it's great to see because you go in and go, "All right, look, if you're even, he's going to throw it." And it happened a few times. And what's cool about it happening is you said it is practice. So, we can learn. So, it's good to see different people. You mentioned them a little bit. big offensive line, little bit different blocking schemes, different motions than our offense runs. Awesome. Because we get to practice our rules against a real opponent before we play a real opponent. So, we it was great for that aspect. Every aspect, individual players as a defense, seeing plays we haven't seen, sometimes getting absolutely after them, and sometimes things to learn from. you have been in this league in a prominent role and you could you're old enough to remember just like I am when the preseason was oh in the first game the starters play an entire quarter in the second game they play an entire half in the third game they usually play they call it the dress rehearsal they play three quarters of football ones ones that's gone nobody in the league really seems to have a true consensus on how to operate that so do those practices like the one against Buffalo are they more important is that really probably the most important day of this whole off season >> yes because It's going full speed against somebody else. Different schemes, different humans because it gives you every day is different. Every person is different. Every game is different. And you got to figure it out. That's what's great about football. You got to figure it out quickly using your rules with your team, your communication. And you don't really I mean, you study, but you don't know what order they're going to pick plays. I mean, there's only two things they can do. They can run or they can pass. And RPO is both. That's what we say in the room because as soon as we'll find it, but there's nothing better than that and just the increased level of competition. So we need you need that. You need that. And it also allows you to anytime now it's a normal practice after that go hey remember what happened when we're not all the way going all the way up. Let's go start start your tempo. Let's go. >> What's the biggest difference for you in your room when next week in the middle of next week? We talked with Todd Mon last night on the Todd Monet show and he said you know maybe next Wednesday or so that's when we transition to regular practice. We're going to still do some ones on before that but then we'll transition. How does that affect what you guys are doing when you're getting into full actually game plan mode? We still need to learn how to play with pads. We still need some of that. So the that week is very important now um to make sure you still have all your timing. Yes. >> What happens with whatever you're playing, not the starters. Every team's different like you said. For us, we need the timing. So, that week's very important. That is going to be a Next week is going to be a big practice week for us. Not only against offense versus defense, but just playing in pads, shedding blocks, all those good things that come with real football and pads. >> All right. So, tomorrow night, preseason finale, national TV, New England Patriots. Al Michael's going to be on the call. Starters aren't playing. We know that. But in your room, not a whole lot of guys in your room to begin with. And we saw last week, you're gonna have guys, you know, who haven't played in a while, Buki, Winston, they're going to play, they might play 60 minutes for all we know in these games. How good was it to see them get all that work last week against the Bills and then know that these young guys who need these reps, East and Buy and Win and Justin Jefferson are going to get all they can handle again on Thursday night. >> Oh yeah, it's great. We talked about it today. It's this is we're all excited about getting the reps and getting better. And this is a time when you can do it. And at some point, you know, you you're battling for roster spots. You're battling for playing time. You're battling for your depth chart. All of it. All of it's alive. And learning how to make your next play your best play can happen for those guys. Another thing, linebackers play special teams. So, they'll have to cover all the kicks and then go play defense. That's incredibly tiring. So, that is cool because the ultimate measure Yeah. The ultimate measure is can you do it when you're tired? And we'll get to see some of that tomorrow. When you look at these young guys and the reps, East Mascaranus Arnold stepping in obviously alongside Quincy, Winston, Buki, Justin, all them, all the reps they've gotten. How have you seen those guys improved? And I'll start with East who it really feels like has kind of said, "Look, I I can be that third guy here." >> He's become a pro because he studies. He wants to know every linebacker position, what everybody's doing. He wants to make the call. And then he he has great pride in helping everybody get the call, get everything right, and make a play. And his study his study habits have gotten better and better. Really proud of just his process. And then if you tell him to work on something, he's working on it. Get off blocks faster. Check. He's doing that. Just keep going in his process. The more experience, there's still some things he hasn't seen. Second year player, that's cool. But proud of his process. You told me earlier we were joking if you had to go into a a frecus, you want Winston Reed with you. What do you love about Win and why do you want him with you? >> We were kind of joking. I want win with me. Um when he I mean he loves contact. When he sees it, he goes and what we've been working on with Win because he's been off for a year is his eyes. His eye progressions at the line of scrimmage. Some have been outstanding. First preseason game. It's really hard to get three people using in a game as a linebacker. He got three. He got three in a quarter and a half. >> Um so that was cool. But it's eye progression and just he hadn't played in a year. So, it's getting used to, oh, I'm in this spot. Where do my eyes go? What's this? And he's gotten better and better. So, we just want to see him keep going because we know he'll hit you if he if he's in the right spot. >> Yeah, it seems like Buki's come a long way. Certainly in his pass coverage, getting in drops, got his hands on the ball. Even that joint practice against the Buffalo Bills there was almost able to take one the other way. What have you seen from him as he's kind of continued to develop? >> Yeah, same thing because he hadn't played in a while. So, his feel of reading run pass has gotten better. He had a great break on third down last week where we had some feeder broke all the way from hash to hash. And that's one of the drills we do is you got to be able to cover six yards sideways. We call it 12 yard break. It's a drill that's bit of football. Wade Phillips and and Greg Manusky and all kinds of great coaches do it. And he just gotten better and better. That's taking the drill to the game. So when Nate does things like that, that's really good. So powerful learning how to control his body again because Nate is is taller. So, keeping his feet apart on contact, he's getting better at those and and we want to see that this week, too. >> And how's the young guy Justin Jefferson coming along? >> Justin loves contact and he plays. He's he's fast. He's quick. He's got a good feel for football. With all young guys, it's the same. You got to get aligned right and put your eyes in the right spot. So, when he's done that, there's been some good flash plays. There was a couple runs again in the first game where he was right. There's a couple. Last week he was a little bit better with his hands, but what he's learning is when his eyes aren't right or he looks at the wrong thing, then he's a little bit late. And that's progression from every young human and linebacker and safety [clears throat] and every any position. So, he's working through that right now as all rookies do. But we like how much Justin likes contact and loves to play. >> These guys realize that this is a big game for them. The guys that are going to be playing on Thursday night, it's an opportunity not only to say, "I belong on this 53." It's to say, "We're good in this room. Look at all the reps we've got. Look at the progress we made. We don't need to bring somebody else in. There's a lot at stake for for your room, I think, in this game. Do you agree? >> That's that's pretty close to what we just said before our walkthrough right now is this is your opportunity. Let's go. And it's everything you always wanted. You've built your whole life for this. Your whole life football life is shoot, let's go play. It's a game. Next play is my best play. Let's go. And and that's what we're that's what we're talking about today and we'll talk about more tonight. >> Tar, you're the best. We appreciate the time. Good luck to you and your guys on a Thursday night there against Patriots with the the eyes of the nation watching the Cleveland Browns. [laughter] >> Thank you. Great to be here as always. Go Browns. >> The best. Then we'll be back with more Clean Browns Daily right after

The pressure is yes to win, but there's also the pressure of making sure that there's a lot of people that are counting on me in this organization to be at my best and do the best and make the right decisions for this team to be successful. Whatever suc- successful is can be you know, deemed a lot of things, but there's no pressure any greater than that and knowing that there's people's if we don't have success here, there's people's families beyond mine that can be affected. And as we know, when when people in charge, you know, at the top, you know, get let go in this business, a lot of times others can can can be a part of that. So all of that drives me way more than any outside pressure. Um and you know, I'm sure Joe in his own way feels feels very similar even though it is year one for him. >> Do you have a moment or a story where all of this kind of like clicked with you of like this is what it means to be the general manager of the Buffalo Bills? This is what it means to you professionally. Always interested in that. Was there a moment that stands out? >> Yeah, I mean, listen, there's there's always going to be moments. I don't think he it's hard to put one thing. I would say the first moment >> Um, was seeing the fan base's reaction after we got in in 2017. Just um, I don't [clears throat] recall seeing the number of tears and emotions of you know, so many men, you know, for for one thing and and we we didn't even hoist a trophy. And so it honestly was a you're plenty motivated, but it it it motivates you any more like holy cow, that's to get in the playoffs. What would What would the emotions be to hoist the the trophy and you know, bring what this fan base and this city deserves is that first world championship to Buffalo. And so um, that will always stick with me. There's there's there's been very, you know, a lot of fun moments along the way of the the nine seasons that I've been here. But that one was probably the first time, Matt, that I'm like wow, this is different. This is a different fan base. The passion is um, beyond what I even realized when I took the job. >> You took the job in 2017. There were already rumblings of a new stadium. You're about to open that new stadium. I know that there's a preseason game, a couple of those, but regular season Thursday night football opening that new stadium to see this come to fruition. I know in Kim's vision as well as Terry's obviously. How cool is that for you to be a part of this? >> No, it's so exciting. Yeah, I know um, when we got here you know, they had tried multiple times to to get that going and so that was one of the things that we wanted to help Terry and Kim be a part of, have bring success here to where people will look at the Buffalo Bills in a very positive light and make this all happen. And it took a lot of people. Obviously, they were the the number one people to to do that and and but it's going to be fun. It's It's been exciting even where we're at. I know we've played you know, we've had a couple practices. We've played a game. We're about to play another game, but um it's it's cool to me cuz I've gotten texts from people like are we actually in Buffalo? Like from from the stands like because this stadium it could be in LA. It could be in in South Beach. It could be in Vegas. It could be in New York City. It's it's so nice. It's got so many bells and whistles. Our players are blown away at the facilities that they have over there. It's so nice that we don't even have to come into this facility on game day. They have everything all the pools, the tubs, the saunas, the they're fed over there. Anything that they could want. And then of course, you know, we've moved from turf to grass, which I really really appreciate the Pegulas and I know our players do. Of funny that it's much cheaper and and and more cost-effective to to roll out the turf. But ultimately, they decided to do and and I again, I know our players are very appreciative. >> And I I could you're talking to two guys who grew up here. And I I I tell people all the time when people ask me about the stadium I grew up being told the Bills would not be here long-term. Every every time. Ralph Wilson, you know, once he passes on, the NFL's not going to want the team. They're in a a market that's not going to be able to support it you need a new stadium. To see that happen and know that it's here for generations. My son who loves going to the games as you know, for Matt and his family and his daughter to go to the games, you know? That to me, that's the cool part of what's happening here. I I get emotional thinking about it, Brandon, because, you know, this is a a city that is so passionate about it and now we'll know that this team is here long-term. And for you now to be here, your roots, with your family, and your kids have grown up. I knew your kids when they were younger and going into college now, and your wife, and how cool is that to know that they're also a part of this long-term. >> No, it's uh, listen, when when you're here this long, you're you're fully a Buffalonian, invested here, and and we've we've established very good roots here and and and love it and hope to be able to stay here, you know, for for many more years and and get that trophy. But I, you know, I do think, you know, you you never know, but I do think if if most anyone else that got that was awarded the team other than the Pegulas, yeah, I think it would be a different conversation. And so, I don't think Terry and Kim get enough credit not only for keeping this team here, um, but getting this stadium and and putting the financial resources that they had to do. Yes, they had funding, but we all know that thing went way above budget. It's not something Terry would ever talk about, um, but I'm aware and and and so, I just hope, you know, when it's all said and done that people realize he how much he cares about this community and Kim and what they've done and and it's uh, it's been cool to see. I'm a proud Buffalonian. I've sent videos from where I'm watching the game up from the sidelines to some of my buddies around the league, like, "Dude, you guys used to laugh at our stadium. [laughter] Look at Look at what we got now." So, it's it's a proud It's like a proud dad moment. >> I have two more questions. One's football, one's non-football. Dealer's choice, which one do you want first? >> Uh, let's go non-football. >> Non-football. When you're not thinking about football, what are you thinking about? What are you doing to entertain yourself? >> Football. >> That's what my wife would tell you. She's like, "Can we watch something else?" And uh, I struggle. I'm in there watching preseason football trying to watch some guy that maybe we thought about drafting that's playing for some other team. But [laughter] no, in all seriousness, um, I love to golf. You guys know that. I think everyone knows. So, you know, when you know, when I'm either here and there's a little off time or I run down to South Carolina for the summer, it's play as much golf as I can and then um, just get out and and do fun things outdoors, get out on the water down down there. Just just get away. Just chill like out in nature. Love Love to fish a little bit. Um, those are probably the the two things if I'm not doing football, but uh, I struggle I struggle with enjoying many other things other than football. Yeah, I do. It's a it's a weakness. It's not it's not something I'm [laughter] bragging about by any means. >> My football question is, and this has the chance to you can answer this however you want. This has the chance to be the thing that gets like aggregated and people pick up on. Call your shot. What player that we are not talking about enough do you think could be really special this year? >> Man, that's hard. Uh, gosh, I don't know. >> say Josh Allen. >> I can't? >> That's crazy. Um, you know what's funny? I'm not going to give you a player, okay, but I will say I'm excited to see what some of the guys will do in in the new defense. Like just uh, some of the way Jim is talking about using these guys. Uh, you know, whether that's an Ed Oliver, a a Cole Bishop. >> Um, some players like that that uh, and and again, I could I could name some others just to see what they could do. Uh, Dion Walker, you know, you know, stands out as a guy that I think Dion can play in any system. Um, but I think he, you know, you know, if healthy those guys uh, could thrive. >> I don't know if you heard the story yesterday. We had it on the radio this morning. Thought I had my first hole-in-one yesterday. Literally celebrating it. >> Uh-oh. >> It never went in. >> What happened? >> We thought it We disappeared and then Jeremy White says, "I think it went over the green." So anyway, like should I feel super embarrassed or is that kind Like I mean, you know what I mean? Like I We're trying to figure out like what the right tone is here. >> I have I have one. >> one? >> I have one. >> And you know it went in right away? >> Uh well, I didn't actually see it. Two guys in the group Two guys in the group saw it go in. I didn't actually see it see it go in. Uh but they they told me it did, but it's That's 2008. It's been way too long. It's way overdue. It was at this course called The Witch in in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina. >> Yeah. So it was uh Um and it was fun. I don't know what to tell you. >> I don't know. >> Were you already at the bar drinking, celebrating, or were you actually >> said, you know, it's going to be expensive to round of that went in, but what happened was literally celebrating, I threw my hat off, I got my hand on my head like, "I think it went in. We think it all went in." And then Jeremy was the party pooper and he was right. He's like, "I think it went over the green." So I'm on my way to the cart brand and I'm thinking, "I got to remember the hole, the the the club, the yardage, everything so I can say it." Then we get up there and it wasn't. But at least I know now how I react if I ever do get a freaking hole-in-one. >> Yeah. Did you like run up and down the >> No, I didn't do that. We just We were We were celebrating it for sure. Matt had one at Olympia Fields. >> Olympia Fields in Chicago. Yeah. >> One of my buddies got uh One of my buddies played for the Blackhawks. One of my best friends growing up and it was the day before his wedding. And his rehearsal dinner that night was at Olympia Fields. And we went out in the morning, we played. It was 171, little downhill, so eight iron. So it looks good. Looks like I know what I'm doing. Eight iron, 171, hole-in-one. And I mean, that course has hosted Ryder Cup, US Open, >> good place. >> BMW, PGA. So like it's got the history. Put my name on the wall. Right? next to Bryson with the US Am, Matt Bove hole-in-one. >> ball up there? They said they >> They gave They actually made me a plaque like they would for the members that I have in my basement. They take out the hole, they put the scorecard, the logo for the course, which is cool. But if he would have got it, they do a hole-in-one pool for all the members. He would have won like 20 grand. >> Uh he gets a ball, I get a meme. I'm getting meme >> because of this. We talked about it on the radio, I'm getting meme now. >> At least you didn't do what the guy in St. Louis and fake the hole-in-one. >> the craziest It is the craziest story. It's more insane than you could imagine. >> Isn't that AI or is it just >> No, no. He actually went out early before this tournament and dropped a ball in there and fake like he knocked it in. Yeah, it was >> And then it got caught on camera. >> He claimed like he had to take a phone call. So he ran up and played the hole before his rest of his group. >> the shot. >> Hit the shot, but like put one way over the green. They came up and they're like, "Where'd you go?" He's like, "Oh, I don't know, I couldn't see it." Then they went up to the green, they saw it was in the hole. So then there was a huge prize is attached to it. They went on the cameras at the golf course and found him at like 5:00 a.m. putting the ball in the hole. >> That's the uh story of a documentary later on. >> So at least you didn't do >> No, I didn't. I I Well, listen, you have given so much time to us today, we really appreciate. We've gone for close to an hour with you here, Matt, right? Anything else? >> No, I just appreciate the time, you know. Obviously, we covered a lot of stuff today, but I always appreciate when you peel back the curtain on a lot of the like some of the stuff you were talking about with the pro people, I find fascinating, so I know the audience will as well.
