title: Tucker Kraft: 'Everything is clicking right now and we're ready to keep it rolling'
text: What about the the late hit? Would you Would you say on the sideline? >> That was No, that was just That was just competition. Like I've done that multiple times in my career now in in a practice situation where you kind of make eye contact with someone. And you know, you just you just finish on the sideline. Um Use and abuse. That's what That's what we'll refer to it as, but um no, I needed I needed some contact like that to wake up the nervous system, get me ready for week one. >> How did you feel? You Are you even thinking about it anymore? >> I'm I mean, when I'm out there competing, I'm trying to have a plan for each step I take just to clean up my footwork and my fundamentals. When I'm out there though, you know, running routes, that's really what you're asking. Like I don't I don't I'm not thinking about it. All I'm thinking about is running as fast as I can and getting open. >> Tucker, it seems like if if there's anyone who appreciates the extra contact in a joint practice, it might be you. It seems like you seek contact more than anyone. What do you take away from a practice like Does that feed the inner beast within you that that craves that and doesn't get that in training camp or what? >> Um it's kind of like what I was talking about with with K. She was referring to like an event like this, like a big collision, getting an opportunity to just move on from it. You know, people Some people might be holding their breaths when they see me do something like that, but that's just my 9-5. So, get getting an opportunity to have a a good team come in um and and give us uh you know, new looks. You know, granted it's similar defense to what we've been working with all camp with our defense. Um but joint practices are always a great opportunity to to just get new work. You're not you're not hitting your own teammates all the time. >> How would you describe the vibe in today? >> You know, I thought we got a lot of good work in. You know, you can always expect some chippiness, but as far as all the joint practices I've been a part of, this this wasn't that bad. >> You told us preseason week three you wanted to be 100% no Flacco, no limitations. Do you feel like you're at that point in terms of >> Yeah, I felt I felt free out there today. I really didn't have anyone counting my reps or you know, trying to trying to pull me out of stuff cuz I've gotten to the point now with my attitude for my health now where I feel good and I'm confident where I'm going to stay out there and you guys can take me out when I when I need to come out when I'm tired. Um if not like I'm I'm not doing the rep count stuff anymore. You can pull me off the field. I'm I'm going to try to be out there as much as I can. >> How good does that feel just to say that? >> It feels good. I mean, it's just uh the the practice coming off the pup after our first practice and and the plan that we've had um over the course of the last 4 weeks to continue to raise my my expectation and uh really just get into the the good solid positivity thoughts of availability throughout you know, the whole season. So you know, we're we're just going to continue to stack days and and we're not having setbacks and that's the key. >> How would you say the offense looked >> [laughter] >> today just in your opinion? >> You know, we were doing great. Um we just have to we have to continue to build, you know, that continuity with each other. Stacking those reps, you know, Jordan Jordan with us eligibles and uh um you know, being being more on the offensive and using our cadence in the run game, you know, really coming off the ball and playing on their side of the line of scrimmage. Uh but you know, I thought I thought overall it was a great day. >> After missing a significant amount of time last year and getting back into it today, how much did you miss it? >> Well, it's I've been I've been building this um and I really mentally I've been in it um if that makes sense. But yeah, get getting out there today and and getting more of a a move the ball call it. Those are my favorite periods because like they're non-scripted plays, you know, you have to you have to be locked in in the huddle. Um so getting an opportunity to to do multiple reps of uh the move the ball periods, uh um those are good. >> Tucker, I jumped in late. What's your overall reaction to that hit on the 17-yard >> Yeah, I mean, it's just it's just a good wake-up. Um It's uh it's it's something the coaches are always going to preach they want you to finish. Um and sometimes that requires violence on sideline. Now, you might not always win those. Um he got me good. I will admit it. I give him props. Uh but um it's just it's just uh in a 2-minute drill, got to have it. I got to finish with my momentum going forward on the sideline to keep the get the clock stopped cuz otherwise it rolls, but um you know, it's just it's just a good opportunity to get up, you know, hot stove, pretend the ground's a hot stove, get up as fast as I can, and shake it off, get back to the huddle, and ready to go. >> I saw you shake your head like this afterwards. >> Yeah, that was I was smiling. That was that was a good hit. I haven't had any contact like that since November 2nd. So, that was an opportunity for me for me right there to, you know, wake up. Season's here. >> You've been part of the camp like practicing, you've been early on you were watching from the sidelines. How do you feel this team got better during this training camp? >> Uh I would say we've gotten more in a rhythm. Um our our play pass has cleaned up significantly, you know, uh the tight ends are matched up with with edges, but we're able to sell it with our run action fundamentals, and and we're hitting those um routes over the middle in timing, and everything right now is is just clicking, and and we're ready to keep it rolling.

title: General Manager Brian Gutekunst/Head Coach Matt LaFleur Press Conferences
text: [music] Hey, hey, hey. hey, hey. It's sound. Heat. Heat. Hey. Hey. Hey. alive. Heat. Heat. N. hey. Hey. Hey. Hey. Morning. Are you the offici? >> Oh, we're letting that one go. Yeah, we're going to let that one go. Keep everybody back. See, see how it ends up. So, I got money on my guy. So, >> who's your guy? [laughter] >> Come on now. [snorts] Brian, just how cool is that though to have, you know, two brothers, head coaches on the same, you know, >> it's it's it's exceptionally special, you know, for, you know, I mean, it's obviously unique. Um, but for Matt, his brother, uh, his mom and dad, you know, probably it's an extended family. It's just a it's just a really cool thing, cool moment. Uh, at the end of the day, you know, there's work to be done, but um, no, excited, you know, happy for them because that's, you know, it is very unique and, um, you mom and dad got to be pretty proud. Judy, how much does this do for you evaluationwise? You know, you guys do these every year. And in an ideal world, would you love if there's three preseason games to do three of them, one with each team? >> Yeah, Jason, that's an interesting question. First of all, having another team on your on your field in your environment. I love that, you know, um even if we have to go, you know, [clears throat] somewhere else. It's just to be able to evaluate another team in this format is is for for scouts, it's um it's it's really valuable. It's valuable to evaluate our own guys and I think the work is really good. Uh I've talked a lot about, you know, the joint practice allows you to kind of control the competition, but it is obviously ramped up compared to a normal practice. You can protect the quarterbacks a little bit more. Um Matt and his staff can kind of really um you know, script some things that they want to see and and kind of see where we're at with some things. So, I think it's really valuable. I've talked to a number of guys around the league. There's some teams that are doing three this year. I think if we ever go to 18 games with two preseason games, you you'll probably see two every year with most teams just because we're going to need to get to work uh in the evaluations. Um so, you know, three might seem a little heavy. I mean, I you know, um I think two is probably a sweet spot. I would have loved to have another opportunity, but um we're excited for today and um and and Friday. Those are the next obviously two points to evaluate our own football team um before we have to make these decisions. So, no, I'm all for them. Um and I think you're you know, they're not going away anytime soon. If I remember right, um, last year cuts might have been on a Tuesday >> or Sunday. I know it's only a couple days, but does that do you think there'll be even more roster adjustments from that Sunday until you get all the way to the day before the game? >> Yeah, they moved it, I think, because the Australia game is the reason they moved it. Um, which I'm not a huge fan of, but um, that's a I'm not sure. We'll kind of see. I mean, there certainly could be. Um, but you know, I think the one thing I thought of it affected, I mean, we as we talked about when the last preseason game was going to be, you know, you might might love it to be Saturday, but with the Sunday decision point, it was, you know, with all the medical information we need to get after a game and stuff, it made it kind of tough. So, that's um, you know, even even with the Friday game, it limits our time a little bit, but um, yeah, that's a that's a a good question. There certainly could be. Um but um I do love the the the by-week in between. You know, when we had that last preseason game and then went right into the season after cuts, that was always I always felt that was rush. So it's it's nice to have some time to get some guys healthy and kind of work through the the exact roster mechanics that you're you know to try to get your team ready for game one. >> Just going back to the do you anticipate doing at least two every year moving forward and they only do one this year? Yeah, I mean that'll be really a Matt decision and it'll be probably year to year just on, you know, who are playing and does it make sense and and travel and different things. Um, you know, again for, you know, for a scout, you know, to be able to go see two or three teams, you know, in a practice setting like that, have that film. Um, you know, we I'd love to have that, but um I think it'll be year to year and just kind of, you know, just depending on our schedule. >> These joint practices used to not be a thing. Now they become regional. What was it that first kind of came on your radar like hey that that could actually be a good way to get ready for the season? >> Yeah, I think you know certainly when we dropped the one preseason game went to three you saw started to see more because I just think people felt that they needed more evaluation uh points. Um, and I do think, you know, the the ability, particularly with the quarterbacks, but even, you know, some other players, the the ability to kind of protect them in the practice setting compared to just playing in the games, um, made some sense. And I think, you know, that's probably why you started to see it took up. I don't know when when that kind of started hitting, you know, they all run together now, but, you know, five, six, seven years ago, something like that. >> How much can these two days swing your decision-m when you got months of >> information? Um, can two days of a strong closing statement kind of supersede all that to some extent? >> I wouldn't say supersede it, but yeah, it certainly affects it. No doubt about it. Um, you know, and obviously injuries do that as well. Um, but um, yeah, I mean, I think, you know, we I always kind of feel at this time we got more more than 53 that are good enough to make, you know, make it and and we're going to have to make those choices. Um, you know, so I think, you know, the these two um the practice and the game, I mean, they're they're really important, you know. Um, we're so fortunate, I think, you know, not only at practice to have the fans that we have and then in the game to have a full stadium. Um, that helps the environment, you know, and seeing these guys having to react and respond in that. Um, so yeah, that this that certainly could, you know, sway things. It doesn't, you know, erase the things that have happened in the past, but and you try to be careful of recency bias, right? You're always fighting against some of that as well. Um but um you know at the end of the day you're just trying to make the best decision for the Packers, you know, for the season and and moving forward. Um but it'll matter. >> I'm sure each year can vary, but when it comes to those final roster decisions, is there a challenge in balancing potential offensive or defensive contributions versus special teams? Yeah, I think you know um you're you know you're always trying to kind of you know predict or you kind of see what you know everybody's role is going to be and um you always get a little bit of that or you might have a guy who's really good on teams um but maybe isn't there offensively or defensively and then if you have injuries maybe you're not comfortable playing that player in that spot um but he's really good on teams and and and how do you balance that? So there's those discussions you know have been going on uh since the beginning of this. they'll continue and um again it's it's not easy and you know we get a bunch of coaches a bunch of scouts and if you know if you ask them to all draw that up and how they'd break down to 53 you probably get a ton of different answers you know so um you know hopefully we'll get to the end of this make the right decisions for the Packers but um there's always those those kind of uh tough calls >> when you're putting that puzzle together you're going to keep guys on the 53 who you feel like your biggest contribution is going to be teams right so how big of a swath that 53 is is what your target is. It might not just be one number, but is there is there a range that you want to kind of keep these many guys that can really help the year? >> Are you talking special teams? >> Yeah. Like you're talking like a number. Yeah. Um I think every year is different. I think you know, you know, in a perfect world, all these guys have a role on offense and defense as well. Um I think you also balance um you know, if you're going to be a draft and develop team and you're going to develop guys, um you're going to have to live with some young players playing teams for you, right? that's just kind of how how it was going to have to happen. Um so it's very hard to develop um players without playing them and if you got you know nine or 10 guys are strictly special teams guys um that's hard, right? So um but at the same time it's an incredibly important part of what we're doing. Um so I think you it varies year to year but that we don't have like a number say hey we need we need seven or eight special teams guys only and that's how we're going to break it up. We don't do it that way. It's just kind of year to year. Has that number grown for you in the past or or struck? >> No, I think it's um yeah, obviously it's it's always been a really important part. Um obviously, you know, with the kickoff rules, some things change and and it can alter things, but um again, it's I don't think we've ever looked at it from a numbers perspective. It's just really um when you're evaluating those guys um at certain positions that are going to kind of fill the back end of that of the roster like what is their value on teams? Are they going to be on the 48 you know or will they not be and um you know trying to work through it that way? >> Golden had a really good camp last year [clears throat] too, but what's the biggest difference you've seen from him on kind of the dayto-day? Yeah, I mean again he had again I think he's um much more confident in in the scheme and what they're asking him to do and the kind of nuances. Uh and certainly I think the opportunities with Jordan um I again he did have a good camp last year as well but I think the opportunities with Jordan are more and um I think that confidence between the two are growing. So I think I've seen a little bit of that. >> Ryan, you're coming up on the one year of trading for Micah Parsons a year later. What have you learned from that experience and do you find yourself less or more likely to make a similar type of deal after learning from that? Well, there's not many Micah Parsons on the planet. So, if there's others available, we'll certainly consider it. Um, but no, yeah, I think again, you know, those are rare occurrences that when when players like that become available and, you know, whether in my career another one will become available, who knows, you know, um, like that. But, um, yeah, I mean, I think I've learned a lot more about Micah being here and and and it's just strengthened our, you know, our thought process and what he can do for us. But, um, yeah, I mean, when you have there's only so many guys in the in our game that can affect the game the way he does. So, when they become available, I think you kind of you got to always kind of look at it. >> How do you feel about Tyrod Taylor's training camp? >> No, Ty has been great. He's done a great job for us. Um, you know, obviously I think I talked a little bit about just the luxury of having that experience in the room and having a guy that's played as much as he has. um cuz that guy really does support Jordan in a in a ton of ways and he you know he's just very experienced there so kind of feel very fortunate to have him. >> People obviously react to the preseason games and McCord's been pretty productive through the two games. He's obviously played a lot more than Tyrod has understandably so. So I guess how much do preseason games actually factor into the evaluation of a guy in his 16th year like Tyrod? >> Yeah, I mean they do. I mean they obviously do, but obviously he's got a lot of pelts on the wall as well. So, you know, again, I think Kyle's done an incredible job and I'm really excited to see him not only today, but then he's going to get obviously a ton of work on Friday night. Um, so, but I mean, you know, we brought Tyride in here for a reason and and we're we're very happy we have him. >> You Josh's situation is obviously still open. Um, I'm not asking you what's going on with the legal situation, but um, if he does get suspended, do you need to make another move there or are you confident with what you have that you can sustain? >> Yeah, I'm I'm I'm pretty confident we can sustain it. That doesn't mean we wouldn't do that. Um, but um, yeah, we'll deal with that when that comes, but we've obviously been, you know, you know, preparing for that if that in case that happens, but at the same time, um, I feel really good about the guys we got in that room and I think we could survive that. >> Does that mean you might have to keep an extra though? you might employ. >> I think again we'll deal with that if that if that transpires, but um we could um you know, you're always usually going to keep three or four running backs. Um and I think we have enough to do that. Um but again, it comes down to choices and trying to figure that out. And uh the one thing I think particularly at that position is um you know, elevating a guy from from the practice squad is um you know, I wouldn't say it's easy to do, but it's um something we've done in the past and and not something we would shy away from. Ryan, how do you personally balance the excitement of building the initial 53 versus the difficult conversations you have to have to get there? >> Um, you know, I think, you know, you there's there's so many different areas in our organization that kind of that that are part of this. Um, obviously, you know, our scouts, uh, the coaching staff, um, the contract, the financial part of it, the medical stuff, and those things are going on non-stop. And at the end of the day, it's my job to kind of take all that in and then and do what's best for the Packers, knowing that what we do on Sunday and Monday um may not be what it looks like on the first game, third game, and whatever. So, it's it's kind of a constant um you know, thing that we're looking at as far as what's what's best. And um again, you know, you know, you want five of this, six of that. It may not look like that right out of the gate sometimes. Um, but you're kind of I think you're looking at it more over the total of the 17 games and into the playoffs and how that's going to look and and trying to give your your team the best um you know depth and uh um just kind of maybe hardness to get through this this long season. >> Seems like you've been pretty pleased as a as an organization with Shawn Ryan's camp. Obviously the first time he's ever been able to just stick up one spot and learn it and train it. >> What was the first time you looked at him and thought he could be a center? because you never >> Yeah, I think right when we got him in they, you know, guys felt they could do it and then we wanted to train him there and then as he obviously that takes time. It's not an easy transition. Sometimes we played left tackle in college and um we were like we do it with a lot of guys we move them around but the center the center position there's obviously some certain things obviously the snaps and and um just some communication things that take some time and I I think he was doing a great job along the way uh with the limited opportunities he had but then obviously last year when he had to step in and he just got better every week not only uh with his play but then how he was running things with Jordan. Um, so I think through that time was really where I was like, "Wow, yeah, I think this this guy can do this and they can do it at a high level." Um, so it was probably then where you just you felt really comfortable. >> What what is it about a college tackle that you look at and say he can play that spot inside? >> Yeah, I think you know um obviously college left tackles usually, you know, at times the best player in that group and they're usually pretty versatile athletes. Um, usually if you have, particularly in Matt's offense, if you have the the foot quickness and the athletic ability to play left tackle, you're going to be able to do some of the things we're going to ask of a center as far as reaching and and getting out to the second level. Um, so we've seen some crossover that way uh in the past and um and Sean certainly has >> What's the uh next 40 after the game ends on Friday? What do those 40 whatever hours look like for you and Triumph in this pretty short turn round? Yeah. >> How much is a balancing act of of what Matt or Cam or whoever wants on the roster go with what you think they maybe is a long-term best? >> Yeah, it's never really about what anybody wants. It's just about what's what's best for the Packers. But, uh, I think, you know, it's just it's, you know, we we'll come in on Saturday morning and and break down the game and try to, you know, one of the things I think you got to be careful of is, you know, is not getting to it too quick. You know, allow that game to to matter and and and take your time just like you would the other preseason games and um really break that down. Um, and then, you know, over the course of the last few weeks, you know, we basically every, you know, with these guys maybe that we're trying to make some decisions on, every team rep that they've had since the spring, we're watching and comparing and, uh, comparing them to to our guys, um, to comparing them to other guys in the league. Um, and then, you know, sometime, you know, um, you know, in the evening on Saturday, I think we'll, you know, there's obviously going to be a lot of phone calls with other teams and kind of seeing where everybody's at. Um, and at some point I'll get with Matt and we'll kind of start going through it and and try to get a, you know, good idea of what we're going to do uh on Sunday. Now, we don't have to be righteous on Sunday until about 5:00, I believe, which is a little later than usual. Uh, so we'll have some time Sunday to continue to work through some of those things. Um, you know, get a good night's sleep hopefully Saturday night and uh um have an idea. But at the same time, there's so many phone calls going on between teams and possible trades and, you know, and and guys that might get cut. um the three or four days uh going through this. I mean, it's just a lot of tape watching, right? You know, a lot of you maybe guys getting let go you weren't expecting to get let go, you know, can he help your team? Um so, you're just going through all those things and um and again, it's not a it's never perfect. Um but at the same time, I think it's it's um it's a good process. >> Two more, please. >> When you look at it, Brian, these last two, you know, joint practice and the final preseason game, how do you determine or is there way to determine whether you whether a guy just flashed something or whether his arrow was really winding up and it's trending in the right direction. Like how do you how do you sort >> Yeah, I mean again we've been evaluating most of these guys since the spring, right? And you're watching them and I think you know we talk a lot about we want to get these guys into their comfort zone and early on they're not. You know, they're they're they're learning and they can be frozen out there at times because they're still thinking and trying to figure out what is asked of them. Uh some guys still might be going through that. you know what I mean? And um you know, so it's our job to kind of figure out when they do get to their comfort zone, what what kind of player they're going to be. Um the guys who are there right now, you're probably seeing, you know, start to excel a little bit with what what what they're doing. Um but that's that's it's different for every player. Um and there's there are times where guys get there quicker, but we kind of feel that the that another player when he gets there is going to be a better player, right? You know, that's that happens sometimes. So, um, but you're constantly kind of, you know, watching that and seeing how these guys are going. Some guys fade, some guys, you know, really pick it up at the end. So, um, but at the end of the day, it's it's not necessarily what, you know, completely what they've done, but it's what we think they're going to do. >> Chicago reporter, apologies. Um, in your time with the Packers, the Bears have been on a roller coaster that now was on the upswing. What are you seeing as the biggest differences in this administration? >> Oh, that's a good question. Um, I don't know if I've, you know, um, yeah, I don't know if I could say anything. One, obviously, they, you know, I had a new coach last year. Um, but, um, we've always had a lot of respect for them and and how they go about things. But, um, >> is it players? Is it coaching? Is it is it general culture change >> without being in the building? that's really hard to to to to comment on. Um but again, it's just um you know, it's obviously the team we're going to play twice a year and so we pay close attention to them and they got good players, you know, good coaches and um but yeah, nothing specific. >> Brian, you mentioned any potential moves that might still be made before 5:00 on Sunday. Are there any positions in particular that you'd like to be a little deeper at? >> All of them. you know, um you want to, you know, I'd like, you know, Hall of Famers and all pros at every level, but uh um there there's some areas I think that, you know, we'll be looking at hard to see, okay, hey, you know, how's this going to play out, but uh I wouldn't I wouldn't, you know, talk about them in here, but there yeah, there's there's going to be some areas every year. There's a few areas where you're just kind of, okay, um what's our what's our practice squad going to look like? And and the guys that we have in the practice squad, do we feel are those guys that can help us during the year? Are they more just developmental guys for maybe next year? Um, so we have a few of those positions. Um, I think the injury thing will will factor in pretty heavily in that as well. >> I know we don't talk about contracts in here. >> A couple years ago, you know, Jordan was under contract, but you were working on the extension, so you guys kind of had an understanding at the start of camp, right? >> There really was no understanding, but yeah, [clears throat] >> Ter's done everything, right? I don't I I'm guessing he's going to participate today. There is some risk involved for him. What has that told you about him that he's approached it that way? And is it a priority to have that done before you kick off in Minnesota? >> Yeah. So, I mean, I mean, you know, Duck Tuck handles himself exactly how we want him. He always always has. He's a competitor. It's important to him. Um, so, um, you know, we've always had a lot of faith and he's going to do those kind of things. Um, we would love to have that done. Uh again, you know, these things are complicated at times, but uh um we know Tuck's obviously going to be here and that's very important to us whether whether we're able to accomplish that before the the beginning of the season or not. We'll see. But um it's very important to me. I think it's uh imagine it's important to the player. Um but um these things take time and and sometimes they work out, sometimes they don't. But um we're excited what Tuck's going to do, you know, do for us this year and in the future. >> Thank you guys. All right. >> Thanks, Sound. >> [music] >> Hey, hey, hey. Hey, break down. Hey. >> Hey, Good morning. >> What do you want to get out of today? What do you hope to see today? >> I just want to see two teams go out there and compete and push each other to get better. And that's exactly what I told our team. I said, you know, the way I view it today is we're all one and obviously the ties are pretty strong. So, um, if I'm not rooting for the Green Bay Packers, I'm rooting for the Arizona Cardinals. >> Does it feel more like you're all one in this situation? We can ask you all day about your brother, but you're obviously focused on your team. Sure, you need to be, >> but that's your brother. play. Does it feel different than if that's just another >> Yeah, I definitely think it feels a little bit different. You know, I've we've had some some of my close friends like when Robert Salah brought the Jets in. Um it's always a little bit different when when there are some strong ties there, but ultimately we're just looking to get really good work in. >> How often do the two of you talk during training camp or during the regular season? How often are y'all communicating with each other? >> I would say most days at least. you know, checking in, seeing how you're doing and um but I would definitely say most days. >> It's obviously two big days coming up. Does anything need to be said for the guys fighting for spots or starting jobs or is it just so obvious that it's just standard operating procedure for them? >> Well, I think some of them are obvious, but there's many that aren't. So, we have two more opportunities to get great evaluations and then ultimately have to come to some sort of decision. And there's going to be a lot of tough decisions moving forward. >> Matt, how do you feel about the depth of this team versus some of the other ones you've had? I mean, you lost a lot in free agency. You only had the six draft picks. Just how's the depth right now? >> Well, we'll see. I think that's to be determined once guys get out there and are forced into action, which is in inevitable in this league. So, um, but I I love this group of I love this team. I love the guys. I love how they come in to work prepared each and every day. I haven't heard a whole lot of complaining going on, which I don't know if that's good or bad. Um, so they they just come in, they put their head down and they >> two week each training camp or does it matter to you? >> I would say that's ideal. I think it just all depends on the circumstances and like I mentioned before, you know, I would have loved to gone out to Denver and had a joint with them if we could have played a earlier game, but that wasn't the situation. So, it is what it is. >> Matt, will >> Sorry, go ahead. >> Will Tuck be doing uh team stuff today when the Cardinals join you guys? >> Yes, >> Matt. I think in the past, maybe even before you were head coach, the teams would kind of make their own preseason games and then the league took it over. Did you request this one specifically or how how did this work? >> Yeah, so the way it works, you get one request um certainly we sometimes put in for more than one and sometimes it happens and sometimes it doesn't. Mike said um yesterday in Phoenix that he was excited to come to Green Bay, not only because he knows the guy up there, but uh it's 113 today in Phoenix. So, he's looking for a team in the north. Do you get calls from Houston and Miami and like every year guys trying to get out of the heat? >> Yeah, absolutely. Every year it's And you know, obviously I told some of the guys like um you know, Halfley's a good example. if if we didn't play him in the regular season, that would have been a a possibility as well. >> So, you can't make a decision on who you're going to practice till you see the uh preseason schedule. Is that how it goes or >> No, I a lot of this stuff goes on, you know, as soon as the season ends, quite frankly, you know, coaches start talking about getting together with other teams and then, you know, as far as how the NFL puts out this the schedule, then there's there's some after that as well in terms of practicing together. >> Sorry. So, like with Denver, um was it the fact that it was played on Thursday night that you couldn't do it? I mean, did you want >> Well, we could have. Um, I don't know if Sean I I didn't even talk to Shawn about it. So, um, and I thought we got great work in there a couple years ago. It didn't go our way in practice, but it was still, it's still good quality work. Every every time you go out there, there's a good lesson from it. >> Mike had mentioned the other day in Phoenix about all of his kids wanting to go over to Aunt Bree's house because of her her snacks. Yeah. >> How how much is this a family reunion this week and how much is it a work week for you? >> Well, I I would say it's mostly work week. Um but there are some cool moments. I mean, I know Lauren's going to bring um her kids up or their kids up today and they'll be staying at the house. So, that that'll be fun. Do >> you and Mike sit outside after practice and chop it up or is he off on his own doing his own thing? Well, yeah, they'll go back to the hotel. They'll be watching the tape. We'll be watching the tape and then we're going to get the staffs together later this evening. >> Yeah. You know, when you've got a quarterback who's been in the system for a while, how do you challenge them in practice during the week, you know, and you're also trying to catch up other guys who maybe aren't as >> Yeah, I think every day is a challenge. Uh every every time you go out there, you know, certainly we'll put in some new concepts that maybe we don't have a lot of time on task. you see something on tape, you want to test the other side of the ball, which ultimately tests the quarterback because he just doesn't have a lot of time on task with certain certain things. >> What do you thought about the the camp that Sean Ryes had? [clears throat] >> I'd say he's he's had a pretty solid camp. I think he's really cemented himself in that position and taken control, taken initiative. Um, so I've been pretty pleased with him. I know you can never really know what to expect in this league, but how unlikely would that have stayed two, three years, you know, Ryan solidified starting setup? >> Very it it's been really cool to watch his progression. And you know, one thing I've always really respected about Shawn is he takes um full accountability for everything. um even even probably to a fault, which I think that's when you have that mindset, that's when you get better. So, you know, football's an imperfect game, there's going to be mistakes and you just you the guys that own it and just keep it moving and learn from it typically end up becoming better football players. And that's exactly the the approach he's taken. >> You had some injuries against Denver. I was, you know, thinking Savad and and Brinsen and Oliver among them. Any concerns there as far as like week one linking kind of stuff? >> Uh, potentially. Yeah, definitely. Potentially, but I think all those guys are making good progress. So, we we'll see where they're at. >> Did Bo request a one-on-one? I don't know if you're doing one-on- ones today, but is he going to get a one-on-one with his brother? >> Potentially. Were you sitting in the team meeting? Matt, Chicago reporter, a question about completion percentage. There's a lot of talk in Chicago about the goal of getting to 70% completion percentage. It's been an obsession. Is that in your mind an attainable goal for a quarterback? Does it even matter? >> Oh, it definitely matters, but I think it's all, you know, what what are you calling um you know, just the situations? Are they easy completion plays? Um, but I definitely think uh that's definitely an attainable goal. >> Do you hold certain players to or such as Jordan to s such statistical goals? >> Um, not necessarily. I mean, certainly the more completions you get, the better the chance you get to move the ball down the field. But like I said, it's all circumstantial in terms of what are we calling the the deeper the concepts that that you run. Typically, the the lower the completion percentage, especially if you're pushing the ball down the field. Um, but that's why I think as a quarterback, you just you got to make great decisions. If the deep ball is not there, can you check it down and just keep the sticks moving? Thank you. >> For guys who maybe are fighting for a roster spot or a starting job, do you give them some extra opportunities over these next two days for like a final final look or is it just keep rolling like you have done? >> No, I absolutely I think you try to be very calculated in in terms of the positions you're putting certain guys in, especially when it comes to, you know, a lot of these back of the roster spots are going to be determined by by their um ability to go out and play special teams. So, yeah, you're putting guys in certain spots to make sure that you get the proper evaluation. >> Is are there any of the periods where you won't know what uh the defense is calling or what what >> I would say every period. Really? >> Oh, yeah. >> Yeah. I mean, we we give them the personnel's um if there's some non-normal matches, they'll let us know and then you adjust accordingly. But there's going to be some call it periods where we're just out on the field and you're just playing the situation. It's great that we have NFL officials here to kind of, you know, um just so we can operate in in that type of environment, but um yeah, there's there's definitely going to be some calling. >> It might get you to adopt anything into your practice script that you uh don't particularly like. No, he pretty much uh gave me his thoughts on it and uh but we're rolling with what we've it's very similar to what we've done with other teams in the past. >> Matt, there's been a lot of rotation at guard. How close are you to solidifying the two spots? And what gives you confidence in Jacob Monk that he could potentially be one of those guys? >> Well, I think a lot of it is just what is our health up front and where can we get our guys in the best position possible. Um, in in regards to Monk, I I love the mentality he plays the game with. He just I mean, he is as tough as they come and he's I think he's shown steady progress throughout his time here, especially in the tail end of last year and then into this season as well. >> Hey, man. >> This is obviously JG's former team in here today. Um, I'm just wondering how you've seen the defense kind of develop since you hired him to now. And once he got let go, was he immediately on top on not maybe on top of your list, but certainly high on your list? >> Yeah, I would say it was a very short list. You know, I I think um his resume speaks for itself. Uh, and then just when you get around him and just his level of understanding of football, I think I've said this before, I think he looks at the game very similar in terms but just from a defensive lens, but he's always thinking like an offensive guy. So, I think he's he he does a great job communicating, holding people to a very high standard, um, and getting the most out of guys. >> Has the process been any different? I mean, you've obviously you had Joe B come in, you had Jeff come in. Has it been different transitioning this time around versus the other times you had a transition? >> I think every Yeah, there's a transition with with anybody and everyone every situation is a little bit different, but I do think we've got a a lot of brain power in that defensive room. Um, they do a really good job of adjusting. Certainly, I'll go in there and and tell them, hey, here here's what I see. This is what offenses are going to see. um you know but I'm not like hey we have to do this there for the most part um there may be a time or two I'm like hey man I wouldn't do this but u those guys have been been really receptive and we have great conversation and quite frankly I I mean I'm learning as much from them as I would think that they are from me. So >> two more please. >> You joked the other day about throwing down on the 50 with Mike. Did you guys fight a lot growing up? >> No, not really. Uh, he was more of a pest. So, there's a seven and a half years age difference. So, picture me at 18, he's 10 and a half, 11. So, um, there was not a lot of fighting going on. >> Was he just annoying at that age? >> Pretty much, but he's I mean, he's he's I'm as close to him as anybody. So, I love him and I'm super I'm I don't want to say like cuz this isn't a slight, but I am proud of him. I think he's done a great job. He's true to who he is. He's a great human being, great father. I think he's got an exceptional football mind and I think he does things the right way. >> When did that shift happen though? Like that is a huge gap and you're off at college and he's still in like middle school. Yeah, I would say that happened probably when I transitioned to college. And then you start he's getting a little bit older, he's getting more involved in in football and sports and I was playing college football and you come back, you watch them and it was really cool being there for his senior year being a GA at Central Michigan and that that was one of the reasons I wanted to go back to Central was I wanted to watch my brother play and that was a really cool time for us. >> Yeah. When you guys were in the same house though, was was he one of your biggest fans at that time? I mean, Bill called it annoying, but I mean, was he kind of one of your buddies and cheering hard for you? >> Yeah, I think so. I mean, he was at everything that I was playing in and that's why I get kind of pissed at my kids when they don't want to go watch their brother play. But there the age difference a little bit different, two years versus seven years. Um, but yeah, absolutely. He was he was at at all my sporting activities. Matt, presumably he's kind of like you, always wanting to grow up and be a head coach, right? And that's the track. When did you >> I don't know if I I ever wanted this. It kind of just happened. Um some days I wish I didn't have it, but uh it just it was one of those things. I think one thing that was instilled with from my parents is just be where your feet are and do the best job possible. So when I was a quarterback coach, I just wanted to be the best quarterback coach I could be. And then you get other opportunities. You get around great people. You know, being around the, you know, Gary Kubak, the Shanahan's, uh, Shawn McVey, I mean, has afforded us a lot of opportunity. >> Yeah. I'm just wondering when you look at him and realize that he could do that, too. >> I think a couple years ago, I think, you know, is I was like, you better start getting prepared for this, man. And you know, it seems like anybody that goes through LA has an opportunity to be a head coach. So, um, Sean does a great job just and he he's he gives you so much insight. I think that was so valuable for both of us because he will lean on the people he's closest with and and you get some insight that you might not get in every situation. >> Atlanta was where you first worked together. Is that right? >> That is correct. Yeah, that was a rough year for him. >> Was he your assistant or >> not? Not not per se. No, he was he was an offensive quality control. I think he was working with the receivers at that time. Um, but you know, he definitely hurt a lot for me. And then he had Kyle on top of that. So, it was just it's always it starts at the top. Kyle Kyle's hard on everybody. But I think that's why he has been so successful is he demands a lot out of you. Um and you know you're you're always trying to please him and get get his approval and um but it was always a compounding effect cuz if Mike screwed something up he'd get mad at me and then I'd go get mad at Mike and then he'd get mad at Mike and u but I think there was a lot of great lessons along the way. >> Thank you guys. >> Thanks guys.

title: Cowboys Players on Final Push for Roster Spots | Player Interviews
text: It's been good. Uh I feel like I've gotten better every single day. Um I feel like I'm in a good place with offense and um it's been good to get a bunch of reps and uh feel like I'm in a good place with the system and I feel like I put together a good camp and we got one more opportunity on Friday. Um so it'll be fun to get out there and play it play with the guys with Joe Milton. How have you been? >> It's been fun. I feel like we've made each other better. I think that's the main thing is we've we've been trying to push each other. Um and you know Drew's Dro is a great guy. He's a great player. Um I have a ton of respect for him. and we've been trying to make each other better this whole camp and I feel like we've done that. >> Sam, going into this preseason finale, what's something that you feel like you still need to kind of check off in your task list to kind of complete this training camp? >> I wouldn't say there's one specific thing. I think it's just going out there and putting putting together a good performance. Um, and you know, I feel like I put together a good camp and uh I feel like I'm playing some good ball. Just got to go out there on Friday, one more opportunity and you know, put my best foot forward. Is there anything that you, you know, I know there was a lot of skirmishes in the joint practice against the Saints, but is there anything that you take away from that joint practice productive wise, you know, that you can transfer to using against them in this game? >> We'll see. Um, honestly, we, you know, we've been focusing on, you know, our training camp here against against each other. We haven't really started looking at the Saints yet. We'll we'll start on that tomorrow. Um, but yeah, I'm sure we'll look at the practice and see what we did and see if there's some things we could use for the game. Um, but preseason, you never know what you're going to get. You know, teams are usually more simple and they try to do things that they don't usually do in the season. So, we'll see how it goes, but we'll definitely have some type of plan for sure. >> First training camp with the Cowboys up to this point, up to yesterday, actually. It was out in Oxnard in Southern California. Let's talk about, you know, practicing here for the first couple times in in the Ford Center in Dallas in front of these Cowboys fans. >> It's been awesome. Um, you know, you can tell it's different here with the Cowboys and, you know, whenever the gates open, I I peaked my head in here and the stadium was full. Um, so they take it serious down here and it's a fun thing to be a part of. >> [screaming] >> Thanks, sir. Good. Cool. Thank you, guys. >> Your development this off seasonason, I know it's been a little bit of a challenge, but it's been a challenge that you welcomed as far as outside linebacker, inside linebacker, showing that versatility. >> Yeah, it's been it's been a lot of fun really. Um, it's definitely been a challenge learning something new and just trying to keep up with the guys, but they've helped me so much. That room, I can't thank them enough. our coaches, uh, Coach Ch just on the amount of time that they helped me, uh, in this process and have poured into me. So, I'm so grateful for that. >> You know, and what's the challenge? I mean, now we're going into year three, >> third defensive coordinator, you know, how has that helped with your ability to adapt more quickly to be able to make an impact? >> Yeah. Um I think it's just accepting the fact that you can't control a lot of things in this in life in general and especially in this profession. And so just taking that mindset and all trials that I I receive taking it as joy and going at it at that mindset um and just using every day to get better. just being grateful to be here uh every single day coming in working hard and um really having a service mindset to to come like make this team better. Um fill in wherever I'm needed, help out where I can and uh ultimately make myself better as well. >> What is Bond taught Tom? He I know he's a player, but he seemed like he's been tutoring a lot of guys. You talk about what he brought to the room, teaching a guy. I mean, a guy like that, he's like another coach in the room. So, it's such a blessing to to have him. And he's really just since the first day he came, he's just been pouring into us and helping us and pretty much just giving us his insight on every single thing that he can in the meeting room. He's non-stop talking and helping us out. Obviously, on the field, um before practice, getting ready to practice and working on different things. So, he's been super helpful to us. >> What about being an inside linebacker? has have you taken over to the outside linebacker alone to excel there. What about learning the outside linebacker role has helped you become a better inside line? >> Yeah, I mean um I think for helping me to become a better inside linebacker is just block destruction. I'm on the edge all the time. I'm dealing with a lot heavier bodies every single play. Um getting hands-on and so that's helped me to work on my striking, block destruction and and things like that. title: Udinski and Lawrence Share Takeaways on Final Day of Training Camp | Jacksonville Jaguars
text: All right, what's up, guys? How are you guys doing? Appreciate you guys showing up today. I thought for sure there'd be nobody here. I'd be able to walk up, check the camera, and leave. But, you know I could count on you guys. >> Yeah. >> He did mention you first. >> Appreciate that. >> How you good to you, Rock? >> Yeah, sorry. Struggling. Struggling. New new technology here. >> All right, I like it. >> All good. >> Yeah. Now that you've been able to kind of see the same five kind of mesh together along the line over the last couple weeks, just I mean, how happy are you guys with their progression and just their comfort, you know, around one another? >> I think the progress is certainly exciting. I don't know that that progress is ever done because it's going to be probably a couple different iterations between now and the beginning of the season or even beginning of season to the end of the season. So, you're never satisfied, you're never necessarily content with it, but it's really enjoyable to see those guys progress in their communication and chemistry working together, whether it's in the protection game, picking up twist games, or whether it's in the run game identifying different fronts. So, really excited about the future and outlook of that group. >> When you're calling plays in the preseason finale, are you calling specific plays to get a specific look at one guy or two guys on a specific play just to fill out the mind on what what whether he's going to make the roster or not? >> Yeah, that that's a great question. There are instances where you are certainly calling a specific play for a certain guy cuz you want to give him an opportunity to go make a play or run a certain route or an offensive lineman make a certain block. And then there are other plays where you want to see three guys work together and say, "Can these three guys work cohesively together to execute a concept or a release pattern as receivers or certain block combination by the offensive line?" So, sometimes it's one guy, sometimes it's three guys, and then sometimes it's the whole offense, can they execute a certain concept? So, that there's kind of a little bit of a science to it sometimes where you're calling plays where you might not always call in a real game because you're trying to get things evaluated, but we know that's the purpose of preseason, hopefully set us up for success when the games are counting in the regular season. >> How tough is this week kind of narrowing it down to 53 when you've got so many guys out here putting in it every day? >> Ooh, I probably don't have words to describe how tough it is. It's honestly, it might be the worst part. There aren't very many bad parts about coaching and especially being here at the Jaguars, an organization like this, but it probably is the worst part having to see guys who work so hard in the off season, guys who you care so deeply about, who have invested so much in the team and everything they put out there on the field and see them leave is, you know, probably the toughest part in coaching. So, it's extremely difficult. Like I said, I don't have words that do it justice cuz you appreciate all the work that these guys put in. >> Liam said yesterday he's happy with the progress of the running game. I'm sure you guys had an idea of how C-Rod and Etienne were kind of complimenting each other, but just seeing that kind of come to life over the last month, what's that been like? It was certainly long awaited with the spring. We didn't get to see those guys working together. So, to actually see them in live action, really between this joint practice and the Carolina joint practice, kind of see both those guys hit their stride with some of the different run concepts we've been trying to hit and some of the different reads we've been developing and really see those guys be able to go out and play fast, finally hit their groove and not have to go out there and think about and who am I reading, what am I looking at, and just go out there and play and play free. So, that's been the most exciting part about seeing those guys reach that level progression. Like I said with the offensive line, that progression's never done, but it's nice to kind of hit that threshold and see the glimpses of their hard work, their studying in the meeting rooms, their work in the indoor and the walk-through rooms see that materialize. How would you describe Trevor's off season? Could you do it in like one or two words? >> One or two words? Oh, man. I don't know if I can do one or two words, D-Rock. That That's a tough one. Um I don't even I don't even know if I could do 10 words to be honest with you. That That's a really tough one. I would say that that if I had to pick one one or two, of progress would probably be in there, process, consistency. So, you know, one of those three would probably be among the two cuz I probably have said it a thousand times you guys are probably sick of hearing it how we know that progress is not a straight line, but the consistency to show up day after day after day and build on what we had last year, but not take any of those details and fundamentals and foundational steps for granted and continue to work over and over and over got the at those things whether it's a drop in technique and fundamentals or whether it's a read or whether it's just calling a certain play or a certain motion. All of those things are so important. They're critical for the success not only the quarterback, but all 11 on the offense and he's a guy that has continued to work at all aspects of that which is once again why he's such a joy to coach. >> Seems like Amir Abdullah just, you know, showed up consistently throughout camp. What's it been like just being around him and what he's brought to the room with all his experience? >> Amir's been awesome to be around. I have was fortunate enough to be around him briefly in Carolina and it's it's like time has stood still. I mean, he hasn't changed at all. He works so hard at it. He's one of the first guys in the building taking care of his body, doing all the extra work, rolling around doing flips on the physioball, all sorts of stuff. I can't even describe it. I don't even know what he's doing in there. You'd have to ask him what some of those moves are called, but he's such a pro about it. His approach from the off-field stuff taking care of his body and that carries over to the same way he prepares in the classroom, in the meeting room, film study, all that stuff. So, I think he's a great guy not only for the offense and what he adds as a player, but he's a great guy for the young backs, the young receivers, the young offensive lineman to be around and see a guy that's had sustained success for so long in this league and what that actually looks like. >> I know we've spoken a lot about how impressive C.J. Williams has been, but what's been like the biggest progression that you've seen from when he came in the door in rookie mini camp to now? >> That's a good question. I don't know that there's one thing that necessarily jumps out because when you're in it day after day, it kind of just builds slowly over time. I think that there's a different confidence when you go out there and you have a mastery of the system and you can go out there and snap the huddle and you're not thinking about the play, you're not thinking about which way do I line up, that he's inched closer and closer to do. Now, he's been challenged to play multiple positions, as really all the wide receivers has, but he's really excelled at understanding his role and what he can add value to the offense. And I think as he grew into the comfortability with how we're talking about defenses, how we're talking about routes, and understood the language terminology, the way that receivers are communicating out there, that's really what's accelerated the growth and highlighted some of the plays that he's made, whether it's the pass game the run game, you see phenomenal blocks out there as well. >> You mentioned the idea of whether players like playing free. Is there I'm sure it's different for every player, but is there usually like a typical path to that, like mastering the system or just being present? >> Yeah, there's so much that goes into it, and I think it starts with that mastery of the system and preparation process, and you know, we have a bunch of different analogies that we talk about, whether it's whenever you first do anything, you're thinking about all the steps and processes that go into it. And then once you've really got it down, whether it's driving a car or whether it's riding a bike, whatever analogy you want to use, you really don't think about all the steps that go into it. And we're trying to achieve that level of mastery, that level of playing free. We know it's never going to be automatic out there cuz the football, you know, the game is gray, where there's going to be decisions made, there's going to be different looks, there's going to be different timing, but we want to try to limit as much thinking as possible and really just let them process and play. So, I think it starts with the the the mastery of the system, knowing what you're doing, and over time with the experience of seeing all the different looks, you see quarterbacks especially, guys who are playing well late in their career, it's hard to show them a defense or a different look that they haven't seen before, and it just accelerates their processing by that much because they have the ability to recall what they've seen, they recognize a pattern, and they make a quick decision. That's a quarterback, but it's the same thing for running back, wide receiver, tight end. >> Speaking of not getting a lot of looks, like quarterback rushing and scrambling is obviously a big thing over the course of the second half of last season. You want to rely on Trevor especially in like the red zone area and stuff like that. But you can't really simulate a lot of reps. Is there like stuff you can do behind the scenes to like improve Trevor as a rusher? >> That's an excellent question because it is extremely challenging. So you probably notice when we get plays that break down and we have the opportunity to work a scramble in a team setting or even a seven-on-seven setting that we were in here where there's no pass rush, we're still going to try to make that as much of a game rep as possible. You can't fully replicate it cuz there's no opportunity to get hit. There's nobody chasing you and those. But we want to try to take those opportunities to practice those reps at full speed because we'll go out there and we'll put together drills and try to build it into drills or team periods. But it's a different it's really a different process when you know the scramble is coming versus when you have to instantaneously respond and you're not thinking it and you're not expecting it. So it's one of those things that is extremely hard to practice knowing that the quarterback's not getting hit out here. >> We saw Dana go off the field during a special teams rep and then kind of walked it off. Does he seem okay or >> I'll let I'll let Liam handle those things, yeah. I'm sure he'll update you next time he talks to you. >> Anybody else? >> Perfect. Thanks. >> Thanks, guys. >> What's the feeling you guys get when it's you know it's the last day of camp you don't have to be out here anymore? >> Um is it today? Is today the last day of camp? I guess is that what it is? Honestly, I feel like we Yeah, I Uh it's I always feel like there's always something around the corner to stay ready for cuz uh you know next week is kind of an in-between week as well and we still got some prep this week to finish up. So but I mean just in general that feeling of the season being so close and obviously in camp when you start off it's just you know you have so much camp ahead of you and so much time to work on different things and it can be kind of a grind. But then now when you get to this point you're like, "Man, we got I mean 2 weeks less than 2 weeks before we're pre- preparing to play Cleveland. But I mean we play in basically 2 weeks. So now that sounds crazy thinking about it and just realizing how close it is, how far we've come, but still how much work we have to do to get ready for week one and we're on track, but we just got to keep we got to keep plugging away every day. Can't relax, but physically obviously I think coach does a really good job of transitioning and and shifting to where guys can kind of get their bodies back a little bit. >> Will you be diving into Cleveland tape immediately? >> Okay. >> Yeah, we'll we'll start that. You know, maybe not today, but but as you this this next week and a half goes, we'll start that more and more. I'm sure next week's practice will definitely be more geared towards those looks and trying to get some preparation started on Cleveland and you don't have the whole game plan in by any means, but you just start getting familiar with the defense you're playing and and what's your what's you're going to get coming into week one so you can be a little bit ahead. >> We have mentioned to Tommy time again that last season was about finding your edge, this [clears throat] offseason is about attacking the edge. With training camp wrapped up from an offensive standpoint strictly, what would you say is the edge of this offensive unit? >> You know, I think that we're when we play with an edge up front and the physicality that I know we're capable of, we're really really good and those and those guys that unit up front has done an awesome job of responding every day. It's not always going to be perfect, but just the physicality that we've played with the last two weeks, moving people in the run game, protecting and then obviously we have playmakers outside that can go and and make plays and I can get it to them, but it's all starts up front. I think those guys have done a good job of owning that and we got to continue to buy into that cuz that's that's really what it's about. Really on both sides of the ball, but you know, especially on offense up front those guys just having that edge and they've done a great job of it. We just got to keep keep working it. I think we found out what we need to get better at also through training camp and some of the some of the details, the attention to detail, you know, whether it's formations, motions, different checks, just being ready for everything. Our whole operation just needs to continue to sharpen and refine and and move quicker. And I'm a big part of that and and guys knowing what to do all that is. And we got better, but that's just something that I still think we need to work on. So, that's another thing is you find out what you need to get better at. And I think we know that and and can continue to attack it and work on it. >> Assess your last few weeks personally. Did you get out of camp what you wanted to? >> Sorry, what you say? >> Yeah, I I feel like individually definitely got got better every day. I feel like I found a little bit of a groove the last week or so. Like I said, every day wasn't my best and it can be frustrating cuz you want the result, but it's taking a step back and using it That's what we talk about in our room all the time is the practice is only as good as what you learn from it, whether it's good or bad. So, I think that's something that we focused on this year and it's like, "Hey, there's some There's handful of bad plays out there that I need to learn from and get better from, but as long as I do that and move forward, we're going to be fine and I know I'm going to make make a bunch of plays, too. So, I think just continuing to be detailed, you know, I think taking completions, all those things that I want to work on. I think I did a better job of it over the last week or so, creating off schedule, and being smart with the football. All those things are are things that I do well, but I also need to work on. So, that was a big point of emphasis that I think I got better at. >> Yeah, and where are you in terms of building on what you created last year culture-wise, but then also having to start over at the same time, knowing that 40% of the team is going to turn over. Is it You have any thoughts about that? >> Yeah, I mean, you mean turn over just from now this over this next week with losing a bunch of guys, you're saying, or or just from last season? >> the culture that you built and that you want to sustain, right? I mean, that's that's, you know, the accountability that you have for each other. Do you have to start over every year, or can you build on it? >> I I start over in the sense of you got to earn it every year with the new your new team, your new group of guys. Obviously, there's a lot of carryover, but I think the whole idea of, you know, working your tail off out here and earning the right to be successful and to win and to make plays. Um that's a real thing and you got to feel that as a team and and if you don't feel that, there is some doubt that can creep in. It's like, hey, you know, are we ready? And um I know we're not going to be asking ourselves that come week one, you know, it's just we've put the time and we put the work and we got to continue to do that and we need to get better. But as far as finding the edge, you know, being that tough team, getting better and better fundamentally um and technique-wise, I mean, that's all the those things are what we've preached and talked about and guys have worked super hard at. So, you do have to start over from that sense of actually doing it in training camp. Um but you also hope there's an expectation and a culture that when you walk into this building, you see that with the guys that have been here and the way we practice and play, there should be a standard that you feel and it's easier to hop in the line. Yeah, no doubt. >> What's the favorite thing about Liam's offense? You've had a little bit over a year to be in it. >> Um I think just the way we marry, you know, I've said before the whole the can system and and being able to run what we want when we want to and to the right look. I think that's obviously a huge part of having a successful offense, but also marrying the run, the pass, the play action, all that stuff, the screens, the movements, all that stuff looking the same and when you get to you run all all against our defense and they they see it every day. So, you don't always get the same response as when you run it against a new defense that comes in and some of these plays work a little bit better because you run it against a team that hasn't seen it yet. So, all the stuff we've been doing in training camp, it's cool to see, you know, some of that come to life against Tampa and against Carolina because they haven't been practicing against us every day and they're not ready for some of the wrinkles that we add. So, um I think that's the cool part and it it it reminds you why you you have all the little similarities, why there's all these motions and shifts and why we're teaching in a certain way and it's just a good reminder for guys like hey, if this all can look the same, if we can be detailed, you know, it's going to create a lot of opportunities for us. >> You know, if there was a change at center that would affect you, no question about it. Asking who the man would be, but with all the changes on the offensive line, how much of that does that have on you as far as maybe their nuances or if you know they're going to do this, but they're not going to do that? What's that like? >> I mean, there there's obviously a little bit of an adjustment, especially at center when you you get snaps a little bit differently. Um and Jonah's done a great job and I've gotten a ton of reps with him, so I also feel really comfortable if he has to come in and um I know, you know, he's a great player. I know he's ready and we've communicated a lot, so there's not a ton there. Um I'd say just with all the guys over communicating when new guys come in at the line of scrimmage and you know, they might not be used to the same, I guess, checks or the timing of everything. So, just making sure that I'm over communicating that everybody's on the same page is something to emphasize when you're shuffling guys around up front. And I think it's great practice for us cuz we've all talked about the O line deal and um the real possibility of that having happened at some point where you plug in another guy. So, I think having all those guys ready at different positions is really valuable. >> What's the set of growing pains for Craig Noll? Just your thoughts on, you know, he's been there now for about a week over at left guard. >> I think he's done an awesome job. He plays hard. He's I mean, he's huge, he's strong. Um you can tell he cares. Like he he he plays super hard. I mean, that's the one the first thing you notice. Um and then mentally it's it's not been too much for him. You know, obviously he's he is a rookie and there's still a lot to learn and there's looks every day that you can teach off of, but um he's not lost at all. He knows what he's doing. There's a lot of plays that we can clean up, but as far as knowing what he's doing and playing hard, he's got that down. I think he's protected well. He's been moving people in the run game. He's athletic. I mean, I he's done an awesome job. So, I think we got a bunch of guys up front that can play and play well and I love what I'm seeing from from E-man. >> What kind of camp has Tune had just from your perspective? >> He's been great. I think also the guy that's just gotten better every day. You know, as he's gotten more and more reps of all of our runs, different versus different looks, you see some of the ones he hit yesterday. He had some great runs and he's seeing it really well. I think yesterday was the the best he's seen as far as just running smooth, full speed, hitting it, trusting his track, all those things. I mean, he looked really, really good. I think as a pass catcher, getting better every day, done some really nice things. Um and just his whole attitude the entire camp has been a really good one. Just wanting to get better, talking to me after every rep, you know, wanting to know what happened on this play or that play and um just wanting to learn more. >> What can you do to improve against the rush here? >> It's obviously pretty tough to like fully simulate scrambles out here. So, is there anything you can do like behind the scenes to work on that aspect of your game or is it something where you really have to just rely on like in-game experience and natural instincts? >> Yeah, obviously that's it's not as uh it's it can be tougher in practice. I think we I just talked about this with, you know, with Liam and Grant of of trying to make the reps in practice a little bit more real. When I do scramble, I think it's easy in practice sometimes to get on the perimeter, take your time, you wait, wait, wait, then you throw up a ball that you probably shouldn't throw and maybe it gets picked or it's in traffic and just some bad habits, you know, I've had a couple of these of those this training camp of just being smart cuz those are really the only times you get to work it and and making those real reps where you get out of the get out of the pocket, even if it's seven-on-seven, get out of the pocket and let the receivers see me do that so they can get used to reacting and getting open cuz if you don't work it in practice and then week one, you want these guys to run around and get open off schedule and they're they haven't seen it all training camp, it's probably not going to happen. So, I need to do better job I do a better job of of doing it more for these guys so we can be ready to roll and um we've had some really good ones in the red zone though in team periods throughout all of training camp, but I think just taking every opportunity I can cuz our defense um you know, unfortunately for our offense, but fortunately for our defense, they covered a lot of stuff this camp where probably could have scrambled a little bit more instead of trying to squeeze one into the backside, you know, in or whatever. So, I I think that's something that definitely want to continue to work these next 2 weeks. >> How much growth did you and Brian have this offseason? I know you've talked about it a lot, but now that you're finally right at the finish line. >> A lot of growth. I think just the trust between us because we've communicated so much has been has just grown a lot. Certain routes I know exactly what he's going to do. He's a really He's just really consistent in in his approach and what he does. He He tells you something and how he's going to run a route, and then he goes and he does it like that, you know, it it's not It sounds simple, but not everyone's like that. I've played with a lot of guys that are really good receivers, but you say you're going to run it one way, then you get in in the game or the live period and the route looks completely different, and he's not one of those guys. I think he's really detailed, and he's really smart, and just building that trust to where it's gotten to the point now where I'm throwing I'm letting a lot of these throws go before he's even starting his cut. I'm trusting where he's going to be. He's getting to the spot. Obviously, you guys saw the deep one yesterday. That's always going to be a weapon of his, but I think the entire route tree and all of the cuts he's gotten so much better at, and we've gotten our timing and and still more work to do, but I love where we're at right now. >> Last one. >> How's the timing with Travis Kelce? You guys haven't really got a lot together. >> Yeah. Yeah, it's something that we're going to just continue to chip away at as we go. Um it's hard to get everything every day with him also, you know, playing defense, so it can be a challenge, but I think just continue to chip away when I can, you know, over this next week or two. Just talking to talking with him through some things, making sure he's good on just some overall things that we're doing on offense, making sure he feels comfortable. Um you know, it's time you don't get quite as much time, but um I I like you know, when the opportunity comes up, we're going to have him ready and um he's going to have to he's going to be able to do whatever we need him to do.
