text: Welcome into Jags A.M. It is the second day of joint practice between the Jaguars and the Buccaneers. I'm Kenani Steven. friend sex and John O with me. And guess what guys, we made it. It is the final training camp day. There's a walk through tomorrow and then obviously the final preseason game, but we made it through. We >> come to the end of the road. >> I did not have John singing Boys to Men on my bingo card today, but I'm ecstatic about it. >> In the 90s when uh Pete Prrisco and I worked together, every Friday when the work was done, he would close his laptop and sing that. So that's my that's my only I did not know it was Boys to Men. Uh, >> now you do. >> Boys to Men to me is one of those new groups. >> Oh, is it? Yes. Okay. Well, they've uh they've been doing pretty good for themselves for that little new group. They are. Um, today's show is in our outdoor Hyundai studios. Our final show out here. The guys are stretching, getting ready for the day. Uh, no, what are they? Half pads today. Looks like spiders. Yeah, shells and spiders. Okay, >> let's get into our big things brought to you by GEA, Government Employee Health Association. And big thing number one is win the day. They try to win the day every day, but if you talk to Baker Mayfield yesterday, he says he doesn't know if his team would have won the day. >> It's tough. Uh I thought, you know, they gave us some good looks. They were playing with their hair on fire. So that um we definitely if this was a full game, I don't think we would have came out on the the winning side of it. Um so just little eye opening. Got to get back and watch the tape. you know, it's never as good or as bad as you think it is, but um I think from from my standpoint, it they out physical us, and that's that's never what you want to have. So, um didn't doesn't matter who we have out there. You don't you want guys that are going to do their very best to be the more physical team and and want it more. And I don't I don't know if we did that today. >> So, a little subjective who wins a day, but um I would say the Jaguars were definitely physical and got what they wanted to get across yesterday. >> But Josh Hines Allen, they had a Chase Young kind of day. If you go back to the New Orleans practice where Chase Young was all over the back field, Josh Hines Allen was I mean, he was John, I thought he looked sensational. Trayvon Walker did as well. Uh listen, the home team, the team that's hosting the practice should they didn't travel. They're not staying in a hotel. They know all the surroundings. They should have the upper hand. And I I thought for a lot of practice yesterday, it looked like they were ready to go. And what you just said, watching a lot of these practices over the years, that's usually how usually it plays out. For a game, it's a little different because players are ratcheted up for a road game. For practice, remember, uh, the Jaguars in New Orleans did not start that practice great. It makes sense. Um, look, they've had two joint practices since that Saints practice, and both of them, I don't know who wins a practice, but both of them there were swats of the practice where you went, that's a pretty good team. Uh, and doing a lot of good things that you like. Uh, I'm standing on defense yesterday. I'm standing by defensive field yesterday and you see them breaking off long runs on the offense, meaning Bashel, Tuton, and Rodriguez. you see all these good things. Um they're a good team and they've practiced well the last a couple times they played they have played other good teams to to to beat the team to death they responded right I mean that that was what they wanted after that day in New Orleans where it didn't look so good for this football team and and every day since when they've had the opportunity they've responded. Let's go to our second big thing today, which is last call because as we mentioned, this is the final training camp day. And for the starters who aren't going to play probably in that final preseason game, this is their last padded work for a while against someone that's not on their own team. John, how is important is it I mean, I know it's padded mostly yesterday. It's half padded today, but to get that quality work in when you're not going to face anybody for a while September 13th, >> no. in talking to players and Liam Cohen yesterday, there was definitely a feeling of of uh wrapping up and trying to get an assessment of what's going on. Um I think it's been a good camp. You know, it it's uh I don't know that it's been perfect from start to finish, but with a good team, what you want is what we've seen. Uh some hiccups early. Uh Liam's never going to be happy with everything in a practice. Uh, but over the last they felt coming out of New Orleans, Brian, like they needed to step it up a little bit. They did. >> It's okay to have moments like that in a camp. You're not going to be good. >> It's It's good to have moments that you respond to and and I think in the last I know what is that nine or 10 days. >> It's felt like a team I wrote it yesterday. It's felt like a team that knows the regular season is coming and is improving thusly. >> Well, we've conditioned them to be strategic with it, right? to be able to learn from the mistakes and get better. It's hard not to dial it back a little bit when you know that you're trying to preserve and and all that all of that stuff. Mentally, you're going to take a little step back. Today's practice is more about speed and technique. They're not going to hit too much. They're going to make sure that they are focused on, you know, when you get a Baker Mayfield and you're you're at the top of your rush, are you finishing right? When you've got Travis Hunter lined up against the best receiver on the other side, how's his footwork? Today is about using the opportunity against another team to improve your technique and to play as fast as you can. >> Absolutely. And our final big thing today is going to be decisions, decisions. We won't be back with you guys until Monday. And before that, Sunday, I think at 6:30, they're going to make their final cuts. They're going to get this roster down to 53. I don't know how difficult or or vexing that will be. They have the practice squad, so there's a lot of guys they're going to try to keep Brian at the end of that, but I think maybe that's where they might lose some guys. Hoping they can maybe sneak them on the practice squad to develop where someone might come grab them. >> You know, every year we talk about John about the roster and the management of it. And we've never really around Jackson, we've never had to worry too much about not keeping some of the guys we want. this year. They're honestly going to have some really difficult decisions. I'm going to talk about mine coming up a little bit later, so I don't want to give too much of it away, but the they have some they have some interesting situations, right? How many offensive linemen do you keep? If if if Cole Vanland is not ready to start, you're probably going to keep 10. And where does that short you? How many tight ends do they want to keep if they want to play as much, you know, 12 and 13 personnel? What are you going to do at corner? How many edge rushers? There's some numbers that are going to dictate what they do on the practice squad. The practice squad's where all the drama is. I think this roster is all but said. >> Yeah, it's uh the other Brian Thomas Jr. is making their thoughts difficult. Uh can they get Jamari Taylor, who I I expect to be a practice squad guy. Can they get all these guys through? They're going to be holding their breath a lot. And uh you know, I don't know how many guys we're talking about them losing that if they lose them, it will be an oh no, it's going to affect us this year, but there's probably three or four guys that they feel like, boy, we'd like to have this guy around because we feel like he's going to develop. You get the feeling that they're going to lose a guy that in two or three years they're going to look at another team and go, "Yeah, we were right on that guy." >> Absolutely. It's pretty cool to see what he thinks and then you got Reggie as well. So, having those two kind of a little cheat code there. >> What do you think it is that makes him special as a route runner after watching so much tape of him? >> Yeah, he's he's really twitchy like first like he's like 6'2" but he he's really twitchy kind of like a a smaller guy and he kind of uses his body and his angles in different way and he has a good change of pace on a lot of that stuff as well. So, um, I've I've been looking at Keenan since I was in high school. So, I used to look at him and Davante Adams a lot and and they had they have they don't like move exactly the same but they have a lot of different change of pace and um, movements that are kind of similar. >> Josh, so even though there is some overlap with some of the skill set when it comes to you and Keenan especially on third down talked about this a little bit last week but like why do you think it can still work even though there is some overlap? >> No, I mean I it's I mean it's I wouldn't say like overlap but I feel like we both work on third down but it's a good thing. I feel like, you know, teams can't like bracket one of the other. They got to just respect both which will give one-on-ones to everybody across the board and then you also got Tyler and you got Alex still and then whoever else is in there. So, I feel like it only helps, um, at the end of the day and and it'll be smooth. >> You mentioned Davante and Keenan. How much as you a receiver how much you appreciate guys who win because they're technicians? They're not just like the Uber app which states know the ins and outs of >> Yeah, no. Those guys get a lot of respect. I feel like just being able to really get open and not just like obviously credit to the guys who are just like super athletic, super fast, and stuff like that. But not everybody has that. So, studying guys that truly just get open are able to use leverage and use different shifts and techniques and change of pace to get open. Those are the guys that you truly like say like oh, that's a route runner. So. >> Josh, at the start of camp you said you're throwing to Daniel back in the summer you didn't feel like for my soft knees hurt. >> Um now you've seen it like in camp and in that camp setting, um what impresses you even more about just the way that he's come back from everything? >> Yeah, I think Daniel looks great. I mean, I feel like he's he's done everything right this camp and he's he's looked fantastic and he hasn't lost a step from last year. So, I'm excited to see him going into week one soon, but I feel like he's putting in a great body of work this whole off season. I feel like it just leads up to this Baltimore game coming week one. >> Back when when he got hurt pretty quickly we were being told like yeah, he's going to be back next year. >> Mhm. >> And I wonder if from your perspective when you know Daniel, you believe in Daniel, but like could were you at that point fully expecting that or was it something that you kind of needed to like see happen? >> Oh yeah, I mean, in a way of course it's a it's a Achilles injury. But when when Jason Tatum came back kind of pretty quick, I had like asked Daniel about it. I was like yeah, I was like Tatum came back. He's like well, I can probably come back quicker cuz he's like I guess he said it's a little different with basketball and football. So, I knew he was doing everything he was supposed to do. And then when I saw him in the spring taking reps I caught I already knew that he was going to be ready for camp because I was I was surprised he was even taking reps that early. So, I pretty much knew then. >> So, when you got back for OTAs and saw him that you were like >> Oh yeah, I knew he was going yeah. Yeah, I knew he was like he's He's be ready for sure. >> Josh, with with last year being of it was, and then you lose Fitz, you lose you trade Fitz and acquire a guy, so there was going to be more to go around. And now you bring in Keenum, who's a volume guy. Are you curious how everybody gets their share? >> Nah, you know, coach going to handle um handle it how he wants to handle it, so that's his that's his responsibility. >> I know you and um Reggie and Chad talked going in the off-season and working more with you on the outside and >> uh you know, outside of the slot. How did that go throughout camp? What did you gain from doing that a little bit more often? And do you feel like it's something you guys can utilize a little bit more? >> Uh you know, just uh goes into the moving around conversation playing in two wide receiver sets more and stuff like that. I feel like uh we've done that, but obviously just game plan week to week keep going and um go from there, obviously, so up to them and I'm going to do my best to make the plays that come my way.

title: Colts Cover-2 Podcast: After Falcons preseason game, who's under most pressure in preseason finale
text: Hey there Colts fans. This is Nathan Brown, your Colts insider with the Indianapolis Star. I'm here with Joel Ericson for another edition of the Colts Cover Two podcast. We've got a lot to dive into tonight. We're taping this on Tuesday evening. We just got um through our first of three days at the Colts facility heading into the preseason finale. On Saturday afternoon, the Colts will host the Detroit Lions. Um, we learned today a lot of um who will and who won't get action in the preseason game here on Saturday. Um, got two more practices to watch before the Colts go through. Roster cut downs from 90 players that they have at the moment all the way down to the initial 53man roster. Um, we've got uh a lot to look at over the past week. Um, we got to see a pair of joint practices between the Colts and the Falcons and then of course that preseason game. um that we saw on Saturday. Uh Colts lose fairly handily 34 to6. Really struggle moving the ball, generating a whole lot of offense um between two halves again split by Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard. We'll get to that. Um we'll get to what they have on the line, where we think that quarterback battle is heading, and more. Uh but first Joel, um looking back at those joint practices that we had, um you were at the one in New England where the Colts um visited the Patriots for a day. This time we get to see the Colts unfilled for two days with the Falcons. What was your biggest takeaway or two from watching those um pair of uh of joint practices with the Falcons? Uh, I mean I I the funny thing after seeing the game is it I don't know if people believe you when you say this, but like it felt like both facets of the ball that I saw the Colts fairly fairly dominated. You know, offensively the Falcons did score some touchdowns in the session I saw, but that was because they have Drake London and because they were starting in the red zone. It's not like they were driving the length of the field. I think though, I just saw this, we're taping this uh Tuesday night. I did just see kind of across my my social media feeds that there's a report out there that the Falcons aren't going to name to a tongue of Aloa the starter. Um largely just because they they feel like they can't. Um, and that >> one of the first one of the first quarterbacks in uh I have to think recent memory to be the only quarterback active on the field competing for a starting spot and uh not win the job. >> Yeah, they um very odd. So So that played a role for sure. Um I think a lot of it was stuff that we knew already. Um at least I think it's stuff I knew already. [snorts] Um, uh, the one really surprising thing was that the the day I watched the offense practice, uh, Daniel Jones moved the ball very easily. Uh, spectacularly easily and and really I I think I had him at 15. I don't have it right in front of me, but it's like 15 or 16. >> I think it was 15 for 15. I think it was a a perfect day. >> It was, you know, you're right. It was 15 for 15. The only miss that I had in the book was nullified by a pass interference penalty. So, I wouldn't count that because it directly impacted whether or not the pass was complete. and that was surprising just because I don't think Jesse Bates may may have been out there, but like Falcon Falcons have some talent in the secondary. That's that's one of their calling cards is that they've got some talent in the secondary. They don't really have talent on the edge rush, but they they have some some talent there. So, that was a little surprising. Just it's just odd and kind of hard to explain that the starters really took it to them, I thought, from what I saw. Um, and I think you saw a better defensive day than I did. Uh, and then once you get the backups out there, it looked terrible. >> Yeah. Um, I mean, again, we have to reiterate, we're watching the Colts backups um on on on Saturday at least. We're watching largely the Colts backups um against the Falcons backups units that um I mean you kind of grow go across the board. The a lot so many of these players um even guys who are playing in the the first half when you're kind of when you have your second string out there largely most of those guys are rarely going to see the field in the regular season. Um and then the guys playing in second half um a large chunk might not even make the roster. So, it's when when you're watching this, it's certainly not something where you are um making a a judgment on what the actual team is going to look like, but I do think you start to get a sense of where there are some depth issues. And if you've been following along with our podcast over the last several weeks, um I think you know pretty well where those issues lie. It's at quarterback. Um, another really rough half of play from Mai Blackman in particular, who we um went into training camp feeling like was the solid, really without a doubt um quarterback number five for the Colts, who then would rise up to number four for week one as Cam Taylor Britt serves his oneame suspension. Um, and even higher if you have any injuries above him. Um, luckily Mooney Ward back at practice today for the Colts did individual drills. Um so he's moving in the right direction and barring any sort of setback, he seems like he should be fine for the uh season opener here in in two and a half weeks. Um uh rough game from him. Um didn't get as much pressure as we saw the starters get um in both of those joint practices. I think you and I both saw some hints of that. um didn't see a whole lot of pressure uh that the second and third units were able to get on the Falcons quarterbacks. Um trying to think through I mean generally speaking the offense did not look great. I think a lot of a lot of that even though um we've heard coaches kind of push back against this. Um I I guess I don't really know what to make of this, but um I think visually I I imagine you would agree with me that the offensive line play um left a good amount to be desired and that left Riley Leonard and and Anthony Richardson under a good amount of pressure for good portions of that game and that contributed to a lot of the three and outs and just the the lack of movement down the field on some of those drives that then led to two field goals and nothing more. Um, again, these are places where if you are fully healthy, I think that both of those units, um, you have to be really confident with where the Colts stand, offensive line and and quarterback. But really, I think that what what you see in the preseason is places where if you start to see some injuries and you know you're going to see them at some point, this was something that Chris Ballard hit on a ton back in January when he had his season ending press conference, feeling like injuries weren't uh an excuse for how last season ended. But what was to blame and something that he took ownership of was the team's lack of depth in some pretty key areas so that when they did get injured, they weren't able to bounce back. And and I think that's where some of the worry lies as we head um ever closer to the the start of the season is that um generally speaking, the Colts are pretty healthy right now. Although we had um some surprises some surprises from guys missing practice today. We can um go over that here in a little bit. Um, but generally speaking, when you look at some other teams in the league, the Colts are really pretty healthy. Um, so you just hope that, um, they stay that way because if there are some key injuries in in certain spots, I think this team that we feel like could be, you know, could and should be right back in the thick of competing for a playoff spot, um, could start to spiral spiral really quickly if we, uh, if we see some guys end up on the sidelines. Yeah, I uh I I think it's it's an odd combination of some places where you could kind of see it coming and then some other places where um the Colts have have maybe had uh some issues uh that that were unforeseen. Like for instance, um cornerback, you know, they add Cam Taylor Britt. I think that was reasonable for what they had. They already have Mooney Ward and Sauce Garden to play the outside. They really like Justin Wall-E. I think everything I've seen suggests that Justin Wall-E is is the right play there uh in camp. So that that makes sense. But then you from a depth perspective like they had reason to believe that Mai Blackman um like I I I went back and looked at this the other day just to see if I was maybe misremembering some things and I was misremembering some things just like how effective he was last year. Um and this isn't like a a great number by any means but like it's a it's a solid number in today's NFL. He he played 783 snaps. the the NFL's NextGen stats has him as an 88.8 rating uh when quarterbacks threw in his direction. Now, there's there's a caveat there. Um I know for a fact that would be higher because I remember from last year that uh his big mistake falling down against the Rams and giving up the game-winning touchdown pass that get that goes on Cam Binham stats because he's the closest defender. um which kind of shows the um pitfalls of those stats sometimes. Um >> yeah, if you get if you get beat so badly um it doesn't go on your record, which is a weird caveat in there, >> right? So, you have to go with that a little bit. But but generally, I think he was not great, but at least >> serviceable. At least at least he you know for what he was going to be which was a fifth corner is what we thought and um for that like I think you feel pretty good with with the experience level and the experience of defense and really through the first couple weeks of camp it felt pretty good honestly and it's just it's just this last two weeks in the joint practices with both the Falcons and the Patriots and then the preseason game. It's been abysmal. There's just there's no other way around it. He's been terrible. He's got four um he's got four pass interferences. The one was declined, but he's been flagged four times for pass interference. He's given up six or seven catches. I'm not sure the exact number. They don't have NextGen stats for preseason games, but I had him at like seven. And then we asked Luan Rumo about it and he said like you know this is a big week for them and kind of hinting at roster spots and so like with him and Jonathan Edwards and that's a spot that like I feel like it makes sense that you felt like you had depth there. It just is not working out that way. linebacker is another one where their best laid plans have kind of gone to heck because CJ Allen was supposed to be the middle linebacker and instead of being the middle linebacker, he's going to be in a rotation early because of injury and not being able to to get enough time on the field in training camp to convince coaches he's ready. >> Yeah. Um, you you actually wrote a a really good story on on CJ specifically um that published uh this afternoon, this evening on indiestar.com taking a look at kind of why CJ finds himself in the position that he's in. Um it was interesting going back and reading some of those quotes um from the the Colts draft night. The Colts of course draft him in the uh toward the back of the second round pick number 53. They traded back um and got a guy that when you look at the quotes um and even if you know when you talk to people kind of behind the scenes a little bit they were really excited about who he who he was. He came with great pedigree from Georgia. Um he'd started I think three and a half seasons there. Got some starting time even as a freshman. um or the green dot for them. So, he was kind of that captain of that defense. Um you know, a very strong unit across the board that played in, you know, SEC football eight or nine weekends out of the year. Um not, you know, not the the caliber of maybe that top echelon of linebackers that you could have drafted a little bit earlier in the second round or late in the first round. Um but really kind of you know in that that second tier of guys I think someone that they um more than anything were were really excited about his instincts and his smarts and his vision and his way that he saw the game and way he learned things very quickly. Um and and that's why you you know when you look back at those quotes um let's see what would that be about four months or so ago um you see them talking about um a guy that they felt like was going to be an automatic kind of really without question green dot guy in you know as a rookie in year one in the NFL. And we've seen, of course, he's missed time. Um, first was just a a I think a couple days of practice with um an injury that he suffered the week leading up to training camp and then missed a lot more with a uh hamstring, I believe, if if I'm remembering. I don't have the exact number of days, but I mean, it was a it was a a hefty portion of training camp that he missed with that second injury. And so, um, you know, I I would imagine, you know, he he works into, uh, as as long as things continue to progress, I, you know, it wouldn't surprise me if by the end um or even the middle of the regular season if he's um regained that starting role, but even just missing a week and a half or two weeks of training camp, he's gone from being a surefire starter and guy that is the captain of this entire defense to not ly losing that green dot Mike roll to Cambinham starting safety veteran um who's in this the second year with Lou Anarumo's defense to not even being a guy that we think is going to start when you look back at the rotations you saw it today in practice you've seen it for um even the the couple days since CJ Allen has been back um it it looks like a Davis Gaither and Jaylen Carl actually is uh the the group that the Colts are trotting out at least when you first go out on the field. Um the the duo that we see together most often um you mentioned that they're going to do a lot of rotating and I I think there are certain situations where you could see CJ Allen where you could see Bryce Bcher um out there where you could see um Austin who I think has looked really strong for the most part throughout camp. Um the the problem is and there was this poll um out on ESPN um who did a ranking of all of the positions um throughout the NFL. So you take every position um ranked teams one through 32 and the Colts linebacker unit is ranked dead last. Um, and I from an experience standpoint, um, you know, not being an an expert on the other linebacking crews in the NFL, um, I could see where you could get there. Akeem Davis Gaither, of course, um, a very, um, pedestrian year as a most most of the time starter with the Cardinals last year. and before that um was a a rare kind of a a spot um situational type guy earlier in his career. And then you've got four other guys that have not seen the field very often or are rookies in um CJ Allen, Bryce Bcher, Keh Austin at GK, and Jaylen Carise. But I I think I think if they are playing well and and from some of what we've seen in the preseason, I think these guys can really surprise um there's some been some really strong plays particularly from Ber and uh and Jaylen Carlay's in the preseason. Uh but they're I mean part of the reason why I think we could see a lot of rotation there is because they have some guys who do certain things really well but they don't have anyone who has really mastered the position or someone who they have confidence being on the field in you know as an everyown guy like we had in Germaine Pratt like we had in Zire Franklin last year in in year one of Louis Anaruma. They made a point going into this off seasonason that they needed to get younger and they needed to get faster in that position. And I think without question they have when you look at the unit that they have compared to Zire and Pratt. But what you lose in that is an ability to be confident that someone can stay on the field and do everything for you. And and when you're doing a lot of rotating and you're kind of guessing or predicting what the opposing offense is going to be doing is sometimes you're you you know you might get caught out in the the wrong spot with the the wrong guy on the field and you're going to be doing a lot of guesswork and predicting rather than just being able to rely on a couple of guys to be out there and play 90 95 close to 100% of the snaps and just do what they can do. I I am very interested to see how they do this. Linebacker is not a position that you rotate very much. >> Uh with the exception of like sometimes there are coverage guys who come in on third down like very obvious passing situations. It's just not something you see around the league very often. Um that that guys are kind of rotating. and Louis Anaruma offered up a an example with Cincinnati, but I think if you go back and look at those snaps, it didn't end up that way. So, I think the goal here is to buy time for CJ Allen to kind of figure it out or or for someone to Carlize is really interesting to me because uh the injuries had kind of made us all write him off, but they liked the idea of converting a safety into a uh a college safety into an NFL linebacker because of the coverage capabilities. And we've seen that. I think he's the best cover linebacker they have. Um, some of that partially because of the guys they acquired. Um, but I'm I'm interested to see how he gets used. I It's just It's an odd idea. It's not, like I said, it's just not a position you see a ton of rotation at. Um, and I'm curious to see how they use it, how they do everything. Uh because their plan like I we went back and looked at all those quotes. Their plan was very clearly if you go back and listen to the quotes and everything, it was we've got CJ Allen to play the mic. We'll let these other guys figure it out for the will. >> And instead they have to figure it out with both guys. >> Yeah. I remember I remember us asking questions of uh of Shane and Chris Ballard coming out of the draft and asked, you know, Bryce Bcher was also a Mike in college. Um is that a you know, is that a competition for those two guys? And they said not necessarily. Um but but they also said um you know there it it also wasn't a situation where they um couldn't foresee them both being on the field at the same time. So, as you said, I think this was a, you know, they they brought in a veteran in Hakee Davis Gaither in in free agency. They I think probably felt like there was a pretty high likelihood, especially when we saw what they they did in free agency, that they were going to go after a linebacker going into the draft. And so, you leave um leave a spot open um from the crew that you would presume would be starting to a guy like CJ Allen who they go and draft. And then it it it really felt like um Carl, who again I think I think Chris Ballard mentioned even a couple times when we were asking him about the his view of what the the prospect of the defense he would try to build in the offense would be. He mentioned Carlize if they could get him healthy that they would thought that he had a lot there. They go and get uh Bcher in the the fourth round. Um Carl of course is still there. GK is still there. And so it it kind of felt like a unit that was built around CJ Allen and then you've got one veteran and three young guys kind of fighting for that one spot. Instead we find ourselves in a position where Aake Davis Gaither who frankly looking at his body of work from last year. Um I I don't know that I would have expected frankly to be starting. Um, you know, I know Lou likes his veteran guys and so maybe it shouldn't be it shouldn't come to a great surprise. He hasn't had, I would say, a ton of moments in camp or in these preseason games where he's really stood out probably as much as uh as Bryce Bcher and Jaylen Car. Um but at the same time, um he's maybe he brings the most knowledge, the most certainly the most experience and a little bit of consistency to a unit where if you're going to be rotating guys out, maybe he's kind of the the foundation of that unit and then they kind of rotate guys around him. I know we'll we'll have to see how all of that works. Um coaches aren't necessarily showing their cards or telling us exactly how they're going to do things until we truly get to that week one game on September 13th against Baltimore. Um we uh we we didn't see super great quarterback play um in that that preseason game. Um and and that some of that uh carried over into today's practice that we uh got a chance to see all of. Um the the Colts did break training camp at Grand Park at the end of that joint practice on Thursday, but we still got an opportunity for today and the next two days to watch all of practice, take notes. Um we're continue continuing to do the live blogs on indar.com. If you guys have been following along with those, we will continue to do those the next two days. and I know there was a lot of sentiment coming out of the second preseason game that even if he didn't look great that Anthony Richardson, I think a lot of fans believe is head and shoulders above Riley Leonard for this um for this backup quarterback spot. uh Shane Syen told us today um reiterate a lot of what he told us even last week in camp that not only is he going to ride this through the rest of this week in practice and the preseason finale, but I think even take this through next week um the the practices that the Colts do uh and then maybe make a decision either two I guess it would be two weekends from now or heading into the true week one week of practice uh in early September make that decision on his backup quarterback. Uh someone asked him today in our press conference that we had with him if he felt like that would be something that would be static or if it could be fluid. He didn't really have a great answer for that. Um I I think there's there's two ways to look at this. there is who has had the best moments in preseason and I think that question is um pretty easy to be answered as as Anthony Richardson. But there's I think a second way that a lot of folks maybe forget or look overlook when we're we're talking about this quarterback battle and it is who is Shane Stiken going to pick because ultimately it is not who is performing the best. It is who Shane Styen who is the ultimate decision maker here. Who is the best fit for Shane? Who do who would Shane like the most? Who would Shane trust the most? Who is the best fit for what Shane wants to do? And I don't know that that is such an obvious choice as it may look like from what we've seen in preseason. I I think the other thing is that like I mean a lot of the those opinions are formed off of seeing the two preseason games and and really it's just one half from Richardson >> and an imperfect half. Like I I wrote I I don't want to I'm sure you're going to hear that and think well he's you know he's being harsh on Richardson. I wrote that it was his best week of the training camp. But like if you go by what we've seen in practices, like I think it's much closer than people give it credit for. Now I I think that there's a chance that you can run a a different kind of offense with Richardson. So, in a in a in a situation where there's one or two guys or one or two games that that Daniel Jones has to miss, I kind of like the idea of the Malik Willis thing the Packers did where you're running a basically a a completely different stripped down offense that fits him perfectly and will make it a little bit hard for guy for teams to prepare for you. Um, and so I can see that, but I I don't think it's as as uh cut and dry as Anthony Richardson has been so much better because like today in camp, we've seen or today in practice, he was he had three passes in a row that didn't come close to hitting their target. He was two of five. He's had a three of 12 day in camp. like he he goes through these bouts where he does not he just will not set his feet or get his feet in the right position and it costs them and it costs him accuracy. And so I think my uh my uh numbers on him I haven't looked at them but they were it was about a 10% difference and I think that would probably hold. Um maybe maybe Leonard's come down a little bit. I think that that would hold. Now Leonard has not been great either. I don't think he's had a lot of good days or really really any great days um the same way that Richard Richardson has. But Richardson's it's really just that preseason game. That's that's really it. It's that it's the first quarter of that Patriots game. I think one of the one of my takeaways from from last week is that like you know there's a reason these two guys are backups. I don't think they're as bad as like you need to go trade for somebody, but there's a reason those two guys are backups and there's a reason this battle is for the number two job and not for something else. >> I think it's a great point. Um, yeah, folks that, you know, I know there's, you know, there's some fans that were able to make it out to a good amount of training camp. um you know, maybe they're catching good days or maybe they're watching things and or seeing things uh a little bit differently than we are. But I yeah, I I think my biggest takeaway on this is that I I think I fall pretty close to you is that there whoever ends up being named the number two quarterback, I barring some stark change over the next two practices or a change in what we see in this final preseason game on Saturday, I I I almost don't know that anyone will have won the job. it will be the person that is named the backup quarterback. Neither of the two have put together a body of work that make you feel super comfortable about the prospect of them filling in uh you know potentially at the drop of a hat if Dana Jones get gets hit the wrong way or hits his head on the ground and needs to be pulled out to be evaluated for a concussion or something or or suffers something more serious. Obviously the um in that that Jacksonville game back on December 7th of last year, he was hobbled already with the fractured fibula, but certainly had no indication that he was going to go and tear his Achilles tendon and be out for um not only the rest of that game, but the the four games after that. So, whoever, you know, in a in a perfect situation, whoever you have in that number two role, you need to feel confident that they can go in and of course, they're not going to be as good as your starter. Um, because if they were as good as your starter, they would be on another team and starting in the league. But, um, you want to have faith that they can there could be as little drop off there as possible. And from what we have seen between the two of them and and contrasted by how well frankly Daniel Jones has performed throughout preseason, I think there's definitely some worry when you consider the fact that Daniel Jones has only had one season in his seven in the NFL where he's been able to play the entire season as the sorting quarterback. Um that was of course the the season that helped earn him um his massive second contract with Giants. um that then petered out and he was out of there I think what like 18 months or so after that. Um and then ends up on a short stint with the Vikings and then um wins the job a year ago almost to the day right now with the Colts and um gets through uh 12 games and change uh kind of the kind of the baseline for where he's been for the most part in his career. So, you uh I wish I you know, if I'm the Colts, I wish I felt a little bit more confident in this. I think again, no surprise, Anthony Richardson can give you more fireworks um than Riley Leonard can, but he can also bring you more mistakes. You see some passes that are just wildly off the mark in practice um as well as in games. Um, you see, you know, him fumbling the ball on a a run that looked like it was going to be pretty great. You see him put the ball in places where uh uh a wide receiver can't automatically get their hands on it and then it ends up in in a a bat of the ball and then that, you know, kind of is a 50/50 for the offense or the the quarterback that's right there. We saw that in that Patriots game in the first preseason pre-season game. So, um, yeah, it's it's a it's a weird situation. I don't I don't know that I came into camp, you know, with a a prediction necessarily of who I thought or or really thought that there was someone who had an advantage. title: LIVE: The Houston Texans address the media
text: So Monday, how was today? >> Yeah, today was a really really great day. I thought we got a great competitive work versus the Panthers. They showed up, very gracious hosts. Thankful for them for them having us. I like the way our guys showed up from start to finish today. We we executed really well. Guys played physical and we it was a productive practice on both sides. Like both teams came in with the right mindset. Appreciate Dave for how he handled it. Really great operation. Practices ran efficiently and we got a lot of productive work. So it's exactly what we wanted. Danielle is a problem. He continues to be a problem and you know, that's why I love having him and Will. When you have two guys off the edge who can be as disruptive as they are, it makes it hard on offenses. It makes them hard for them to operate on the timing that they want to operate on. So Danielle, you know, I saw a few plays he's back there in the backfield a lot. So it was a great to see that. >> Z'Darius any update on Smith and Gay? >> Smith and Gay went down today in in the practice. So we'll evaluate them when we get inside. We do not know. Yeah, adding K'Waun was a is a big get for us. We know we lost a significant player for us in Za'Darius Smith. It's hard to replace him. When you try to go out and find a guy with the caliber of K'Waun, we've played against K'Waun multiple times over the past couple years. He's continued to make plays time and time again. He's showed up. He's a young player, still an ascending player with a lot to improve upon, a lot to grow. So I'm excited to work with a young player who still has a very bright and promising future. But he has that big play making ability already. So it's been great to have him so far. We'll get him up and rolling here as the week continues. Yeah, Jaylen does a great job playing the F position, moving around a lot in the slot, giving us you know, giving us the option to move guys around, make defenses have to communicate. That's where Jaylen provides that force, and he's done a great job of punt returning. You know, last year was his first time doing it for us. He got better. He grew as the year went along. So, I'm expecting him to pick pick up where he left off and continue to improve as our punt returner as well. Yeah, from our vantage point, the offensive line was really the bright spot for me watching the offense, seeing how much time CJ and Davis had to operate, seeing the guys pass off games and stunts, seeing them hearing them actually communicate loud, everybody being on the same page. It's what we want from our guys, and that's how it looks when we execute. CJ Davis made some outstanding throws today as well. Our receivers caught the ball really well. The backs ran well. They blocked it well. Just overall, offensively, we definitely took a a jump from where we were in our last practice. Yeah, adding Keyshawn is not about, you know, the one play. We know it was a spectacular play that he made, but it's a just watching him, you know, throughout his career, just seeing what he's done. He's one of the the better contested catch players that I've seen. If the ball is close, he has a knack for going up, playing physical, and coming down with the football. So, that's what intrigued me when I continued to watch his tape from last year and previous years. He continued to make those tough catches, and that's what you want. You want I want everybody on our team to be tough mentally and physically and he's showing that on his tape. >> What about Blake Fisher and what he's had to go through and he's added some guys to the offense. What have you seen from him from a focus standpoint kind of staying with it with new bodies in the room? >> For Blake, I have seen a a definitely a a focused guy. He's been He's improved a ton. If I gave out awards, he would be he would get the award for the most improved offensive lineman this year as a from what he did last year from being in that jumbo type role. Like he's just lined up at left tackle and every day he's gotten better every single day and I'm really pleased with Blake. I'm proud of the work that he's put in. He's showing up daily. He's improved. He's taking a coaching really well and that's what it looks like, right? When you put the work in, you can get better and Blake has shown that tremendously. >> What's enabling Hutch to have this kind of He had a really good day today, another good day. What's enabling to have that kind of production? >> Starting with Hutch, man, it's his attitude. I love it. He has an infectious infectious energy. Every time he steps on the field, like he has this joy about him. He plays hard every single snap and he makes plays. Like the ball comes his way, he finds a way to make plays and so it's exciting about Hutch. I'll never have a bad day, always great attitude. He works the right way. He works hard at his craft and he he has a confidence in himself which you have to have at the wide receiver position. Hutch has that confidence and he's playing confident and showing up every day. >> Take a few more. Do you think any starters will play on Friday? >> No starters will play this this Friday. >> Good. >> What will you guys do to kind of ramp Booty up? I I noticed he was working with trainer. You know, I know he's been working. >> Right. >> What will you guys do to ramp him >> Yeah, for us to ramp him up, we'll start with our with our S&C group. They'll start him on the side just ramping him up, making sure we we like to understand our player's body, uh understand where they are. We go through some prelim- preliminary testing to make sure, you know, he's ready to go when it's time to get in. He got in today, did an individual, did some routes on air, and we'll continue to build him and progress him, you know, as the week goes along. >> All right. >> Thank you, guys. All right. >> No problem.

title: Defensive Coordinator Sean Duggan meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: We saw Jacob didn't practice today. Can you tell us as much as you can of his chances of playing on Friday? >> Yeah, I'm I'm going to just playing time stuff. I'm just going to push all that to coach half. Um you know, whatever he decides is the best interest of the team is what we'll do. >> One more in pursuit of that that might get shut down. Uh Atlanta has said that they'll probably play their starters. Will that affect how you approach the game? >> No, I mean, you know, the way we've been approaching preseason is you know, it's an evaluation tool and it it's a it's a big opportunity for the guys, right? To go out there and you know, play against their ones or their twos or their threes, whoever we put out there. What what an opportunity, right? You know, it's another chance to go play football. Um so now really, to be honest with you, it doesn't change how we go about it. We're just trying to become a more consistent defense. Um and just can just get better, whether it's a game or practice. That's always the goal for us. >> What we didn't see today and in what ways have you seen Jacob grow over camp? >> Yeah, I think the game's slowing down for for Jacob. Um you know, just the understanding of the call, understanding what's going on, not only in front of as it pertains to the run game, but what's going on around him and whether it's zone coverage or man coverage. I think, you know, when you play when you play defense, the more understanding you have of what's going on around you, the faster you can play and you can start anticipating. So I've seen that. Um and it's something he needs to continue to get better at, too. So. >> Sean, what's the ceiling for this football team? >> You know, I I I think we have a lot of talented guys who play physical, play the right way. Um you know, I I never like putting a ceiling on a group of, you know, whether it's the defense or a certain player. To me, I'm just always looking for continually getting better, right? Um you know, we should be playing better football today than we played yesterday. You know, week 17, we should be better than week one. It's It's just all to me about getting better, not necessarily a set ceiling or we we could be this or we should be this. We need to see steady improvement every single day. >> What areas do you see Chris Johnson growing? >> Yeah, I think Chris has done a nice job. You know, it it's similar to what I was saying about Jay Rod. It's the understanding of the techniques of what's going on around him of issues in coverage, you know, how he can be attacked in certain coverages or techniques and that understanding. You know, again, he's a guy that has gotten better every single day. So. >> What would you say or could you say you've seen in regards to his instincts? >> Yeah, you know, I I think you just kind of when you see it you're like he just he has a feel for the game. It's one of those things like, you know, when you talk about instincts for me just sometimes it's a little hard to explain but it's one of those when you know it you see it. Um or sorry, when you see it you know it. so I think just him just listening to himself as a football player and then executing the techniques within the call is is he's definitely an instinctual player. >> So in regarding Chop, from the from the untrained eye it seems like he's improved in both setting the edge and attacking the passer. What have you seen? >> I think Chop's done a great job this camp. Um again, you know, I I don't mean to sound like a broken record but he's he's put in the work and he's gotten better every day. You know, you see the growth from OTAs to now and that's a huge credit to him and the work he's put in, you know, not only on the field but transforming his body in the weight room, you know, being in the this shape you need to be in down here to play in this heat and play be an every down player. Um you know, cuz everybody wants to have the gas on third down and rush the passer, you know, if you ask D-line that that's fun for them, right? But you got to earn the right to do that and I think he's put in so much work on the field and off the field and then I think the coaches have done a a really nice job with him getting him to to understand where to put his eyes, where to place where to put his hands, um situational football, right? Obviously, third down's very different than first and second. When I can take a shot, you know what I mean? So I think he's done a nice job and again, just just getting better every single day. >> When the staff first took him in, what was the first thing you wanted to either emphasize to him if you wanted to change, you just emphasize to him. >> I think the first thing we did with Chop is just tell him we're going to demand from him, right? You know, we're we're going to demand a lot from that guy cuz he's capable. You know, he's capable of doing playing first, second, early down, playing the run, setting edges, then rushing the passer. You know, we're not just going to let it the guy off the hook and say, "Oh, you can only do this." And it's really the same for a lot of guys, right? We're not just going to say, "Oh, he's a one-trick pony, you can do this." We're going to demand he gets better at his weaknesses and then continue to grow on his strengths. >> So, is is Kyle Lewis a safety or linebacker? Safety or linebacker? Big nickel safety? How do you classify him nowadays? >> How do you classify him? >> Uh all all three, really. >> I think Kyle's Kyle's a really good football player. You know, he's he's a guy who plays with instincts, plays with passion and physicality, and and really plays the game the right way, and you know, being able to move him around has been pretty fun. >> And we all know what Zach Sieler can do, but with with him being out the last couple of weeks, is there someone who really benefited from those extra reps filling in for him? >> I think a lot of guys benefited. You know, I mean, Zach brings a lot to the table. You know, his leadership, obviously he's played a lot of football at a high level. Um you see guys stepping up in, you know, the communication aspect that goes along with the front. You know, when Zach's not in there, other guys have had to kind of learn how to do that without him. Um you know, and you've seen a lot of guys step up as far as reps and taking advantage of their opportunity. >> You've been upstairs the first two, right? >> Yes, sir. >> How is What have you and Jeff learned relative to you being upstairs and him calling it from the field, working together? >> Um you know, honestly, it's just it's it's really the same communication it's been since I've been with him. The only difference is he's in the heat, and I'm in the air conditioning. But it's uh it's it's been good. Um you know, we have really good communication between the two of us and the rest of the staff. Um so, it's been good, and it's been getting cleaner every game. >> Does some play corners like noise in their ears from their friends more than others? >> Uh you'd have to ask them. I'm sure it's a personal preference. >> Coach, after every game >> With Kyle obviously he hasn't played safety that much. How long do you think that process or that transition takes for a player? >> Oh, that's a good question. You know, I think you know, we said he's an instinctual player, so you do definitely see some instincts show up, whether it's, you know, him playing in coverage, reading the quarterback, or him coming down fitting the run. You definitely can see that. I think with any position it's the the details of the position. You just need reps, and you need to you need coaching, and you need you just got to keep doing it cuz, you know, I'm a big believer in, you know, not only do you learn from success, and you let's say I, you know, I came down and fit the run, and I fit it perfectly. Okay, now in my brain I can go, "Okay, I I can do this again. I got a feel for when to come down. Where are my eyes?" But, I think you learn a lot from scars, too. All right, you learn if okay, maybe on this one I wasn't wide enough in my drop, or maybe I'm looking at routes too much here. So, I think just the more reps he gets, I think he'll learn, you know, as far as putting a timetable on it, I think it's it it is based on the player and how many reps they get. >> And Michael Tab, what have you seen from him this training camp? >> I you know, I yeah, I I really don't mean to sound like a broken record here, but he's a guy that's gotten better and better and continued to learn the scheme. You know, he he knows when he can play fast, he knows when he can take a shot. Um he understands what's going on around him. I think he's a really good communicator, which I think is very important um at the safety position, but I think he's a guy that just I think he loves football, he loves learning, um and he's gotten better every day. >> What have you liked from Keith Washington? >> Uh Keith's Keith's done a lot of good things. Um you know, I really you got a lot of respect for the guy cuz when he first got here, you know, it was not what you're seeing right now when you watch practice. Um, so the work he's put in, you know, the techniques and same thing, understanding when I can whether I can loosen up, whether I need to play thicker here. Okay, where are my eyes here? What is the backfield set telling me? He's taking in all that coaching and playing faster and faster and faster. Um, you know, as far as what I see, I see a quick guy who uses his hands, who can doing a good job anchoring in the run game. Um, and he's got some juice in the pass game, which I think with him the confidence is showing, right? He made a couple plays. Now he has some confidence. Now he's playing faster and I I just think that's that's building upon itself with him. >> Last question, guys. >> What can having a trio of linebackers like J.B. and Jacob do for a defense? >> I think the more good players you can have on the football field the better. Um, as far as specifically linebackers, you know, it's a position where depth is you're going to you always want depth at every position, right? Um, it just allows you to get good players on the football field.

title: John Harbaugh: ‘There are still spots up in the air’ | New York Giants
text: Appreciate everybody being here. Good practice and we're getting ready for the the final preseason game against the Jets. I've heard a lot about this preseason game, so I'm excited to be a part of it for the first time. We'll be the visiting team, so we got to figure out just as I figured out, you know, where we go for the home games. Now now you got to figure out where you are for a visiting team, so that's a lot to keep track of. But we're looking forward to it and can't wait for the game. He was doing a great job across the board, offense and special teams. He he had definitely carved out a role for us on our team and then to see that happen, especially, you know, just a non-contact type of an injury, uh it's just kind of shocking to see. So, you feel bad for him. I mean, that's the biggest thing. He and I were, you know, texting last night and even more this morning, so I I think he's in a better place now than he was yesterday. But um it's going to be a a long road back, but he'll get back. He'll get back and we'll be behind him the whole way. >> What does that What does that do now for the wide receiver room? >> Uh it just means that the next guy steps up and and fills that role.
