I think he would have, if not started, I think he would have been in the rotation for the Giants and would have been a special teams contributor. I think this clearly paves the way now for both Beckham and Barios uh to probably make this team. But you don't know, you know, what could happen as the as someone else may become available. But right now, if you ask me, if I had to guess, um I think the Giants probably go with six receivers. And it's um neighbors. Uh, it's Mooney, it's it's Sllayton, it's of course the rookie um Malachi Fields, Odell Beckham, and uh Barios. That that would be my guess as of now are the six favorites. But things could change if if certain guys become available uh that the Giants may be attracted to. But I think it clearly um is good news for Beckham in terms of making this roster. But tough loss for the Giants because I do think he would have played a role in this offense. >> Yeah, like Anthony said, you you hate to see anybody get injured, especially in practice. But this this is why I'm such an advocate of let these guys play in the preeason. Everybody's always worried about injuries and you see it doesn't matter. I forgot um uh is it one of the Falcons um one of the Falcons like one of their best edge rushers. I forgot if it I forgot one of them's arrested or not is suspended for eight games and one one just hurt himself in practice. I don't know if it was James Pierce. That's why I I forget who it was but it just goes to show you these things can happen in practice at any point. something like that. These freak injuries, these these soft tissue injuries, these tendon injury uh injuries, they can happen at any point, even without usually I mean those things are non-cont injuries and they can happen at any point. Sucks. You feel bad for Calvin Austin cuz I'm pretty sure he was going to make this team. I think that they were looking the reason he returned punts on Saturday was I really feel like that was going to be his role. I always felt like Odell was going to make this team, but I felt like between Austin and Barios, they were looking at Austin return of those punts because they were probably going to go in that direction since he was going to play that slot receiver role. Very similar size to Janell Robinson. They could have been our Well Robinson this year. Um, and you just hate to see anybody get injured. They may look on the wide receiver. I mean, who knows? The Giants are going to explore all options. So, you know, never say never to another wide receiver, but I I definitely do do think that this means Odell is almost a lock for the team. And yeah, we heard about the Darnell Mooney trade rumors and, you know, maybe Darius Sllayton, but obviously that's not going to happen. So, it it sucks. You you don't like to see anybody get injured like that and you you feel for the player, but again, you know, the things happen. I mean, it's football. This is very common place nowadays. People rupture their Achilles. We, you know, Audriana's mentioned we've lost three players to ruptured Achilles in May and they weren't even doing anything. Um, it's, this is very common this day and age. This is a very common injury. They're stronger. They they cut harder. Um, you know, our turf is garbage, but it just it happens. It's not just on our turf. It happens all over the league. It's unfortunate, but I do think that this presents an opportunity for guys like Odell Beckham, for guys like Braxton Barios to step in there and and fill his role. So, next man up. You know, it sucks, but that is the nature of the beast. That is the nature of the business. It's next man up. So, somebody's got to step up in that spot. And we're going to go from bad news to good news. The good news is we had a guy tear ACL last year. We were hearing that he might not play until week four, week five. He's way behind schedule. Well, now it seems like he's almost a definite to play week one. And that is Malika neighbors.

title: Tristan Wirfs & Josiah Trotter on Getting Better Everyday | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: How you doing everybody? Good to see you. Yeah, I feel great right now. Um, wasn't how I was hoping to start camp. That was really frustrating, but um very nice to be back out here with the with the boys. Um, yeah, I feel good. Yeah, 100% 100%. Um I think we're trying to be smart a little bit early like early on in camp. I was like I've never had a hamstring before. I was like what the I was like what is this? Um But no, yeah, being able to got a couple plays yesterday and then kind of just keep keep doing that moving forward. Um I think you know these next these next 2 weeks will be big just to get as many reps as I can, you know, but yeah, really really happy to be back out there with the boys. Um just grinding with them. I know it's we got blessed early in camp with the weather so I didn't feel too bad, you know, but no, it's it's I'm really happy to be back with them. Yeah, I think it was interesting at first like in OTAs and everything, but now kind of we all got the hang of it got the got the hang of the aiming points and the footwork and and what we're what we're trying to accomplish with it, but yeah, I'm a I'm a big fan of it. Yeah, 100%. Yeah, I think just trying to uh use it to diversify our offense a little bit and and and marry things up, but I think it's been good so far. It's been a been a lot of fun. Yeah, I mean it it it means a lot. I mean these are my these are my brothers. It's it's you know, I love coming out here. This is one of my favorite parts of the game is is being with them. Um, so for them to to say it to say that really means the world to me. Um, you know, it makes me want to go you know, even harder and and and you know, do everything I can for them. Um and just do anything I can to help this team win, but yeah, that means a lot. Yeah. >> I think we're very tight-knit team. I think both sides of the ball, I think um I mean, I got to see the I mean, last year I missed training camp. That that sucked. Um but to to see it uh through that lens, you know, like just got on the outside is is was was weird. I mean, I wasn't a fan of it. You know, we didn't like didn't like that point of view, but um to see guys step up and to see guys, you know, um take on that leadership role has been has been um really cool to see and um you know, just the guys, you know, going out there every day grinding, you know, not complaining what it matter what the weather is, how hot it is, whatever, you know, not making excuses, just going out and and and doing their job. >> With you out there now, we see you there with Brandon and Graham >> Mhm. >> and Cody and and Luke. >> Yeah. >> It's the same group that got such great results in >> really drove that offense. >> Assuming you're all good to go and we point, do you think you can play at that same level this year? >> Yeah, that's I mean, that's definitely the goal to be one of the top units in the NFL. Um you know, we want we want teams to turn on the tape and and say that's a you know, those are those are a bunch of badass, you know, badass guys um that that that finish plays and um you know, it's it's nice to have us all back out there. I know we went through a big reshuffle, you know, throughout the whole season last year, got but at the same time guys stepped up and and you know, came in and did their best and and gave us everything they had. So, I think that's just uh uh uh a credit to our room, you know, guys that come in and and you know, there's there's a standard that we all want to uphold and we all want to play for each other. Um but yeah, it's nice it's nice to have to to have the whole gang back. >> from the sidelines. Now you've kind of seen it through the last week. [clears throat] You put a lot into this defensive front seven this offseason. >> biggest difference that you see in that group? >> Man, they're uh they're tough. It's it's it's fun to watch. It's fun to compete against. Um and I think I think they're going to be a problem this year, but it's nice to see that that kind of mentality, you know, with with Nacho coming back and and of course adding adding Akiem, you know, I'm glad I don't have to block him twice a year anymore. That's always a That's always a fun match up, but then you got Baine and and Yaya on the edges that I think I mean Kansi's, you know, back back too, so I don't know, it's a mean it's a mean front. It's a mean front, so, you know, I know they're excited for a big year coming and I think we all are too. I think they're going to do do great things. >> Tristan, what are your impressions of Baine? >> Yeah, you know, I haven't got to go against him much yet, but he's a he's a freak. Watching his some of his his bend is pretty nasty. And then just what he's been doing I think it like overall as a rusher, you know, he's so he's so young and he's still like just figured, you know, figuring stuff out. Like I think he's he's finding out he can do stuff that I don't think he knew. So, it's cool that we got some conversations just about what I've seen from him and and and what I think would would be beneficial against tackles and No, I'm excited to kind of get a couple reps against him here going forward, but No, I think he's been been out here busting his balls. Yeah, I think it's it's exciting to watch. >> Tristan, you've got a new running back there in the game well. >> Your thoughts on him too but also too how Bucky has looked fully healthy he's Yeah, size too just overall thoughts on the running backs. >> Yeah, no, I think I think they're a bunch of dogs. I think I think Kenny G brings brings um that veteran presence and and also like I think it kind of expands our our our pass game too. He's he's he's he he's got some hands on him. But and then to see Buck, you know, back healthy and and flying around just being a joystick is is pretty pretty sweet to watch. You know, we all love it when he's out there. He definitely makes us a better team. I think our room our room as a whole like it's, you know, there's just some dogs in there and it's it's going to be fun to watch them fly around. >> Recently Baker said that the Bucks are going to shock a lot of people this year. Do you echo that sentiment? >> Always, yeah. Always. That's That's our goal, you know, it's I mean the goal's always the Super Bowl. I think that's what it is for every team, but you know, ending with a with a pretty shitty taste in our mouth last year is just, you know, I think everyone put in a lot of work. It's also we had a really good group of guys here at the facility training. I think it's going to be fun. >> You still have a couple of weeks before the opener, but can you explain what you had to do and how do you feel like you have grown physically >> Yeah, they put me through some crazy stuff. Um wasn't a fan, but I was like, "Guys, I was like I was like I I want to come back and and be in shape, you know, the bike, the VersaClimber." Um I was in the pool. Um A lot of cardio, the skier, like I don't know. It just It sucks. The the prowler put like It sucked, you know, but I was like, "Listen, I was like I want to be in shape, you know, I don't want to get out of shape, but you know, it's not you know, it's it's nothing the same as being in football shape, but I feel like I'm in damn good shape good shape from what they were putting me through, but um yeah, like that was the that was the plan. It's like, "Let's, you know, do everything I can to to come back and just start rolling." So, um yeah, I think we crushed it. I think it's awesome. >> Tristan, what can you say specifically about Cody Myers? Uh just how he's looked in camp so far seeing him out there in the preseason. >> Yeah, I think Cody Cody looks great. Um moving around like he always does. Like his recovery is unbelievable. I think he's his his his punches have been really really strong this this camp. Um it's it's fun to watch. It's just fun to watch like all of us, you know, back you know, back together on the same line. Um you know, we've been together for a while now and it's it's it's fun, you know, the more reps we get together, you know, the more comfortable we get. Um and that nonverbal communication starts coming back. It's like I know what Ben's going to do, you know, he knows what I'm going to do. We We're all just kind of on the same page, you know, five guys seeing stuff through the same set of eyes. It's it's it's it's pretty fun and um that's what you want, you know, that's what you want to get to. That's what you want to have from your line. So, I know we're all just um excited to be back together and then um yeah, Cody looks great. >> And then assuming the line stays at full strength throughout the season, what do you think this unit's potential is up front? >> Oh my gosh. Um I don't know. I know we want to move the line of scrimmage and I know we want to keep Six safe cuz if we do that, you know, I think we're going to win some ball games. Um let let him let him go be the dog that he is and then let our you know, let our running back room eat, you know. Um we're just trying we're just trying to be great, you know. >> Tristan, you're your closest friend is Baker Mayfield and just wondering what you think his mentality is going into this season. You know, he plays the a chip on his shoulder, but just all the contract stuff and everything that I expect Baker to be Baker, and I expect him to lead us like he always does, and I expect him to bring the best out of us, and and you know, I I expect this old line to lead from the front and not, you know, not wait for six to get everybody started, you know, um we got to help him out a little bit. Um we got to bring the juice. We got to bring the fire. Um you know, cuz he does you know, he does it day in and day out, week in and week out. Um you know, we got to help him out a little bit. But, um no, I think he's going to play with his hair on fire like he always does. I think he's going to I don't know. I think he's going to show a lot of people what's up, and it's going to be it's going to be pretty pretty cool to watch. Thanks, guys. Thanks, guys. Thanks, guys. Good morning. >> You made a big play today with an interception. >> Yes. >> Through that, and also is the game starting to slow down a little bit for you near the end of camp? >> Yeah. Yeah, we just had a man-to-man call. Uh just, you know, playing my leverage, and then just took it up He just tried to take it up the field that point. Just played my leverage, and then just, you know, when the ball's in the air, you can't panic. So, just looked up, saw the ball, just made a play, and you know, try to come down with the ball. So, that's all I can do. But, yeah, I feel like the game's been slowing down, you know, pretty quick. Just coming in, kind of already used to football's football at the end of the day. You know, especially when you have a brother and dad that played. So, just blessed to have them, and then but like the game coming in uh was pretty slow down. It was just uh the detail things. Trying to be very detailed in your work. I feel like that's the biggest thing in the NFL that I've seen. It's just the little things where between either making a play, not making a play, uh little things like that. So. >> What's been the biggest adjustment for you playing in the NFL? >> Yeah, just the details, honestly. I don't think um really it's been like, you know, anything with the play strength or anything like that, cuz I feel like playing in the SEC, having a dad and a brother that played, blessed to have them, just the kind of help me going into the league and then before that. So, I feel like I've been prepared for this moment my whole life. I'm just out there just trying to you know, just play my game, play fast. And obviously there's things I got to continue to clean up and be better at. But I feel like the big thing I'm trying to focus on is my details, the small things. >> What's your chemistry like with you and Alex Anzalone and how much of a blessing is it to have him seasoned NFL veteran play next to you and be able to answer any questions you might have? >> Yeah, no doubt. It's a great blessing to be have a guy like Alex. You know, a guy that you know, has been a vet to other guys, you know, from when he was at Detroit to the Saints. So, being able to talk to him, have him help me, coach me up, see things from a different perspective or when we're out there talking back and forth, him asking me maybe what I saw or what that may have happened. But yeah, no, I enjoy having him out there, being able to learn from him, ask questions and kind of continue to grow. >> How would you assess the defense did over the past few days against the Jaguars? >> Yeah, you know, we talked yesterday and we feel like yesterday wasn't our standard and we feel like we came out yesterday had a faster start than you we did yesterday and we're able to make some plays and just overall we just knew yesterday wasn't the standard or what we hold ourselves to. And so, we just you know, obviously talked about that and we want to come out here today, try to do what we could even though we didn't have pads on, but just be smart from a mental standpoint and go from there. >> Are you finding your voice in this defense? I mean, whether you have a C on your chest or not, the middle linebacker is the voice of the defense. Is that the role that day by day you're you're becoming more comfortable with and letting that come out? >> Yeah, no doubt. Just talking, you know, having a voice. You know, everyone kind of knows their role. You know, even as a rookie but I still feel like I have a voice. You know, I'm going to speak up if I need to speak up and also you know, obviously you got to make calls. You're the middle linebacker. So, you got to have something to you. You got to say it, say it with meaning and just you know, just go to them and just talk to your guys, you know. >> Jacksonville has been one of the better defenses in the sorry, offenses in the NFL the last few days. What have you learned about yourself and about this defense going up against Jacksonville the last few days? >> Oh yeah, really good offense. You know, he the their head coach was here in 2014 I believe they said and you know, their offense is pretty similar to ours. So, we knew that kind of coming in. But really good offense and kind of showed us the things that we got to clean up, we can still be better at. But, you know, when you're in the NFL, there's a lot of good teams and you just like I said, it's just details. We It's the little things that we know we have to clean up from yesterday going into today that you know, we weren't going to be able to obviously do cuz we don't have pads on, but things little things that we knew we had to clean up. >> Your ability to slip past blockers in the run game to get to the line of scrimmage and make that play, what's the key to making that type of play? Is it leverage? Is it physicality? What is it? >> Uh sometimes it's, you know, it's a little bit of those, but sometimes it's just God-given abilities and gifts, you know, I just thank God that he blessed me with the instincts to be able to do it. It's just a feel. Um you know, when you're out there, you can't think too much, you just got to play. And you just got to have a feel for the game to know when to do it, when not to do it um between what you're seeing what you're feeling. So, it's just a feel of the game that not a lot of people um know how they don't know unless they played the game, you know, not a lot of people know, so I just say it's really just a feel and just blessed to be able to have the instincts to be able to do it. >> Is that an area you've improved in? I think that area in the free safety last year and this year. >> You know, you know plays, no coverage you can have it done, right? Oh, yes, sir, no doubt. I know coming in, um I know there's outside noise people saying I could or could not, but I know what I can do. I know what God put inside of me, so I just wanted to come out here and be able to show that I can not only just cover, I can blitz, pass rush and be everything that the Bucs need me to be for this organization um and then try to win football games ultimately. So, if I need to be on the field there's five downs, I wish I'd be on the field for five downs. But, um yeah, ultimately I just try to do what I can to show the organization what I can do to be able to stay on the field. >> You're a mild-mannered guy off the field, but the switch flips when you're on the field. What causes that flip for you? >> Yeah, it's just once I step on the field, I know it's business at the end of the day um and just switching flipping mindsets, you know, having that dog killer mindset that you know, my dad instilled to me as a young age and you know, just going out there to be the middle linebacker cuz it starts with us. The intensity, you know, everything that every starts with us at the end of the day. You know, obviously going to start up front, but I was seeing my line back we got to set the tone energy everything like that. So yeah. Yeah, I think we did a great job kind of just developing our course just not only just our relationship off the field but just on the field. You know, just getting better learning cuz when you come in as a rookie, you know, you know but you don't know everything. You got you got a lot of room to grow a lot of things to continue to work on so I think over from you know, when we first got here to now I just think we've all grown from offense and rookies and defense and rookies where I feel like we you know, been able to help this team and organization in certain way. I'm not sure. That's up to the head coach. I don't know. Yeah, no doubt even I mean yesterday again Vita Vea. You know, that was a great help. You know, you could definitely feel his presence you know, as a linebacker and you know, when you have him in there but over the course of you know, the first day of camp to now you know, the D-line has done a great job. You know, obviously we all have things we can do to clean up but they did a great job you know, trying to help us out you know, with this holding double team and us just trying to help them getting double teams off. So you know, and we have a great rush up front great guys that are going to anchor down in that run game. So yeah. All right. Thank you. Appreciate it. Thank you.

title: Jarran Reed: "We're Hungrier This Year" | Seattle Seahawks
text: What's up everybody? >> How you doing? >> What was What was all the excitement over there for? >> Oh man, we got the little viral sensation Bernard. He's known for saying baptize the chicken. Little South Carolina guy, man. Cool guy. With some good chicken. >> Was it good? >> I have Yeah, it was really good. I only had one piece. I'm I'm ready to go shower up and get a whole plate. >> Who arranged that for him to be out here? >> Uh me and D Hall talked about it. Um I just told D Hall it'd be good to get him out here. Uh you know, both of us being from the south. Uh we just teamed up with Mo. Um D Hall finished y'all. Pause. Later pause. But uh you know >> [laughter] >> You know, getting him out here, man. And uh you know, just treat the whole team to some chicken. Who don't love fried chicken? >> What makes uh great chicken? >> What makes what? >> What makes it great? What makes What's the best? >> Crispy. Long as it's crispy and fried. Whatever sauce you put on it, you know. Can't determine too. But long long as you try it before the sauce. >> You're going into year 11. You're Super Bowl champion now. Like do you Are you too caught up in the present to think about Do you allow yourself to reflect on where your career's been so far and what you've accomplished? >> Uh yeah, I mean anytime I talk to the young guys, I'm always just reflecting back. Just not even Super Bowl, just from where I started, you know, to where I am now. let them know what steps I've made, you know, things to do, and how you can further along your career early. How you can turn into a professional player early on the professional side. Um I just try to let them always know, man, it's always room for growth. Even now, you know, I think I can still grow as a player being in year 11. Um we joke about it all the time, like coming out here, like me, uh D Law, and Leo, we always break it down. Saying like old old guys, you know, just joking around. We just play around. But man, I feel really good. Um being around these guys keeps me youthful, man. And um, yeah, man. It's just been a long road. I'm just thankful where I'm at now. You know, definitely learned a lot. >> You joke about old guys, but what's it like having this you know, you mentioned Leo and D-Law and then um, Dante Fowler's a 10th-year guy. I think Chandler's a ninth-year guy. What's it like having all these older veterans playing together? >> Um, it's good. I mean, cuz I mean, you really look at us, we all still look really young, though. You know what I'm saying? So, like, we're not like the old guys from back in the day. They look old, you know. I'm trying to just pass for like 25 to 28. You know. But I mean, it's good to have them around, man. You know, there's a lot of experience that's in the room. Um, we know how to get to work. You know, we can show the guys a way how we get to work, man. You know, how we attack the field, how we attack film, how we attack getting our body right, getting our mental right, you know, to prepare for training camp, practice, meetings, and games. >> Is there a piece of advice you remember from your rookie season that you still think about? >> Oh, yes. Definitely about how to be a pro. As soon as you said that, of course, the same two guys come to my mind every time, man. I was just very thankful to come to the situation that I was in as a rookie. You know, having Mike, Cliff, Autry, Reuben. Shout out to Brandon Hill. You know, he was he helped me definitely a lot, you know, when I first [snorts] came in. You know, uh, uh, just the coaches, you know, everybody we had. Especially like huge shout out shout out to Clint Hurtt. It was definitely, you know, how to take care of my body. You know, when I was young, you know, I could just get up and go. You know, well, we weren't really on our phones that much, but I could just probably like sit around a ping pong table or something, then go practice. But now, yeah, I got a whole game plan. I need at least a good hour, you know, just just feel good. But no, you you you just feel better, you can move better. Um, you just play better. I just carry that on throughout my practice, throughout my week. You know, it carries me on the game day. >> What's that routine look like? >> Uh, I'd rather keep that in the vault. But uh, seriously, though, you know, just a little you know, little cold tub, hot tub. Just working on anything that makes me feel good in the training room. I do a lot of massage work, acupuncture massage, cupping stretching all the way down the line. You know, I got a whole little routine that I do. >> How do you feel this team is right now compared to where you guys were a year ago this time? >> Um, you know, I think just going into year three, we're just really more connected. I think we're more more focused than ever. Um, a lot of people, you know, always try to bring up the Super Bowl and all that, but literally nobody talks about it. Seriously. And like we don't bring it up. We just worry about the day that we're in, the present that we're in. Um, and we just attack the day. I think we're more hungry this year, too, which is surprising. Um, just we we know what we got to do. I think everybody wants to play good ball. Everybody wants the operation to be well. We want our alignments, our assignments, you know, how we take the ball to be good on defense, you know, how we play our style of defense. We just want to up everything we're doing. >> Have you guys talked at all about how other teams are going to kind of test themselves against you uh differently now that you're the Super Bowl champs? >> Um, no. We just worried about us, you know, focus on being the best us that we can be. Um, you know, one day at a time, one play at a time, one meeting at a time, you know, just really just focus on being the best that we can in the present day. >> Now, how does that feeling of being more hungry sort of show up? >> Um, just the way we attack practice. I I think the way the guys attack the field, it's the want to that every guy has. Um, how we get in the meeting rooms and how we're critical of ourselves in meeting rooms, and how we're in our individual, how detailed we are, you know, making sure that we coach up the young guys like Harbaugh, still making sure they know, "Look, we're here for you. This is the way we do it." Showing them the way. I think just the little details the little details that we do every day. You know, guys are just hungry and we want it. Even to the way we work out, man. Like all of us work out really hard. Um, we're not skipping any reps. We're doing extra. And that's on our own. That's just cuz, you know, I think everybody wants to be great in their own way. >> Jarran, Hard Knocks showed a scene of the leadership council you guys have meeting with Mike. What do you like about the way Mike does that and the chance to kind of have a open dialogue with your head coach with the leaders? >> Oh, it's always good for us to get in there man, you know, get over the guys that call the leadership council. Um, you know, we go in there we just brainstorm, put our minds together. Uh, he he asked us questions about the schedule, see how we feel about it. See if we want to add something on ourselves, is it something that we feel like we need to do especially as O-line D-line just to make sure we stay in the shape. Um, you know, it's it's just little stuff like that, you know, and just good cuz you know, he gets our opinion, he listens to us and uh, he takes that on and and and intertwines that with what he thinks and we come together and then we take it to the team. >> Mike told us that after the Super Bowl he told you guys, "Hey, you can, you know, do it remotely for the first couple weeks to make up for how long a season it was." And look like most of the team showed up anyways for the the start of it. What do you think that said about like how you guys were going to handle being champions and all the all that comes with that? >> Uh, first and foremost I think we miss each other a lot. >> You know, but uh, that just shows that guys are ready get back to work. Um, we took some time off and I think it, you know, when the Super Bowl was over we all went to the locker room like, "Man, this is it?" I mean, cuz we work so hard and we're just used to working hard and we was like that we could play a couple more weeks. But, you know, the guys are ready get back to work, hungry. You know, I think they were excited to see what this new season is going to bring, the new faces that we could bring in, you know, how it was going to attack. >> Jared, obviously sounds to you like today. What does it mean to you that the culture, everything that here is so strong somebody wants to spend half of their money to be the new owner of this team and it's really built on what you and some of your teammates have really kind of forged here the last few years? >> Yeah, um, I've been on the practice field so I really didn't know much about it. I I seen I seen it earlier, but I mean, I guess that's good. Um, that just speaks to to the culture that we're building here and uh, we have a great staff, we have a great, you know, uh, GM, president, you know, uh, from top to bottom, man, it's top tier. You know, I think it's like another like the Seahawks organization, you know. It's great, you know, hopefully we get to meet them, you know, bring them along and get them in the 12s, the Seahawks way. >> Going against Sam every day, what's what stands out about the kind of camp he's had? >> Oh, Sam's elite, man. I think he's at the top of his game right now. Definitely one of the best, if the best quarterback in the league, in my opinion. You know, I love my quarterback, man. The way he he he keeps his head down, he attacks every day. He doesn't really say much. Shout out to Ginger Cola, you feel me? You know, man, Sam is a great guy, man. Another guy who's just been through something, who had who's had a lot of obstacles to overcome during his career. You know, to see where he's at now. I've actually caught the the ball from Sam one time before. He throws the ball really hard. You know, it's it's it's yeah. That thing spins, man. But, um he he definitely gives us a hard test, you know, between him, Jack, Scoob, Shaheed, you know, Tory, you know, Elijah, you know, all of those guys that go out there and run and catch and stuff, man. It's it's definitely tough. I feel like, you know, it's good on good every day for a reason. >> Thanks, man. Appreciate it.

title: Cooper Kupp On Playing For The Seahawks "It's A Very Special Thing" | Seattle Seahawks
text: Hello everyone. >> Hello. >> Thank you. >> How's the wing T coming along? >> It's good. It's good. We're we're enjoying it. >> I can't put that up there, can I? Uh so you walking off with Jake Peetz. What do you think he's adding to the quarterback room? What kind of coach is he and what do you think he's adding to that room? >> Uh yeah, I mean shoot, he's a a high energy individual um and he knows a lot of football. Yeah, they uh I mean, I think there's always stuff. There's always I mean, there's something you're grabbing from everyone in terms of this you know, how you're seeing a stem of routes like, you know, I've I've run a certain route along for a long time. Um they're not just out there doing things just to do them. There's a reason behind them. And so, uh yeah, you're always I mean, keeping an eye on things and um having those conversations in our room. Um it's it's makes it a lot of fun to uh to talk ball. >> Perspective in your 10th year, what can you say about perspective on the field, off the field? I know it's a big question, but >> Yeah. Uh yeah, it is a big question. I mean, I know there's so much I think the uh I think things get uh I don't know what the word is exactly. Probably this is not this is not the right way to say it, but things become less things aren't as pivotal, right? Like you when you're young, every single play holds the weight of the world. And um you know, a win a win can put you in a place that you feel like you can't like you're you've got it all figured out, which isn't the right place to be. Um and then a loss and a rep can make you feel like you can never you'll never be able to do it. And being able to both those things are wrong. Um but I think as time goes on, you realize it's all journey, it's all process, it's all about this build into who you're going to be and just constantly responding to those opportunities. That ultimately is what is going to write the story, right? It's not the outcome of the moment. It's how you're going to respond to the string of moments that happen. >> Cooper, somebody from Yakama with the sale, what does it mean to have this next chapter with the team that's special in your whole life? >> Yeah, well, you know, it's uh it's it's pretty cool. I mean, I you know, I've talked a lot about, you know, growing up a Seahawks fan. And then eventually, you know, learning bedtime was bedtime was when the game ended. So, then it became just I was rooting for overtime at all times and just enjoying football. But uh I uh you know, it's not lost on me how cool it is to come back to the state that, you know, I was I grew up here. Spent 18 years of my life. Um 18 years of my life in Yakima. Spent, you know, 23 years in the state of Washington. And um you know, that there's a lot of memories, there's a lot of people that came alongside me that helped get me to where I am today. So, um it's definitely something that's not lost on me, a very very special thing. >> Yeah, so with that said, you said you're happy with the sale today. What does it mean that somebody wants to spend $9 billion on the culture that was built by this team? >> Yeah, that was super cool. And um yeah, I'm I'm excited about that. There's plenty of stuff on there that you I'm sure don't see that for sure you don't see on you know, Hard Knocks, but like there's there's it's a great space for conversation just for guys in every room around the team to be able to kind of have a say in how guys are feeling, where guys are at, you know, what the what they see if there's a need that needs to be met or something we can do better. I mean I think I probably ask more questions than he's asking me questions. I mean I've certainly asked him more than he's asking me, but it's just great. I mean he's got a open door policy. At least I think he does. I don't want to put him on the spot, but you know, pretty I mean guys go in there they have got something to say. You know what I mean? Mike's a Mike's great about you know, giving you his time. >> When you have a chance to speak with the Kohoku family, what is it that you want to tell them about what it feels to be a Seahawk? [clears throat] >> Um What do I want to tell them? Oh, I don't know. I mean I I think I mean I'm sure they've done their due diligence, you know, on what we're about and what it's like in this building. and you know, I think there's there's a reason why um they want to be a part of it and want want to and see the value in it. And so I hope I hopefully I didn't have to say anything. They would just know that there's something special here in terms of how we go about our business and you know, actions speak louder than words in that way. >> Back to Bobo, what do you think your receiver core will miss with him out? >> Yeah, you know a lot. I mean just the I mean first and foremost just the person that he is. you know, it's like that I think is the thing that is overlooked upon all of this stuff, right? It's like, you know, we're we're a a group of men that come together every day to pursue a goal and have our own lives that all, you know, coalesce into this story that makes this season come alive. And so not having him be a part of that story um moving forward for this year is is tough. It's really hard. And you know, I know he's going to get after things in terms of the rehab and all of that stuff. Um but just not just not having Bubba the person um around us is uh is going to be tough. >> You've talked >> guys? >> Okay. You've talked in the past about kind of with the the cerebral side of the game, all of a sudden that coming out of necessity. You've said you know, you weren't the biggest guy, the fastest guy. But other than that like that you had to do it, how much do you enjoy that side of like finding those edges as Mike would say and like helping Mike unlock something on tape? Is that fun for you to see that side of >> Oh, without a doubt it is. I mean I think that's the I think that's one of the coolest parts about this game is finding ways to and really I think it's just finding ways for the team to have an edge, right? Finding something that comes alive in in a game. And it's it's not I mean it's it's almost better I would almost say it's better when it's not even you that's the one bringing it alive, but when you find a way for someone else to have success and bring something bring that edge and and and be and find success and find a way to to beat a team based on things that, you know, we collectively work together to solve. Like that is that is my favorite thing in the world. And so um yeah, that's like that's what you come in and watch the film for. That's what we communicate for. That's what makes, you know, a team that wants to collaborate together so much fun. I mean in all all honesty, cuz that wouldn't be that wouldn't be much fun for me. But um being able to collaborate, being able to figure it out together and work together, um having guys having guys in our room, players that are open to asking questions and also giving suggestions, like that that is what makes this uh this game so much fun. >> All right. Thanks. Thanks, awesome. Thank you. Appreciate it.

title: Khosla Family Press Conference | Seattle Seahawks
text: Right. Uh I'm thrilled to announce uh that the clubs have unanimously approved the transfer of the Seattle Seahawks and from the Paul Allen estate uh to the Cosa family ownership group represented right here. So, congratulations to all of you. Um before we get to the celebration there, I just want to thank uh Jody, uh the entire Allen family, and of course uh the Seahawks for uh their stewardship of the team um since Paul's death and and even uh since he took over ownership uh they have done a amazing job over the 30 years. Um and I know that the Cosa family uh respects that, appreciates that, and uh will do their best to to beat that standard. they know our league well. Um as you know, they uh have been ownership uh in the NFC West through the San Francisco 49ers. They understand um the passion of the NFL. They understand the 12s. They understand the Seattle community uh and the NFL. And so, uh that makes this transaction uh particularly attractive to all of us. they also uh have demonstrated throughout this a tremendous passion in football, um but also uh communities and how important the communities are to our success uh and their desire to make a difference in Seattle. Um but then also, I would say their experience um uh in technology uh and innovation and uh as we uh address many of those issues, uh I think their expertise uh will be incredibly valuable to us in helping us make better decisions moving forward. Uh and I know, most importantly, uh with tremendous confidence um that they will be outstanding caretakers of the Seattle Seahawks uh and the organization uh and the great partnership they have with their community. Um I also have to say you have great timing. It's not very often you can buy a Super Bowl uh championship team, um but you've done that. Uh many of our owners struggle to find ways to get into Super Bowl and and win a trophy, and you'll be walking into your new building shortly with a a fresh shiny trophy there for you. Um so to your family, thank you. Uh we appreciate all that you've done uh through this process, but more importantly what you'll do going So I think we're >> any photos with you in front of the podium? Can we have [clears throat] you in the middle? Okay. Nice and tight. There we go. Okay, let's continue. >> Well, thank you everybody. It's a great honor to be here. I do want to start by thanking Jody Allen and the Allen Trust for trusting us with this franchise. Roger's been incredibly helpful and the NFL staff incredibly helpful in getting here. as as Roger said, it's pretty simple when the team is one functioning as well as it is today. How often do you get to buy a franchise that just won the Super Bowl? Uh so we are incredibly lucky and humbled by this uh gift, I would say, from the Allen Trust. And of course, uh having been to Lumen Field and watching the 12s everywhere, I do want to thank them for their passion and fervor. And the community in Seattle is incredibly valuable. So, we hope we'll engage a lot more with the community also. the the task ahead is actually pretty simple. Keep the winning streak alive, get another Super Bowl. That's simple. In general, our approach was is generally going to be long-term focused. That's our inclination always. Um so, keep winning, take a long-term approach, and learn a lot. We don't know enough, and so hopefully the other owners have been incredibly welcoming and willing to teach us, and so we'll learn a lot. We learn a lot from management and see what they are recommending. So, we'll just be in learning mode for quite some time. I'll be happy to take questions. >> We do have our microphones, and why don't we begin here with Bob from the Seattle Times? >> Hi, yeah, Bob Condotta with the Seattle Times. Just curious how you came to be interested in wanting to buy the Seahawks. We obviously know you had a stake in the 49ers, and I know you Sounds like you guys were fans of the 49ers for a long time. Just kind of how did you then pivot to wanting to buy the Seahawks? >> Well, we are huge fans of football. And these opportunities, especially Super Bowl winning teams, seldom come along. So, we were very excited to have the opportunity and I've been tied to the Seattle tech community for a long time. And so, it was pretty easy to make the jump. >> To add to that, if I might, sorry. If I might add to that, see that guy on my left? Not this one, that one. >> [laughter] >> He's been a big fan of sports, and in particular football. So, he's wanted forever to get involved in in actually strategizing and kind of doing something about that. So, he's the one who actually really pushed us into doing this. He's worked really hard, so I'm very proud of him. >> Now, we've been very passionate about football for a long time. I would say we've been going to home games at the 49ers since we were 5, maybe half of all home games since he was 5. And so, football is definitely a passion. I also happened to come to this country in '76 when the Steelers were winning the Super Bowl. So, actually I was originally and still am a big Steelers fan. Also. A little-known fact, but I still watch all the Steelers games, too. >> Okay, let's do a couple more questions. To Chris from Seattle. >> Hi, Chris Daniels with KOMO TV in Seattle. Congratulations. On a day like today, with a lot of people watching back in Seattle, what do you want to say to the 12s and the Seahawks fans about being the new owner of the Seattle >> I I just want to say a big thank you for being such a passionate fan base. It's actually pretty incredible. I think it's the best fan base in the country of any NFL team. And the 12s is such a iconic brand that uh it's it's hard to not be honored to and humbled by inheriting that and being part of that fan base. >> Let's go to our last question to Randall Rance, KOMO. >> Um congratulations. There's been conversations about uh Lumen Field in particular and potential renovations or building a new stadium altogether. Um the offense, I feel like we've we have a good idea of, you know, how we want to operate and so does Flurry and I feel like he kind of came in and um we've been able to kind of just feed off that our energy from last year. Um the offense is pretty similar. You know, there's some some nuances, but um I feel like we've, you know, just came in and had the right mindset and, you know, continue to grow with, you know, all of us together with within the offense and um yeah, it's been good so far. >> And what are you learning about either as a coach or a person? Uh yeah, like I just said, he he wants to move the ball down the field. He's he's aggressive. He wants um to run the ball. He wants us to be physical in in all aspects of the game and uh with that mentality, you know, we just have to go out there and do it. Um I feel like we've done that up to this point and we just got to continue to grow along with him. >> I know you didn't play on Sunday, but one of the things Mike McDonald wanted the team to work on was mechanics and in and out of the huddle and just some of those things. What did you see in terms of improvements there or where there's still room for improvement? Yeah. Uh, always room for improvement, but I feel like we grew a lot over the last week. Um, from the first preseason game to the second, um, I feel like we honed in on those details throughout the week and, uh, we were able to go out there and execute them. The young guys, they did a great job. Um, it just put a lot of good on, uh, film, uh, out there, and, um, yeah, I'm looking forward to the third game. >> What does this team lose without Jake? I mean, fans will look and see two catches last year. Obviously, the NFC championship game was a big one, but like his impact seems to go quite a bit beyond that. like what's his loss going to be like for you guys in that room? >> Yeah, know it's a huge loss. He's he's a heartbeat of the offense. Um know we look to him for a lot of big plays and um you know he's been that you know since he's been a part of this organization and um losing him it definitely hurts. Um just at this point we're just trying to keep his head high. Um it's a tough situation but we know he's going to bounce back from it. >> As a wide receiver room how do you guys feel about your depth because obviously you jack Cooper you guys are pretty established in the league. How do you feel about the depth feel on the three of you guys especially with Jake going down with injury? Yeah. Uh, unfortunately with Jake going out, it definitely puts a little dent in it, but um, we have guys that are going to step up. Um, I love our depth. Um, we have a lot of guys that can make a lot of plays, tons of talent, and, uh, you know, we're all looking forward to all the opportunities we're going to get throughout the season. And, um, yeah, we're a locked in group and, uh, we kind of feed, the offense kind of feeds off of our energy, and, you know, that's exactly how we want it. >> When you put in Monty Foster, >> uh, everything, uh, his mindset, how he attacks every day. Um he worked super super hard and I'm just glad that it's finally coming uh out and for every for everybody to see. Um but yeah, no I I try to stay in his ear, try to keep him locked in, you know. Um he understands what it takes and uh I just got to continue to remind him that, you know, he's he's here and he has opportunity to do something special. >> What impression did you get from him last year when he comes in and joins you guys in December on the practice squad? Kind of runs out the string with you, but what what did you kind of get a sense from them and seeing how he's kind of taking advantage of the opportunity now? >> Yeah. Um he came in with the same mindset. You know, obviously it was later later on in the season. Um but you saw him make those type of plays at practices. Um you knew that you saw his potential and um now he had a long off seasonason and you know with us and he was able to you know just keep his head down and work and like I said the work is showing and um he just has to continue to make plays and I think he's going to continue to do so. >> Rasheed, when you were in New Orleans you had Alvin in the back field, one of the top passcatching backs in the league. How does having a running back room that's heavily involved in the passing game open things up for you guys on the outside? Seems like that's been an emphasis with Brian Flurry this offense. >> Yeah, for sure. Um it opens up everything. You know, you always have um something else to key on. You know, with us going vertical, you have a running back that could, you know, you could um dink and dunk to down the field and know as long as the coverage is is um you know, back, he could kind of work and um you know, just kind of do that for the offense. and uh I think it's going to be a big part of, you know, what he wants to do and how we're going to move the ball down the field. >> You had the long catch uh from Sam in the championship game, but there's a few other deep ones that just you guys were like a hair off. >> Is that the kind of thing that gets easier when you have more time with the quarterback? >> Yeah, 100%. I feel like we've worked on it a ton throughout this offseason, OTAAS, and now through camp. And we're starting to hit on them more. I'm starting to practice them a lot more and uh let things like that just take time. and you know those little um uh this game a game of inches like we always hear and um now we're starting to kind of click and uh it's been good. >> Thank you.

title: Jalen Hurts on End of Training Camp
text: How we doing? Well. >> Saw Marquise Goodwin get back out there and what's it been like building chemistry with him on the field? >> He continues to stack. He's hungry, eager, excited. I feel like he's learned a lot just in this short time being in the league and really he's been very direct and forward about trying to take care of his body and all the things that he can be better in and that so happy to have him back out there on the grass. He's a great player. >> How do you think you performed in this camp from your personal perspective? >> I feel like it was a good camp. Just taking in the coaching, taking in the the time and the growth that comes with a camp. I feel like Shawn has been great. Great to ask questions and um really great great camp to learn from. So >> John, what do you learn from interceptions in practice? >> Say that again. >> you learn from interceptions in practice? >> I think generally speaking you learn from every play. Um like regardless of how the result is, especially [clears throat] when you're putting in something new. And so I think every time we come out here and we get a chance to get on the grass, you want to take the coaching, go apply it, be aggressive in it and then with your experiences you reflect on them, think about them and you say, "Okay, you can play the game in this type of way, you can play the game in that type of way." And so I think I used the term calibrating with you guys. You know, all of that that whole entire process builds kind of your mind on how you're calculated, you know, when when you play the game and so it's it's been a really good camp. I'm happy about the experiences that we've had to be able to grow from them. Um I was very excited about the opportunity to be able to practice with um you know, the guys, our our receiving core when you know, the the guys that are going to start and we're we're we're we're banged up. And so just to have the time to build chemistry, build experiences with everyone as a unit. I feel like that was very valuable. >> How much of the offense do you guys do you think the team has down to this point? How's the installation process been going 2 and 1/2 weeks ahead of the first game? >> Yeah, you know, it's it's going. It's it's been you know, a lot of new information, a lot of new things and nothing very specific on kind of uh one direction of what we can be. Um it's a multi-faceted offense and approach and you know, when you get to game planning, I'm sure they'll even get more fine and fine and very direct to what we want to do that week. >> With all the multi-faceted offense that is, where do you think your command goes to overall >> Yeah, I feel like I'm in a good spot. Feel like I'm in a good spot. Think it's all about really looking at the experiences The experiences don't mean anything until you reflect on them and you grow from them and you start to apply them and so we're very widespread in what we're doing right now and I think that's good. So when we can hone it down and kind of see who we are, you know, establish what exactly the identity is for us and we you know, it's it'll it'll kind of come together. So still very early. >> You used the term multi-faceted. I guess you know, the changes that Shawn brings versus what you guys have done previously that you weren't successful in. I guess the big question is how much do we keep, how much do we not keep, but in this offense with Shawn so much predicated on under center and that kind of stuff, does it allow a lot for that to happen um in terms of keeping a lot from the previous offense? >> Yeah, I think that's a a great question it's something that you keep in mind of when you've had so much success. So you know, well how will it look? You don't really know. Do you want to win? Absolutely. And so we got to figure out who we are as a team. Obviously, coaches come in with a great mindset, great philosophy and putting everything together. Brings us a bit more structure. In the end, it's um it's about what going to what's going to go out there and be the best for our team. And so um I know Shan will come up with an answer to that over time. >> How long have you been around him now for 5 or 6 months? Where do you think he's grown the most? How's that process going? >> Yeah, want to honor that question cuz it's still really early. Uh still really early. So when we get into the season, you know, we'll begin to find out a lot about ourselves. Um to this point, it's just been a lot of teaching. Um a lot of teaching, a lot of opportunities to get on the grass and teaching off of that. And so once we put plans together build identity going one direction, um you know, you can see it a little clearly then. >> Do you agree or what kind of correlation have you found between camp performance and in-season performance both for you and for the team? >> Um I haven't I haven't thought about it much. Um I think as time has gone on, I've just looked at each year as its own. Um I've got a a diligence that I have about just approaching change and new new coaching and new perspective, new voice. And I think that's where it all starts. Um Performance is definitely important, but the relationship that you have and the conversations that you can have in the process is is really where it all starts. And so I've been in sponge mode this whole entire time taking in the perspective that coach has, um his eye for the game. And just going out there and trying to apply that. And so, when you get into the game, what's the goal? You know, the goal is to win. So, that that always trumps. >> With this being the final day of camp, and you look back to late July to this point now, what's been the biggest improvement for the offense in your eyes? >> Say that again? you think back to the last several weeks, late July, now we're in August, what's been the biggest improvement throughout that time in your offense? >> I think just been able to build chemistry, as a team. Feel like we've been able to come together, been able to compete, and have some fun moments together. So, that's what I value from this camp. >> We haven't seen VR very much to Eli Stove or Flowers. We haven't seen much of him in camp. >> Yeah, he had he had No, he's been healthy. Hasn't been healthy with these last >> Yeah, these last couple of weeks. >> Yeah. >> Previously worked with the ones and twos and the threes. I'm just wondering, knowing how much important chemistry is with you and Yeah. No, he hasn't been up with that unit a lot this camp, but he's he's got a lot of talent. You know, he's got a lot of talent. We spent some time in the summertime, so not not foreign from it. but I think you know, once you kind of know where you are, know your role, I think that's something that can be a quick fix. >> Do you see the offense as something that's going to continue to evolve into the season? And I'm assuming that's probably no different than past years, but is there kind of a difference like with you know, how this offense evolves going forward compared to the others? I mean, I just think about the foundation of what you are, foundation of what is introduced to be. And so, from a you know, intent and the North Star uh structure standpoint, the foundation of it. I think it's I think it's been clear and we've been driving that and um as you see who you have on your team and you begin to progress forward, you hone things down and you say this is who we are, this is you know, how I want to lead it. So, I think that's where Jalen is. Um and you know, a lot of that is is up for him to mold and put together. So, uh with the in the end we can go out there and be in the best position to win. >> Jalen, there's obviously a backup quarterback competition. As a As a starter, what do you want in a backup? What's important to you as a starter? >> Well, I think all three guys have been very valuable to the room. Um they've got a lot of wisdom, a lot of talent. Um and I value the perspective. So, >> I got to ask you guys about Jalen a little bit. Um the wide receiver group as a whole, now that you've gotten this time, gotten extra reps with some of the new guys, what do you what do you think of the group as a whole? >> Yeah, I'm excited excited for the group. Um you know, I think just the time that we've been able to put together uh put in together over the summer, um the reps that we've had, the conversations that we've been able to have about how we can grow. Um and I think anytime you're playing with a new unit, it's just about being on the same page. and that's no different than that's no different than than coaching, too. Um when you've got a new play caller, you've got new voice, you've got new perspective. Um everybody's chasing the same thing. Everybody wants the same outcome. Everybody process looks a little different. So, being able to get that being able to navigate how does our process look? How does this look for this unit, this team and sounds like a broken record a bit from you know, what I've said in the past, but you know, what is this team? What is it this iteration of the Eagles going to look like? And so, I think the think think this camp has given us an opportunity to come closer to that. And we've still got uh time before we we tee it off and it's, you know, live ball. But, we we just want to continue to progress every day, uh keep the uh communication open, being on the same page, being aligned, and going out there and doing it together as a team. >> Hey, thanks, y'all. Thanks everybody for coming in today.

title: Cam Jurgens & More on What They've Learned From Training Camp
text: Omar, maybe maybe my uh untrained eye. It looks like you're moving around pretty well out there. How's your back feel? >> It's feeling better. You know, I feel like it's just trying to be consistent with everything and my process, my rehab, and getting ready for practice every day and just try to work those little things. So then, you know, little by little it's going to get better. And I feel like every week it's been making improvements. I'm I'm really happy with where I'm at. And heading into the season, I feel like I'm in a lot better spot than I was last year. >> Throughout the throughout camp that you were like >> nervous about how your body would react to things and were you pleasantly surprised by the way it did at times? >> Yeah, I I mean I'd say so. I mean there's always like good and bad days with that, especially I mean even today. I mean, I feel like 3 days ago we had like a long drive day and then we go into a long scrimmage last night where I feel like felt like a game and then today we got another practice just like back to back to back. You never know how your body's going to like recover, but like we're all dealing with that, you know? It's it's not like that during the season. You know, you get into a normal structure, but I'm I'm just I'm happy with how it's responding. with how long you missed a a practice or even a rep through this whole training camp. Correct me if I'm wrong, but I think you were out there for everything. >> Yeah, I think the heat may have got me a couple days. You know what I'm saying? It happens. It happens. It got me a few times at the start, you know. >> But as far as I mean, as far as being healthy, how important is it to kind of always be out there? It's great, especially with a new offense, getting those reps in, communicating with the guys, and you know, no matter who's next to me, who's a tackle or guard, it's good talking to everybody and talking through that terminology and, you know, being able to be out there to make the mistakes to go in and uh work on it. >> You went along with Jayl. You still do that training camp? No, I mean we meet at nauseium during training camp. So it'd be hard pressed to find more time to meet. Uh but yeah, when the season starts and we get that normal regular schedule, it'll be changing. But like I mean even this week we have like a three days ago was like a weird time for practice and then we had like the night stadium practice. Now we're at two. like it's hard to get that normal schedule right now. And I think everybody's excited to get into the season and have that structured, you know, I feel like as a football player and athlete, it's nice having that structure. I mean, you guys probably understand that, too. It's It's weird when things always change up on you. >> What's it been like? What's it been like with the pre- snap stuff, like sorting out pressure looks and I guess just like the communication aspect. How's it been iron that ironing that out so far? >> Uh, it's been good. You know, I feel like we've been going out there and you know, when you make a mistake, it's at the same time it's frustrating, but it's also good because you're you're you're talking through things. You know, like last night, we saw some things that we weren't expecting or haven't seen yet. And it's just good to get those reps and, you know, maybe mess a couple things up to figure out, hey, why didn't that go well? How could we iron up that communication and and figure something out? So, you know, we're making a certain call, it it hits our brains all the same way and we get on the same page and, you know, it just comes with reps. You know, when you're coming with a new offense, you mean you just want to make sure you keep building throughout the season. Um, and I feel like we are building, but you know, I think this is going to be something that's going to keep rising throughout the year. >> Like almost exclusively at center in college and then played guard here for the one year. How do you think uh Drew has handled coming in and you know kind of cross trainining at multiple spots? >> He's done great. I mean he's just very smart, intellectual. I mean his dad played for 12 years and so just he goes about it the right way, you know, whether it's, you know, going in for weight room or doing the meetings or just taking care of his body and off time like he just goes about, you know, football the right way and he he's a pro. >> Yeah, definitely. you know, he's he's lean on me and it's always good having an extra set of eyes and figuring out, you know, if something's right or wrong and um he's been great, you know, flipping back and forth between guard and center. And we got a lot of confidence in him. You I mean, that's just kind of how it has to be. You know, he's got to have a swing guy for tackle. You got to have a guy that can play all three inside because never know how many you're going to have active for a game day. Tam uh Sean Tam Sean has talked a lot about marrying the run with the pass. From like a centers perspective, what are like some of the little things that you have to really hone in on to make sure that like everything looks the same so you can build a lot of different plays off like the same level. >> Uh you know, I think part of the the way you attack the line of scrimmage, you know, if you're running naked, uh there's certain ways to do it. I mean, when like a quarterback boot out and you can attack that the line of scrimmage like you're running an outside zone and stretch and and so you're kind of you're treating it like you're running an outside zone and you're seeing how that D lineman's going to react. So when you do run outside zone, you know how it's going to react and and you're kind of playing those like mental games like all game figuring out, you know, attacking him this way and then running naked and just figuring out how they're going to react and are the two gappers or the jeters and how you need your hand placement and and so just making things look the same and you coming up to the line of scrimmage making calls or points making everything look and feel the same until it's not. And I think uh even just going under center, it just it helps you do so many things that look the same. >> Can you talk about the chemistry that Chris Cooper had back in the OTAAS to what it is now with with the young line room? >> Yeah, I think uh I think it just keeps growing just understanding him and how he coaches and how he approaches things and how he likes to work and just going through and doing the individual drills. you know, maybe there's a day like today where, you know, we are feeling it. We're exhausted. You know, how does he change things up? How does he, you know, keep our legs light? And just figuring him out. I mean, it's been nice. And just uh figuring out, you know, how he ticks and how we tick and, you know, he's he's been doing a great job of figuring out how to coach certain guys and and adjust and make sure everybody's uh learning properly. You know, certain guys learn different ways. >> Sean at the um Go ahead. Let's get back into the schedule and the rhythm here and getting a chance to meet with Jaylen. Like how do you what the last couple of years have you both learned about that process together? It is a pretty new offense. Um, and so that's all I'm I'm really focused on right now. Um and show up to work every day and you know, kind of not really understanding or knowing like maybe what the what the whole grind and the process is, but embracing it um and taking full advant advantage of of it. Um you know, I knew where the the coverage mismatches were, so I was kind of, you know, showing some presence over there and then just, you know, followed the quarterback's eyes, broke on the ball. title: Vic Fangio on the Defense's Growth as Training Camp Concludes
text: You guys got a treat today. Coach Vermeil will be here. >> Oh, nice. >> I've been up there visiting with him. >> It's wine? >> What's that? >> Always. >> Coach, at at this point, is your mind made up with the roster or is there still something anybody can do leading into this last game? >> Yeah, they can, you know. It doesn't matter if my mind's made up or not. It's how we and Nick's mind's got to be made up. >> Big Talk about this something the like Why do you think that is? >> You know, everybody's a little different. Um but you see it every year that some guys they're struggling, struggling, struggling and just something happens that that they're able to turn the corner a little bit. And just so happened that it was him in the first preseason game and he carried it over to last week and hopefully this will continue. Now, he's got to be able to uh you know, do it against the front line players, too. >> This battle at safety with Ebner and Carter, any closer to uh >> No, it's close. Um it is close. I you know, Michael has been doing a good job back there. It's just all new to him. And uh we need to get him more exposure, which is hard to do. But I do think Michael eventually can do it. >> Now that we're at the end of camp >> Now that we're at the end of camp, how would you assess Reed's summer? >> Overall good. You know, he's had his moments where he can get a little sloppy. Um we need to eliminate those and hopefully once the regular season starts, that will happen, but we like him. I like him a lot. I like the player. I like the person. I like I like being around him and I like coaching him. >> How do you feel about Maximus and Josh and where they fit? >> Who? >> Uh >> Max and Yeah, good. You know, I think those guys you know, going back, you know, to your question there they're still alive, you know, in this game will mean something to them. >> Uh what's your thought on Reed? Uh we all know about his you know, explosibility. How's he adapted to playing more zone and specifically, you know, your match zone? >> Yeah, he's done I think he's done well. You know, you have our offense in particular, too. You going to you have to play off a little bit more. you know, cuz they'll stack and bunch people and so it's been a good camp for him in that way. But he's getting better at it for sure. >> Yeah, the safety situation, the safety is that something that might could go right up until game day? Like, you know, before you go >> Go up until when? >> Game day before you decide who's >> Game day of the first day? >> Yeah. >> No, we'll decide before then. >> At the time you guys drafted Jaylen, a message was what does this look like in year three? Now that you're in year three, is this what you expected? Is it beyond what you expected? How would you explain it? >> It's what I expected and hoped for, but now I, you know, hope for and expect for more, too. >> And what's that look like? What's what's the next >> I don't know. That you stop asking, not you, but all you. am I surprised? Is this unexpected? You know, where it's that's who he is. >> You mentioned Reed's tendency to get maybe a little sloppy. How do you fix something like that? >> Just keeping um pointing it out and he knows it. You know, it's not like he denies it. Um it's just some guys sometimes could happen to some guys and we just got to try and eliminate that. >> While there's still today's practice to go, what's been your overall takeaway of the defense during this camp? >> Um you >> know, it's it's been a good camp. Um you know, we're we're never I think a lot of guys need some more developing. Um some more reps, but that's just the way it is and and then whatever it is, 2 weeks from now we got a game or 3 weeks, whatever it is. >> How do you feel about the quarterback throwing a lot of interceptions over the last few weeks, pretty much all camp? Like as the defensive coordinator on the same team with a that quarterback, like how do you how do you view that? How do you >> How do I view what? >> When the when the quarterback that plays on your team throws a lot of interceptions, then your defense is responsible for them. >> Well, it's good for the defense, which is good for the team. You know, and I he's learning a new offense. I think he's trying things. Um seeing what's available and what isn't available. So, I don't think that's going to carry over. >> How do you feel about the cornerback depth right now? >> Cornerback? you know, I feel good about uh Q and Rique. Um you know, John Jones has missed a lot of time here. So, hopefully we can get him back at some point. I think Mack has made a lot of strides. He got he's dinged right now a little bit, then wasn't able to finish the other night. Keely, I think is making strides. you know, those are the five main ones and plus the guys that are competing for the sixth spot. >> Hey, I'm pretty satisfied here for a while now. What's your assessment of his third training camp? >> It's been good, you know, he's he knows he knows our defense from the safety's position. He's reliable in that regard. Uh he's trustworthy. And um you know, I think he's a guy that's you will have a spot, you know, somewhere along the line, but we like him. >> Seems like Ty Robinson continues to come on. Is he Is he earned a spot in your defensive tackle rotation? >> Yeah, he probably has. I mean, you know, when you say rotation, I don't know what that means meaning meaning how many plays that means, but >> on game >> Yeah. Yeah. >> Jordan left a little early last night from practice. Is Are you >> Yeah, but he came back. He came back. Yeah. >> When it comes to these last couple of weeks, when it comes to these last few roster spots, um obviously, I'm sure your voice is taken into account, but historically, how what have you found that you value in these last few guys that are on the defensive side and these I mean, how much does special teams factor in the kind of decision that you get to make on the defensive players? >> Yeah, I mean, the special teams does play a factor. You know, it The last few spots are always um a story in and of itself. You know, it might be a guy that's not ready to play and you might not think he's ready to play the entire year, but you want him. Sometimes that happens. Sometimes it's uh a guy that you think can help us in a pinch, you know, if we had need it. as I said, special teams is a big thing. Just numbers, too. You There's minimal numbers you need at every position. You know, you need five or six defensive linemen to make the roster. You need eight to nine outside backers and inside backers to make the roster minimum. You know, so the numbers is part of it also. >> It's our first time talking When it comes to you I just want to follow up on the When it comes to you like I don't know personally, but obviously further along your years, you want to win now. I mean, like how do you accept if they're going to tell you two guys are going to be on the 53, but they're not going to play the entire game. >> Yeah, that's just part of it. Um you know, yeah, we all want to win now. but it's Howie's job to always be building the team for future years, too. >> Is this our first time talking to you since before that joint practice? What stood out watching them against the Patriots' offense this week? >> Yeah, I thought those two practices against the Patriots were um our two most beneficial and valuable practices the entire year, entire camp. just like I said before, you know, it's a different style offense, so that was great in and of itself. they have a good group of receivers. That was good to go against. Way different offensive scheme than ours, great to go against. yeah, tho- those were two really, really good practices. You know, we had I think like 80-some plays the first day, 50-some, 60 maybe the second day with a red zone focus. Fantastic practices. >> Thanks for the questions.

text: Yeah, that was a sun, no wind. >> Yeah. New shape. >> Yeah. Do you still do that training camp? >> No, I mean, we meet ad nauseam during training camp, so it'd be hard-pressed to find more time to meet. Now we're at 2. Like, it's hard to get that normal schedule right now, and I think everybody's excited to get into the season and have that structured You know, I feel like as a football player, an athlete, it's nice having that structure. I mean, you guys probably understand that, too. It's It's weird when things always change up on you. >> What's it been like What's it been like with the pre-snap stuff, like sorting out pressure looks, and I guess just like the communication aspect? How's it been ironing that ironing that out so far? >> Uh it's been good. Um and I feel like we are building. I mean, his dad played for 12 years. Like, he just goes about, you know, football the right way and he he's a pro. Yeah, definitely.
